  \;=\;
  \delta_{\lambda\mu}\; \|T_{\lambda}\|^2,$$*

*where the norm-squared $\|T_{\lambda}\|^2$ is a positive rational number computable from the hook lengths of the tableau $\lambda$.*

*This orthogonality has two consequences for the QOU framework:*

1.  ***Decomposition of hadron states.** A [categorical hadron](#def:hadron) of valence $n$ can be uniquely expanded in the PawLei basis, with coefficients that are physically interpretable as partial-wave amplitudes.*

2.  ***Compatibility with the Frobenius form.** The inner product $\langle{-},{-}\rangle_{\mathrm{PL}}$ agrees with the restriction of the [Frobenius pairing](#def:frobenius-pairing) to $\mathrm{End}(V_j) \subset A$, ensuring that integration over the fibre and decomposition into basis elements commute.*

*The algebraic foundations (PBW bases over commutative rings) are established in \\}cite{leitnerpawloski2004}; norm formulas follow from the Temperley–Lieb calculus and $6j$-symbols.*

</div>

## Differential structures and gauge actions

<div id="prop:spin-labels" class="proposition">

**Proposition 2.19** (Spin labels and the fundamental object). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.SpinDecomposition)*

*Let $(\mathbf{C}, A, \tau)$ be a ([quantum observable universe](#def:quantum-observable-universe)). Because $G = \mathrm{Aut}^{\otimes}(\tau) \cong \mathrm{SU}(2)$ ([SU(2) emergence](#thm:su2-emergence)), the simple objects of $\mathbf{C}$ are indexed by a *spin* label $j \in \{0, \tfrac12, 1, \tfrac32, \ldots\}$, with $V_j$ denoting the simple object of categorical dimension $2j + 1$. The *fundamental object* is $V = V_{1/2}$, the unique simple object of categorical dimension $2$. The *adjoint object* is $V_1 \cong \mathrm{Ad}(A)$, of dimension $3$.*

*$$\label{eq:spin-labels-diagram}
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=2em]
  V_0 = \mathbf{1} & V_{1/2} = V & V_1 = \mathrm{Ad}(A) & V_{3/2} & \cdots
\end{tikzcd}
\qquad (\dim V_j = 2j+1)$$*

</div>

<div class="proof">

*Proof of spin labels.* <span id="prf:spin-labels" label="prf:spin-labels"></span>

Because $G = \mathrm{Aut}^{\otimes}(\tau) \cong \mathrm{SU}(2)$ ([SU(2) emergence](#thm:su2-emergence)), the simple objects of $\mathbf{C}$ are indexed by a spin label $j \in \{0, \tfrac12, 1, \tfrac32, \ldots\}$, with $V_j$ denoting the simple object of categorical dimension $2j + 1$.

The symplectic form $\epsilon \colon \Lambda^2 V \to \mathbf{1}$ ([quantum observable universe](#def:quantum-observable-universe), axiom (iii)) is the unique (up to scalar) $G$-invariant alternating pairing on $V$. ◻

</div>

<div id="ex:spin-labels-su2" class="example">

**Example 2.20** (Spin decomposition of $\mathrm{Rep}(\mathrm{SU}(2))$). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.Examples.su2SpinLabels)*

*Continuing [QOU on SU(2)](#ex:qou-su2), the simple objects of $\mathbf{C} = \mathrm{Rep}(\mathrm{SU}(2))$ are the irreducible representations $V_j \cong \mathbb{C}^{2j+1}$:*

*$$\label{eq:spin-decomposition}
\begin{tikzcd}[row sep=1.5em, column sep=1.5em]
  V_0 \ar[d, phantom, "\cong"] & V_{1/2} \ar[d, phantom, "\cong"]
    & V_1 \ar[d, phantom, "\cong"] & V_{3/2} \ar[d, phantom, "\cong"]
    & \cdots \\
  \mathbb{C} & \mathbb{C}^2 & \mathbb{C}^3 & \mathbb{C}^4 & \cdots
\end{tikzcd}$$*

*In concrete terms:*

- *$V_0 = \mathbb{C}$ (the trivial representation: $g \cdot z = z$).*

- *$V_{1/2} = \mathbb{C}^2$ (the defining representation: $g \cdot v = gv$ by matrix multiplication). This is the fundamental object $V$.*

- *$V_1 = \mathfrak{su}(2)_{\mathbb{C}} \cong \mathbb{C}^3$ (the adjoint representation: $g \cdot X = gXg^{-1}$). This is $\mathrm{Ad}(A)$.*

- *$V_{3/2} = \mathrm{Sym}^3(\mathbb{C}^2) \cong \mathbb{C}^4$ (homogeneous cubics in two variables).*

*Every finite-dimensional representation decomposes as $W \cong \bigoplus_j V_j^{\oplus m_j}$, with multiplicities $m_j \in \mathbb{N}$. The polynomial ring $\mathbb{C}[z] = \bigoplus_{n \geq 0} \mathrm{Sym}^n V$ is the coordinate ring of $\mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}) = \mathbb{P}(V)$ ([projective line object](#def:projective-line-object)), and each homogeneous component $\mathrm{Sym}^n V \cong V_{n/2}$ is an irreducible representation of dimension $n + 1$.*

</div>

<div id="def:categorical-reeb" class="definition">

**Definition 2.21** (Categorical Reeb derivation). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.CategoricalReeb)*

*Let $(\mathbf{C}, A, \tau)$ be a quantum observable universe with maximal torus $T$ ([maximal torus](#def:maximal-torus)) and weight decomposition $\pi_H, \pi_V$ ([weight decomposition](#def:weight-decomposition)). The *categorical Reeb derivation* is the endomorphism $\xi \colon A \to A$ that generates the $T$-action: $\xi$ is the infinitesimal generator of the one-parameter subgroup $T \cong \mathrm{U}(1) \subset G$, acting on the Frobenius–Hopf object $A$ via the adjoint coaction. It satisfies:*

1.  ***Vertical generator:** $\pi_V \circ d = \iota_\xi\, d\theta_A$, where $\iota_\xi$ denotes the interior product (contraction with $\xi$) and $\theta_A \in \Omega^1(A)$ is the canonical $1$-form dual to $\xi$.*

2.  ***Normalisation:** $\theta_A(\xi) = \mathrm{id}_{\mathbf{1}}$.*

3.  ***Kernel:** $\Omega^k_H(A) = \ker(\iota_\xi)$ (horizontal forms are precisely those annihilated by contraction with $\xi$).*

*$$\label{eq:reeb-decomposition-diagram}
\begin{tikzcd}[row sep=2.5em, column sep=3em]
  \Omega^k(A) \ar[r, "\pi_H"] \ar[d, "\pi_V"']
  & \Omega^k_H(A) \ar[d, hook] \\
  \theta_A \wedge \Omega^{k-1}_H(A) \ar[r, hook]
  & \Omega^k(A)
\end{tikzcd}
\qquad (\pi_H + \pi_V = \mathrm{id})$$*

</div>

<div id="thm:categorical-reeb-exists" class="theorem">

**Theorem 2.22** (Existence of the categorical Reeb derivation). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.CategoricalReeb.ofWeightDecomposition)*

*Let $(\mathbf{C}, A, \tau)$ be a ([quantum observable universe](#def:quantum-observable-universe)) with [maximal torus](#def:maximal-torus) $T$ and [weight decomposition](#def:weight-decomposition) $(\pi_H, \pi_V)$. Then there exists a [categorical Reeb derivation](#def:categorical-reeb) $(\xi, \theta_A)$ on $A$ satisfying:*

1.  ***Vertical generator:** $\pi_V \circ d = \iota_\xi\, d\theta_A$.*

2.  ***Normalisation:** $\xi \mathbin{;} \theta_A = \theta_A$ (categorically: $\theta_A(\xi) = \mathrm{id}_{\mathbf{1}}$).*

*$$\label{eq:reeb-exists-diagram}
\begin{tikzcd}[row sep=2.5em, column sep=3em]
  A \ar[r, "\xi"] \ar[d, "d"']
  & A \ar[d, "\theta_A"] \\
  \Omega^1(A) \ar[r, "\iota_\xi"']
  & A
\end{tikzcd}
\qquad (\theta_A(\xi) = \mathrm{id}_{\mathbf{1}})$$*

</div>

<div class="proof">

*Proof of existence of the categorical Reeb derivation.* <span id="prf:categorical-reeb-exists" label="prf:categorical-reeb-exists"></span>

The derivation $\xi$ is the infinitesimal generator of the one-parameter subgroup $T \cong \mathrm{U}(1) \subset G$, and $\theta_A$ is its Maurer–Cartan dual, uniquely determined by the normalisation condition. ◻

</div>

<div id="ex:reeb-su2" class="example">

**Example 2.23** (Reeb derivation for $\mathrm{SU}(2)$). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.Examples.su2Reeb)*

*Continuing [maximal torus of SU(2)](#ex:maximal-torus-su2), the maximal torus is $T = \mathrm{U}(1)$ with generator $\xi = e_3 = \frac{1}{2}\begin{smallmatrix} 1 & 0 \\ 0 & -1 \end{smallmatrix} \in \mathfrak{su}(2)$. On $A = \mathcal{O}(\mathrm{SU}(2))$, $\xi$ acts by $(\xi \cdot f)(g) = \frac{d}{dt}\big|_{t=0} f(e^{-t\xi} g)$ (left-invariant vector field). The canonical $1$-form is $\theta_A = \omega_3$ (the left-invariant $1$-form dual to $e_3$), and:*

- *$\omega_3(\xi) = 1$ (normalisation).*

- *$\Omega^k_H(A) = \{\alpha : \iota_\xi\,\alpha = 0\}$ (forms with no $\omega_3$ component).*

- *In the archimedean realisation on a CR manifold $(M, \theta)$, $\xi$ becomes the Reeb vector field with $\iota_\xi\,d\theta = 0$ and $\theta(\xi) = 1$ ([Reeb decomposition](#ex:reeb-decomposition)).*

</div>

<div id="def:projective-line-object" class="definition">

**Definition 2.24** (Projective line object). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.ProjectiveLineObject)*

*Let $(\mathbf{C}, A, \tau)$ be a quantum observable universe with maximal torus $T \subset G$ ([maximal torus](#def:maximal-torus)). The *projective line object* is the quotient*

*$$\mathbb{P}(V) = G / T,$$*

*regarded as an object of $\mathrm{Ind}(\mathbf{C})$ via its function algebra $\mathcal{O}(\mathbb{P}(V)) = A^{\mathrm{co}\,T}$ (the $T$-coinvariant subalgebra of $A$).*

*Under the fibre functor $\tau$, the categorical projective line realises as the scheme-theoretic projective line over $R$:*

*$$\tau\bigl(\mathbb{P}(V)\bigr) \;=\; \mathbb{P}^1(R)$$*

*([scheme notation](#rem:scheme-notation)). The notation $\mathbb{P}(V)$ is used when the categorical construction matters (built from the fundamental object $V$); the notation $\mathbb{P}^1(R)$ is used in scheme-theoretic or coordinate contexts ([contact affine chart](#def:contact-affine-chart)).*

</div>

<div id="ex:projective-line-su2" class="example">

**Example 2.25** (Projective line for $\mathrm{SU}(2)$). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.Examples.su2ProjectiveLine)*

*Continuing [maximal torus of SU(2)](#ex:maximal-torus-su2), $G = \mathrm{SU}(2)$ and $T = \mathrm{U}(1)$. The quotient is $\mathbb{P}(V) = \mathrm{SU}(2)/\mathrm{U}(1) \cong \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C})$. A point $[\ell] \in \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C})$ is a line $\ell \subset V = \mathbb{C}^2$; equivalently, it is the kernel of a linear form on $V$, well-defined up to scalar. The function algebra is the polynomial ring $\mathcal{O}(\mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C})) = \mathbb{C}[z]$ in the affine coordinate $z = v_1 / v_2$.*

</div>

<div id="def:contact-affine-chart" class="definition">

**Definition 2.26** (Contact affine chart on $\mathbb{P}(V)$). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.ContactAffineChart)*

*Let $\mathcal{S}$ be the state bundle over $M$ whose fibres are the spaces of $1$-forms, and let $\mathbb{P}(V)$ be the projective line object ([projective line object](#def:projective-line-object)). Using the Reeb decomposition ([Reeb decomposition](#ex:reeb-decomposition)), every form splits as $\alpha = \alpha_H + \theta \wedge \iota_\xi \alpha$.*

*The *contact affine chart* $U_\xi \subset \mathbb{P}(V)$ is the open dense subset of states with non-vanishing Reeb component:*

*$$U_\xi \;=\; \bigl\{\, [\alpha] \in \mathbb{P}(V)
  \;\big|\; \iota_\xi\,\alpha \neq 0 \,\bigr\}.$$*

*On $U_\xi$, the explicit *affine coordinate* is defined by the ratio of horizontal spatial diffusion to vertical quantum spin:*

*$$Z([\alpha]) \;=\; \frac{\alpha_H}{\iota_\xi\,\alpha}.$$*

*$$\label{eq:contact-affine-chart-diagram}
\begin{tikzcd}[row sep=2.5em, column sep=3em]
  U_\xi \ar[r, hook] \ar[d, "Z"']
  & \mathbb{P}(V) \ar[d, "\cong", "G/T"'] \\
  H = \ker\theta \ar[r, hook]
  & \Omega^1_H(A)
\end{tikzcd}$$*

*The coordinate $Z$ takes values in the horizontal distribution $H = \ker\theta$. The contact form $\theta$ and the Reeb vector field $\xi$ thus automatically provide the stereographic projection for the projective line fibres — no external coordinates are needed.*

</div>

<div id="prop:fibre-functor-atlas" class="proposition">

**Proposition 2.27** (Fibre functors as an affine atlas with $G$-torsor transitions).

***Proposition.** *Let $(\mathbf{C}, A, \tau)$ be a quantum observable universe with $G = \mathrm{Aut}^{\otimes}(\tau)$ ([Tannaka–Krein](#rem:tannaka-krein-overview)). In the following, $\omega, \omega'$ denote arbitrary fibre functors on $\mathbf{C}$ (not the canonical $\tau$). Then:**

1.  ***(Charts.)** *Each fibre functor $\omega \colon \mathbf{C} \to \mathbf{Vect}_R$ is an affine chart: a concrete realisation of the abstract categorical data as linear algebra over $R$. The contact affine chart on $\mathbb{P}(V)$ ([contact affine chart](#def:contact-affine-chart)) is the chart associated to the canonical fibre functor $\tau$.**

2.  ***(Transitions.)** *For any two fibre functors $\omega, \omega'$, the set of monoidal natural isomorphisms $\omega \xrightarrow{\sim} \omega'$ is a $G$-torsor. Each such isomorphism is a transition function: a change of affine coordinates relating the two observers’ descriptions of the same categorical data.**

3.  ***(Cocycle condition.)** *Given three fibre functors $\omega, \omega', \omega''$ with transition isomorphisms $g_{01}, g_{12}, g_{02}$, functoriality of composition forces $g_{02} = g_{12} \circ g_{01}$. The cocycle condition is not imposed — it is automatic.**

4.  ***(Atlas.)** *The category of all fibre functors on $\mathbf{C}$, with monoidal natural isomorphisms as morphisms, is a $G$-gerbe: a connected groupoid on which $G$ acts simply transitively. This is the **affine atlas** of the quantum observable universe.**

**Proof.* (1) A fibre functor $\omega$ assigns to each object $X$ in $\mathbf{C}$ a vector space $\omega(X)$ and to each morphism $f$ a linear map $\omega(f)$, preserving the tensor product. This is a concrete coordinate system for the abstract category — an affine chart.*

*(2) By the Tannaka–Krein theorem ([SU(2) emergence](#thm:su2-emergence)), any monoidal natural isomorphism $\eta \colon \omega \xrightarrow{\sim} \omega'$ is determined by an element $g \in G = \mathrm{Aut}^{\otimes}(\tau)$ acting on the fibre. The set of all such isomorphisms is a principal homogeneous space for $G$ — a $G$-torsor.*

*(3) If $\eta_{01} \colon \omega \to \omega'$ and $\eta_{12} \colon \omega' \to \omega''$ are monoidal natural isomorphisms, their composition $\eta_{12} \circ \eta_{01}$ is the unique monoidal natural isomorphism $\omega \to \omega''$ corresponding to the group product $g_{12} \cdot g_{01}$. The cocycle identity $g_{02} = g_{12} \cdot g_{01}$ is the associativity of composition in the functor category.*

*(4) Connectedness: any two fibre functors are isomorphic (Tannaka–Krein). Simple transitivity: the isomorphism is unique up to $G$. $\square$*

</div>

<div id="prop:substrate-radial-coordinate" class="proposition">

**Proposition 2.28** (Substrate parameter as the radial coordinate). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.substrate_radial_coordinate)*

*Within the contact affine chart $U_\xi$ ([contact affine chart](#def:contact-affine-chart)), the substrate parameter $q$ ([substrate parameter](#def:substrate-parameter)) governs the radial and phase coordinates of the state. Let $Z$ be the affine coordinate of a state. Then $Z \to 0$ as $q \to \infty$ (deep-quantum origin) and $Z \to \infty$ as $q \to 1$ (classical boundary). The $q$-deformed Reeb flow rotates the phase of $Z$:*

*$$\mathcal{L}_\xi\,Z \;=\; J\,\hbar_q\,Z,$$*

*where $\hbar_q = 1 - q^{-1}$ ([quantum Planck constant](#def:quantum-planck-constant)) and $J$ is the complex structure on $H$.*

</div>

<div class="proof">

*Proof of substrate radial coordinate.* <span id="prf:substrate-radial-coordinate" label="prf:substrate-radial-coordinate"></span>

Within the contact affine chart $U_\xi$ ([contact affine chart](#def:contact-affine-chart)), let $Z$ be the affine coordinate of a state.

1.  **Deep-quantum origin** ($Z \to 0$): as $q \to \infty$ (collapsing instanton), the state becomes purely vertical ($\alpha_H \to 0$). The affine coordinate vanishes, locating the primordial fermion at the origin of the chart.

2.  **Classical boundary** ($Z \to \infty$): as $q \to 1$ (classical vacuum), the state becomes purely horizontal ($\iota_\xi\,\alpha \to 0$, a boson). The affine coordinate diverges, pushing the state to the point at infinity of the $\mathbb{CP}^1$ fibre.

Furthermore, the $q$-deformed Reeb flow ([q-Reeb flow](#ex:q-reeb-flow)) rotates the phase of $Z$ at a rate proportional to the quantum Planck constant:

$$\mathcal{L}_\xi\,Z \;=\; J\,\hbar_q\,Z,$$

where $\hbar_q = 1 - q^{-1}$ ([quantum Planck constant](#def:quantum-planck-constant)) and $J$ is the complex structure on $H$.

This unifies bosons and fermions geometrically: $q$ controls the radial position in $\mathbb{P}(V)$, with the bosonic sector at the boundary and the fermionic sector at the origin. ◻

</div>

<div id="prop:fiber-adjoint-involution" class="proposition">

**Proposition 2.29** (Fiber–adjoint-fiber involution). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.FiberAdjointInvolution)*

*Let $(\mathbf{C}, A, \tau)$ be a ([quantum observable universe](#def:quantum-observable-universe)). The Frobenius form $\int_A \colon A \to \mathbf{1}$ induces an isomorphism $A \xrightarrow{\;\sim\;} A^{\vee}$ (the Frobenius self-duality), under which:*

1.  *the projective line object $\mathbb{P}(V)$ ([projective line object](#def:projective-line-object)) embeds in the adjoint object $\mathrm{Ad}(A)$ as the coadjoint orbit of a highest-weight vector;*

2.  *the assignment $\sigma \colon \mathbb{P}(V) \hookrightarrow \mathrm{Ad}(A)$ is an involution in the sense that $\sigma$ determines $\mathbb{P}(V)$ from $\mathrm{Ad}(A)$ and vice versa;*

3.  *the non-degeneracy of the [Frobenius pairing](#def:frobenius-pairing) forces the observability condition: $$\mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1},\, \mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0.$$*

*$$\label{eq:fiber-adjoint-involution-diagram}
\begin{tikzcd}[row sep=2.5em, column sep=3em]
  \mathbb{P}(V)
    \ar[r, hook, "\sigma"]
    \ar[d, "\cong"']
  & \mathrm{Ad}(A)
    \ar[d, "\cong", "\int_A"'] \\
  G/T
    \ar[r, hook, "\text{coadjoint orbit}"]
  & A^{\vee}
\end{tikzcd}
\qquad\text{(fibre--adjoint involution)}$$*

</div>

<div class="proof">

*Proof of Fiber–adjoint-fiber involution.* <span id="prf:fiber-adjoint-involution" label="prf:fiber-adjoint-involution"></span>

The Frobenius isomorphism $A \cong A^{\vee}$ sends $a \mapsto \int_A \circ \mu(a \otimes -)$, which is non-degenerate by the Frobenius–Hopf axiom.

**(1) Embedding via rank-$1$ projectors.** Let $\rho \colon V \to V$ be a rank-$1$ projector in $\mathbf{C}$: an endomorphism satisfying $\rho^2 = \rho$ and $\mathrm{tr}(\rho) = \mathrm{id}_{\mathbf{1}}$ (categorical trace via evaluation and coevaluation). Since $V$ has categorical dimension $2$, define the traceless component

$$\sigma(\rho) = \rho - \tfrac{1}{2}\,\mathrm{id}_V
  \;\in\; \mathrm{Ad}(A).$$

This is well-defined because $\mathrm{tr}(\sigma(\rho)) = 1 - \tfrac{1}{2} \cdot 2 = 0$. The set of such projectors is precisely $\mathbb{P}(V) = G/T$, the quotient by the maximal torus.

**(2) The involution.** Under the positive-definite involutive structure $\dagger$ ([involutive structure](#def:involutive-structure)), every rank-$1$ projector satisfies $\rho^{\dagger} = \rho$ (self-adjointness). Computing the square of the traceless component:

$$\sigma(\rho)^2
  = \bigl(\rho - \tfrac{1}{2}\,\mathrm{id}_V\bigr)^2
  = \rho^2 - \rho + \tfrac{1}{4}\,\mathrm{id}_V
  = \tfrac{1}{4}\,\mathrm{id}_V.$$

Thus $2\sigma(\rho)$ is an involution in $\mathrm{End}(V)$: it squares to the identity. Geometrically, $\sigma$ identifies $\mathbb{P}(V)$ with a coadjoint orbit in $\mathrm{Ad}(A)$. The orbit is closed by rigidity of $\mathbf{C}$ and determines a sub-object of $\mathrm{Ad}(A)$ isomorphic to $\mathbb{P}(V)$. Conversely, given this sub-object, the stabiliser of any point is $T$, so $\mathbb{P}(V) \cong G/T$ as $G$-spaces.

**(3) Observability.** Suppose there exists a non-zero morphism $f \colon \mathbf{1} \to \mathrm{Ad}(A)$. Such a morphism would represent a $G$-invariant element in the adjoint representation. By the SU(2) emergence theorem ([SU(2) emergence](#thm:su2-emergence)), the reconstructed gauge group is $G \cong \mathrm{SU}(2)$, and $\mathrm{Ad}(A)$ carries the irreducible adjoint representation $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ (dimension $3$). By Schur’s lemma, the only intertwining morphism from the trivial representation $\mathbf{1}$ to an irreducible non-trivial representation is the zero morphism. Therefore $f = 0$, contradicting our assumption.

Hence $\mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1},\, \mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0$. The non-degeneracy of $\int_A$ excludes any hidden global symmetry: there is no non-trivial invariant section of the adjoint bundle. ◻

</div>

<div id="ex:fiber-adjoint-su2" class="example">

**Example 2.30** (Fiber–adjoint-fiber involution for $\mathrm{SU}(2)$). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.Examples.su2FiberAdjoint)*

*Continuing [projective line on SU(2)](#ex:projective-line-su2), take $G = \mathrm{SU}(2)$, $T = \mathrm{U}(1)$, and $V = \mathbb{C}^2$. The projective line object is $\mathbb{P}(V) = \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C})$, and the adjoint object is $\mathrm{Ad}(A) \cong \mathfrak{su}(2) \cong \mathbb{R}^3$ (trace-free skew-Hermitian $2 \times 2$ matrices under the Killing form). The embedding $\sigma$ sends a line $\ell = \mathrm{span}(v) \subset \mathbb{C}^2$ to the rank-$1$ projector*

*$$\sigma([\ell]) =
  \frac{v v^{\dagger}}{\lVert v \rVert^2}
  - \tfrac{1}{2}\,\mathrm{id}_V
  \in \mathfrak{su}(2).$$*

*This identifies $\mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C})$ with the unit $2$-sphere $S^2 \subset \mathfrak{su}(2)$ (the coadjoint orbit of $\tfrac{1}{2}\,\mathrm{diag}(i, -i)$). Observability follows: a $G$-fixed point in $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ would be a matrix commuting with all of $\mathrm{SU}(2)$, hence a scalar — but trace-free matrices have no non-zero scalars, so $\mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1},\, \mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0$.*

</div>

<div id="ex:connection-su2" class="example">

**Example 2.31** (Connection and curvature on $\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{SU}(2))$). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.Examples.su2Connection)*

*Continuing [fibre adjoint on SU(2)](#ex:fiber-adjoint-su2), take $A = \mathcal{O}(\mathrm{SU}(2))$ with its left-invariant calculus $\Omega^1(A) = \mathrm{span}\{\omega_1, \omega_2, \omega_3\}$ ([higher forms on SU(2)](#ex:higher-forms-su2)). A connection is a covariant derivative $\nabla f = df + \mathcal{A} \cdot f$ for $f \in A$, where $\mathcal{A} = A_1\,\omega_1 + A_2\,\omega_2 + A_3\,\omega_3$ is the connection $1$-form. The Leibniz triangle says $\nabla(fg) = (\nabla f)\,g + f\,(dg)$. The curvature is the $2$-form $F_\nabla = d\mathcal{A} + \mathcal{A} \wedge \mathcal{A} \in \Omega^2(A)$, which is $A$-linear ($F_\nabla(f \cdot s) = f \cdot F_\nabla(s)$). (When the substrate parameter $q$ is introduced in [substrate parameter](#def:substrate-parameter), this calculus deforms to the Woronowicz $3D$-calculus on $\mathcal{O}_q(\mathrm{SU}(2))$.)*

</div>

## Substrate parameter and deformation

The substrate parameter $q \in \mathrm{End}(\mathbf{1})$ is not part of the categorical definition of a quantum universe or observable universe; it parametrises the $\mathbb{G}_m$-family of interpolations between the full differential $d$ and the vertical projection $\pi_V \circ d$ ([substrate parameter](#def:substrate-parameter)). The triple $(\mathbf{C}, A, \tau)$ carries both endomorphisms canonically; $q$ records *where one sits* in the $\mathbb{G}_m$-family they span. Once a substrate parameter is fixed, the categorical dimension of the fundamental object $V$ deforms from $2$ to $[2]_q = q + q^{-1}$, and the gauge group $G = \mathrm{Aut}^{\otimes}(\tau)$ ([SU(2) emergence](#thm:su2-emergence)) deforms from $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ to $\mathrm{SU}_q(2)$.

<div id="prop:braiding-eigenvalue-extraction" class="proposition">

**Proposition 2.32** (Extraction of $q$ from the braiding eigenvalues). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.braiding_eigenvalue_extraction)*

*Let $(\mathbf{C}, A, \tau)$ be a ([quantum observable universe](#def:quantum-observable-universe)) with fundamental object $V$ of rank $2$ and braiding $c_{V,V} \colon V \otimes V \to V \otimes V$. Then:*

1.  ***Spectral decomposition.** The tensor square decomposes as $V \otimes V = S^2 V \oplus \Lambda^2 V$, where $S^2 V$ (symmetric) and $\Lambda^2 V$ (antisymmetric) are the eigenspaces of $c_{V,V}$. This decomposition is *intrinsic* to $\mathbf{C}$ — it depends only on the braiding, not on any external parameter.*

2.  ***Eigenvalue definition of $q$.** Since $\Lambda^2 V \cong \mathbf{1}$ ([volume constraint](#eq:categorical-volume-constraint)) is simple, $c_{V,V}$ acts on it by a scalar $\lambda_- \in \mathrm{End}(\mathbf{1}) \cong k$. Similarly, $c_{V,V}$ acts on the $3$-dimensional $S^2 V$ by a scalar $\lambda_+$. Define $$q \;:=\; \lambda_+,
      \qquad
      \lambda_- \;=\; -q^{-1}.$$ This is a *categorical invariant*: it is determined by the braiding endomorphism of $\mathbf{C}$ alone.*

3.  ***Hecke relation.** The eigenvalue pair $(\lambda_+, \lambda_-) = (q, -q^{-1})$ is equivalent to the Hecke relation on $T = \tau(c_{V,V})$: $$(T - q)(T + q^{-1}) \;=\; 0,$$ and the product $\lambda_+ \cdot \lambda_- = -1$ (which follows from $\det(c_{V,V}) = -1$ on a rank-$2$ object with trivial determinant). The Hecke relation is intrinsic: it is a polynomial identity on the braiding morphism in $\mathbf{C}$.*

4.  ***Classical vs.\\} quantum.** When $c_{V,V}^2 = \mathrm{id}$, the eigenvalues are $+1$ and $-1$, giving $q = 1$ (symmetric monoidal, classical). When $c_{V,V}^2 \neq \mathrm{id}$, $q \neq 1$ and the category is genuinely braided — this is the quantum regime.*

5.  ***Connection to the substrate parameter.** The categorical $q$ extracted here coincides with the ([substrate parameter](#def:substrate-parameter)): the one-parameter family $d_q = q^{-1} d + (1 - q^{-1}) \pi_V \circ d$ is parametrised by the *same* $q \in \mathrm{End}(\mathbf{1})$ that appears as the braiding eigenvalue. The braiding determines the differential geometry.*

***Summary.** The deformation parameter $q$ is not imposed externally. It is the eigenvalue of the braiding $c_{V,V}$ on the symmetric summand of $V \otimes V$ — a purely categorical datum, extracted from the monoidal structure of $\mathbf{C}$ via the Hecke relation. The Tannaka–Krein reconstruction ([reconstruction](#prop:tannaka-krein-reconstruction)) then recovers the quantum group $\mathrm{SU}_q(2)$ as $\mathrm{End}^{\otimes}(\tau)$, with $q$ already determined by the category.*

</div>

<div id="prop:tannaka-krein-reconstruction" class="proposition">

**Proposition 2.33** (Tannaka–Krein reconstruction of the quantum gauge group). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.tannaka_krein_reconstruction)*

*Let $(\mathbf{C}, A, \tau)$ be a ([quantum observable universe](#def:quantum-observable-universe)) with fibre functor $\tau \colon \mathbf{C} \to R\text{-}\mathrm{Mod}$. Then the coend*

*$$H \;=\; \mathrm{End}^{\otimes}(\tau)
  \;=\; \int^{X \in \mathbf{C}}
  \tau(X)^{\vee} \otimes_R \tau(X)$$*

*carries a canonical Hopf algebra structure $(\mu, \eta, \Delta, \varepsilon, S)$ such that:*

1.  ***Reconstruction.** There is a monoidal equivalence $\mathbf{C} \simeq \mathrm{Rep}(H)$ under which $\tau$ corresponds to the forgetful functor $U \colon \mathrm{Rep}(H) \to R\text{-}\mathrm{Mod}$.*

2.  ***Universal property.** $H$ is the *universal* Hopf algebra through which $\tau$ factors: for every Hopf algebra $H'$ and monoidal natural transformation $\alpha \colon \tau \Rightarrow U \circ F$ (where $F \colon \mathbf{C} \to \mathrm{Rep}(H')$), there exists a unique Hopf map $\phi \colon H \to H'$ with $\alpha = U(\phi) \circ \mathrm{can}$.*

3.  ***Naturality in $\tau$.** The group of monoidal natural automorphisms of $\tau$ is $\mathrm{Aut}^{\otimes}(\tau) \cong G(H)$, the group-like elements (characters) of $H$.*

*In the classical case ($\mathbf{C}$ symmetric), this is Tannaka’s theorem \\}cite{tannaka1939} as algebraised by Deligne \\}cite{deligne1990}: $H = \mathcal{O}(G)$ is the coordinate ring of a compact group $G$, and $\mathrm{Aut}^{\otimes}(\tau) \cong G$.*

*In the quantum case ($\mathbf{C}$ braided but not symmetric), the reconstruction is due to Woronowicz \\}cite{woronowicz1988}: $H$ is a compact quantum group algebra $\mathcal{O}_q(G)$, and the braiding $c_{V,W}$ on $\mathbf{C}$ encodes the universal $R$-matrix of $H$. The deformation parameter $q$ is *not* an external input — it is determined by the braiding, as shown in ([braiding eigenvalue extraction](#prop:braiding-eigenvalue-extraction)).*

</div>

<div id="def:substrate-parameter" class="definition">

**Definition 2.34** (Substrate parameter). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.SubstrateParameter)*

*Let $(\mathbf{C}, A, \tau)$ be a quantum observable universe ([quantum observable universe](#def:quantum-observable-universe)) with weight decomposition $\pi_H, \pi_V$ ([weight decomposition](#def:weight-decomposition)) and Reeb derivation $\xi$ ([categorical Reeb](#def:categorical-reeb)). The non-commutative de Rham complex $(\Omega^\bullet(A), d)$ carries two canonical endomorphisms:*

1.  *the full differential $d \colon \Omega^k(A) \to \Omega^{k+1}(A)$;*

2.  *the vertical differential $\pi_V \circ d$, which retains only the component along the Reeb direction.*

*These span a one-parameter family of first-order operators parametrised by $q \in \mathrm{End}(\mathbf{1}) \cong k^{\times}$:*

*$$d_q \;=\; q^{-1}\,d \;+\; (1 - q^{-1})\,\pi_V \circ d.$$*

*$$\label{eq:substrate-family-diagram}
\begin{tikzcd}[row sep=2.5em, column sep=3em]
  \Omega^k(A) \ar[r, "d"] \ar[d, "\pi_V \circ d"'] \ar[dr, "d_q"]
  & \Omega^{k+1}(A) \\
  \Omega^{k+1}(A)
  & {} \ar[u, phantom, "q{=}1"' near start]
    \ar[l, phantom, "q{\to}\infty" near start]
\end{tikzcd}
\qquad\text{(substrate family)}$$*

*The *substrate parameter* is the unique element $q \in \mathrm{End}(\mathbf{1}) \cong k$ such that $d_q$ acts as $q^{-1}\,d$ on horizontal forms and as $d$ on vertical forms. Geometrically, $q$ is the fibre coordinate on the $\mathbb{G}_m$-family of interpolations.*

*At $q = 1$ the operator $d_q$ recovers $d$ (classicality: horizontal and vertical differentiation are treated equally). As $q \to \infty$, $d_q$ projects onto $\pi_V \circ d$ (deep-quantum regime: only the Reeb direction contributes). The substrate parameter is *not* intrinsic to the triple $(\mathbf{C}, A, \tau)$; it records where one sits in the $\mathbb{G}_m$-family that $q$ parametrises.*

*When the quantum universe is fibred over a space $M$ (as in the archimedean realisation, [$\mathbb{C}$-quantum universe](#ex:c-quantum-universe)), the categorical substrate parameter specialises to a *substrate field* $q \colon M \to k^{\times}$, encoding the local value of the $\mathrm{End}(\mathbf{1})$-element at each point.*

**Algebraic perspective.* The Lusztig integral form $\mathcal{U}^{\mathbb{Z}}_q(\mathfrak{su}(2))$ \\}cite{lusztig1993} is the universal $\mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}]$-algebra generated by $K^{\pm 1}$ and the divided powers $E^{(n)}, F^{(n)}$. A ring homomorphism $\iota \colon \mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}] \to k$, $q \mapsto q_0$, base-changes this to the quantised enveloping algebra at $q_0$. The categorical and algebraic viewpoints agree: the interpolation parameter $q$ in $d_q$ and the specialisation target $q_0 = \iota(q)$ determine the same deformation.*

</div>

<div id="thm:substrate-parameter-exists" class="theorem">

**Theorem 2.35** (Existence of the substrate parameter). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.SubstrateParameter.ofReebDecomposition)*

*Let $(\mathbf{C}, A, \tau)$ be a ([quantum observable universe](#def:quantum-observable-universe)) with [weight decomposition](#def:weight-decomposition) $(\pi_H, \pi_V)$ and [categorical Reeb derivation](#def:categorical-reeb) $(\xi, \theta_A)$. Then there exists a [substrate parameter](#def:substrate-parameter) $q \in \mathrm{End}(\mathbf{1}) \cong k$, with $q \notin \mu_\infty(k)$ (not a root of unity). In the archimedean realisation this specialises to a substrate field $q \colon M \to \mathbb{R}_{>0}$ with $q(p) \ge 1$, such that the $q$-deformed differential*

*$d_q = q^{-1}\, d + (1 - q^{-1})\, \pi_V \circ d$*

*interpolates between the full differential $d$ (at $q = 1$) and the vertical projection $\pi_V \circ d$ (as $q \to \infty$).*

*$$\label{eq:substrate-parameter-exists-diagram}
\begin{tikzcd}[row sep=2.5em, column sep=3em]
  d \ar[r, phantom, "\xleftarrow{q=1}"]
  & d_q \ar[r, phantom, "\xrightarrow{q \to \infty}"]
  & \pi_V \circ d
\end{tikzcd}
\qquad\text{(substrate interpolation)}$$*

</div>

<div class="proof">

*Proof of existence of the substrate parameter.* <span id="prf:substrate-parameter-exists" label="prf:substrate-parameter-exists"></span>

The braiding $c_{V,V} \colon V \otimes V \to V \otimes V$ of the QOU provides the substrate parameter categorically — no external choice is needed.

**Step 1 (spectral decomposition).** The volume constraint $\epsilon \colon \Lambda^2 V \twoheadrightarrow \mathbf{1}$ splits $V \otimes V = S^2 V \oplus \Lambda^2 V$ into eigenspaces of $c_{V,V}$. Since $\Lambda^2 V \cong \mathbf{1}$ is simple and $\dim S^2 V = 3$, the braiding acts by scalars $\lambda_+ \in \mathrm{End}(\mathbf{1})$ on $S^2 V$ and $\lambda_- \in \mathrm{End}(\mathbf{1})$ on $\Lambda^2 V$.

**Step 2 (define $q$).** Set $q := \lambda_+$. The determinant constraint $\lambda_+ \cdot \lambda_- = -1$ (from $\det(c_{V,V}) = -1$ on a rank-$2$ object with trivial determinant) forces $\lambda_- = -q^{-1}$. Therefore $c_{V,V}$ satisfies the Hecke relation $(T - q)(T + q^{-1}) = 0$ ([braiding eigenvalue extraction](#prop:braiding-eigenvalue-extraction)).

**Step 3 (non-degeneracy).** The QOU assumption $c_{V,V}^2 \neq \mathrm{id}$ ensures $q \neq \pm 1$. The positive-definite dagger structure forces $q \in \mathbb{R}_{>0}$, and the non-root-of-unity condition $q \notin \mu_\infty(k)$ follows from transcendence over $\mathbb{Q}$ in the archimedean realisation.

**Step 4 (agreement with $d_q$).** The categorical $q$ extracted from the braiding coincides with the interpolation parameter in $d_q = q^{-1}\,d + (1 - q^{-1})\,\pi_V \circ d$: both are characterised as the unique $q \in \mathrm{End}(\mathbf{1})$ for which the Hecke algebra $H_n(q)$ acts faithfully on $V^{\otimes n}$.

In the archimedean realisation, the constant substrate field $q(p) = q_0 > 1$ for all $p$ satisfies the classicality bound $q \ge 1$ and positivity. Non-constant substrate fields arise from the Reeb flow parameterisation of the categorical $\mathrm{End}(\mathbf{1})$-valued coordinate. ◻

</div>

<div id="ex:substrate-parameter-su2" class="example">

**Example 2.36** (Substrate parameter for $\mathrm{SU}(2)$).

*Continuing the [quantum universe for SU(2)](#ex:quantum-universe-su2), we specify the [substrate parameter](#def:substrate-parameter) that controls the deformation from classical $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ to quantum $\mathrm{SU}_q(2)$.*

***The specialisation map.** The categorical substrate parameter $q \in \mathrm{End}(\mathbf{1})$ is realised via a ring homomorphism $\iota \colon \mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}] \to \mathbb{C}$ determined by its value on the generator: $\iota(q) = q_0 \in \mathbb{C}^\times$. All algebraic structures (multiplication, comultiplication, antipode, $R$-matrix) are defined over $\mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}]$ and specialise to concrete $\mathbb{C}$-algebras via $\iota$.*

***Classical case.** Setting $q_0 = 1$ recovers the undeformed coordinate ring $\mathcal{O}(\mathrm{SU}(2))$ with its commutative multiplication:*

*$$\iota_{q_0 = 1} \colon
  \mathcal{O}_q(\mathrm{SU}(2))
  \;\longrightarrow\;
  \mathcal{O}(\mathrm{SU}(2)),
  \qquad
  \begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{pmatrix}
  \mapsto
  \begin{pmatrix} a & b \\ c & d \end{pmatrix},$$*

*where $ab = ba$, $ac = ca$, etc. This is the setting of the classical [brane tower](#ex:recursive-brane-tower-su2).*

***Quantum case.** For $q_0 = e^{\pi i / \kappa}$ with $\kappa \in \mathbb{Z}_{\geq 2}$ the Chern–Simons level, the specialisation produces $\mathcal{O}_{q_0}(\mathrm{SU}(2))$ with non-commutative relations:*

*$$ab = q_0\, ba, \quad ac = q_0\, ca, \quad
  bc = cb, \quad ad - da = (q_0 - q_0^{-1})\, bc.$$*

*The representation category $\mathrm{Rep}(\mathrm{SU}_{q_0}(2))$ is a modular tensor category with finitely many simple objects $V_0, V_{1/2}, \ldots, V_{(\kappa - 2)/2}$ when $q_0$ is a root of unity.*

***Root-of-unity truncation.** At $q_0 = e^{\pi i / \kappa}$, the spin-$j$ representations with $2j \geq \kappa - 1$ become reducible or zero, leaving a finite semisimple category. The quantum dimension of $V_j$ is*

*$$\dim_q(V_j) = \frac{q_0^{2j+1} - q_0^{-(2j+1)}}{q_0 - q_0^{-1}}
  = [2j + 1]_{q_0},$$*

*the quantum integer. For $q_0 = 1$ this reduces to the classical dimension $2j + 1$.*

***Physical interpretation.** The substrate parameter $q_0$ interpolates between the classical gauge theory ($q_0 = 1$, infinite-dimensional representation category) and the topological quantum field theory ($q_0$ a root of unity, finite modular category). The Chern–Simons level $\kappa$ controls the "granularity" of the quantum geometry.*

</div>

<div id="def:quantum-gauge-group" class="definition">

**Definition 2.37** (Quantum Gauge Group). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.QuantumGaugeGroup)*

*Let $(\mathbf{C}, A, \tau)$ be a ([quantum observable universe](#def:quantum-observable-universe)) with substrate parameter $q \in \mathrm{End}(\mathbf{1})$ ([substrate parameter](#def:substrate-parameter)), where $q$ is the braiding eigenvalue on the symmetric summand of $V \otimes V$ ([braiding eigenvalue extraction](#prop:braiding-eigenvalue-extraction)). The *quantum gauge group* is the Hopf algebra $H = \mathrm{End}^{\otimes}(\tau)$ reconstructed via Tannaka–Krein duality ([reconstruction](#prop:tannaka-krein-reconstruction)). By the universal property, $H \cong \mathcal{O}_q(\mathrm{SU}(2))$ — the coordinate ring of $\mathrm{SU}_q(2)$ at the categorically determined $q$:*

*$$G_q \;=\; \mathrm{SU}_q(2),
  \qquad
  q = \text{eigenvalue of } c_{V,V} \text{ on } S^2 V.$$*

*The classical gauge group $G = \mathrm{Aut}^{\otimes}(\tau) \cong \mathrm{SU}(2)$ ([SU(2) emergence](#thm:su2-emergence)) is the $q = 1$ case (symmetric braiding). In the archimedean realisation, where the substrate parameter specialises to a substrate field over $M$, this yields a field of quantum groups $\{G_{q(p)}\}_{p \in M}$.*

</div>

<div id="def:quantum-planck-constant" class="definition">

**Definition 2.38** (Quantum Planck Constant). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.quantumPlanckConstant)*

*Let $(\mathbf{C}, A, \tau)$ be a quantum observable universe with substrate parameter $q \in \mathrm{End}(\mathbf{1}) \cong k$ ([substrate parameter](#def:substrate-parameter)). The *quantum Planck constant* is the element $\hbar_q = 1 - q^{-1} \in k$. When the categorical substrate parameter specialises to a substrate field over a space $M$, this defines a field $\hbar_q \colon M \to k$ by $\hbar_q(p) = 1 - q(p)^{-1}$.*

</div>

<div id="def:q-hodge-star" class="definition">

**Definition 2.39** ($q$-Hodge star). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.QHodgeStar)*

*Let $(\mathbf{C}, A, \tau)$ be a quantum observable universe with categorical Hodge star $\star$ ([categorical hodge star](#def:categorical-hodge-star)) and substrate parameter $q$ ([substrate parameter](#def:substrate-parameter)). The *$q$-Hodge star* is the $q$-deformed involution $\star_q \colon \Omega^k(A) \to \Omega^{n-k}(A)$ defined by*

*$$\alpha \wedge_q \star_q \beta
  \;=\; q \cdot \int_A\!\bigl(\alpha^* \cdot \beta\bigr)\;\mathrm{vol}.$$*

*$$\label{eq:q-hodge-star-diagram}
\begin{tikzcd}[row sep=2.5em, column sep=3em]
  \Omega^k(A) \ar[r, "\star_q"] \ar[d, "\star"']
  & \Omega^{n-k}(A) \\
  \Omega^{n-k}(A) \ar[ur, "q \cdot \mathrm{id}"']
\end{tikzcd}
\qquad\text{($q$-Hodge star)}$$*

*At $q = 1$ this recovers the categorical Hodge star: $\star_1 = \star$. The factor of $q$ rescales the inner product on forms, coupling the Hodge duality to the local deformation strength.*

</div>

## Examples of quantum observable universes

We now specialise the categorical framework to the archimedean setting, where the base ring is an archimedean field $K$ (e.g. $\mathbb{Q}$, $\mathbb{R}$, or $\mathbb{C}$) and the quantum universe is realised by CR geometry on a contact manifold. The abstract categorical structures — Frobenius form, weight decomposition, $q$-deformed operators — acquire concrete geometric meaning as differential-geometric objects on a CR manifold equipped with a pseudo-Hermitian structure. The main result (§\\}ref{sec:physical-interpretation}) places gravity, gauge theory, and quantum mechanics in a unified commutative diagram within this setting.

<div id="ex:c-quantum-universe" class="example">

**Example 2.40** (Archimedean realisation: quantum universe). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.CRManifoldData)*

*Let $K$ be an archimedean field. A quantum universe over $K$ ([quantum universe](#def:quantum-universe)) is realised by the $4$-tuple $(\mathbf{C}, \theta, G, \mathcal{S})$: here $\theta$ is a contact form on a CR manifold $M$ (encoding the contact geometry and Reeb structure), $G = \mathrm{SU}(2)$ is the gauge group, and $\mathcal{S}$ is the state bundle carrying the quantum degrees of freedom. The base manifold $M$ is implicit as the domain of $\theta$; the principal bundle $P$ is implicit as the frame bundle of $\mathcal{S}$ under $G$. The precise requirements are:*

1.  *$M$ (the domain of $\theta$) is a CR manifold of hypersurface type (real dimension $2n+1$, $n \geq 1$) with non-degenerate Levi form of signature $(r,s)$, $r + s = n$;*

2.  *$\theta$ is a pseudo-Hermitian structure (contact form) on $M$, determining the Levi distribution $H = \ker\theta$, the Reeb vector field $\xi$, the Webster metric $g_\theta$ (of signature $(2r,2s)$ on $H$), and the Levi form $L_\theta$;*

3.  *$G = \mathrm{SU}(2)$;*

4.  *$\mathcal{S} = P \times_G \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C}) \to M$ is the associated *state bundle*, where $P \to M$ is the principal $G$-bundle (with holonomy reducing to $\mathrm{SO}(3) \subset \mathrm{SU}(2)/\{\pm I\}$) and $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ acts on $\mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C})$ by Möbius transformations.*

*The monoidal category is $\mathbf{C} = \mathrm{Rep}(\mathrm{SU}_{q(p)}(2))$ (the representation category of the quantum group at the substrate parameter $q(p)$, [substrate parameter](#def:substrate-parameter)), the Frobenius–Hopf object is $A = \mathcal{O}_q(\mathrm{SU}(2))$ with Frobenius form given by the Haar state, and the fibre functor $\tau$ is the forgetful functor to $K\text{-}\mathrm{Mod}$.*

</div>

When the category $\mathbf{C}$ is understood from context, we abbreviate to $(\theta, G, \mathcal{S})$. The *strictly pseudoconvex* case corresponds to signature $(n,0)$, where $L_\theta$ is positive definite — this is the primary case of physical interest, giving a positive-definite Webster metric $g_\theta$ and a well-defined Hodge star. The *indefinite* case (signature $(r,s)$ with $s > 0$) admits analogous constructions with the Webster metric of mixed signature; see ([Levi generalisation](#rem:levi-generalisation)) for the extension.

<div id="ex:c-quantum-observable-universe" class="example">

**Example 2.41** (Archimedean realisation: quantum observable universe). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.CQuantumObservableUniverse)*

*An *archimedean quantum observable universe* is an archimedean quantum universe $(\mathbf{C}, \theta, G, \mathcal{S})$ ([$\mathbb{C}$-quantum universe](#ex:c-quantum-universe)) that satisfies the vanishing conditions*

*$$H^0(M, \mathrm{Ad}(P)) = 0
  \qquad\text{and}\qquad
  \Gamma_c(M, \mathcal{S}) = 0.$$*

*These analytic conditions are the archimedean realisation of the categorical observability conditions of [quantum observable universe](#def:quantum-observable-universe): the Frobenius non-degeneracy of the Haar state on $\mathcal{O}_q(\mathrm{SU}(2))$, combined with irreducibility of the instanton connection ([irreducible connection](#lem:irreducible-connection)), forces $H^0(M, \mathrm{Ad}(P)) = 0$; the section-vanishing $\Gamma_c(M, \mathcal{S}) = 0$ follows from the non-existence of $A$-equivariant sections of the associated $\mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C})$-bundle.*

</div>

## Categorical action and variational equations

<div id="def:categorical-dirac-operator" class="definition">

**Definition 2.42** (Categorical Dirac operator). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.CategoricalDiracOperator)*

*Let $(\mathbf{C}, A, \tau)$ be a ([quantum observable universe](#def:quantum-observable-universe)) equipped with connection $\nabla$ ([categorical connection](#def:categorical-connection)), substrate parameter $q$ ([substrate parameter](#def:substrate-parameter)), and Reeb derivation $\xi$ ([categorical Reeb derivation](#def:categorical-reeb)). The *categorical Dirac operator* is the morphism*

*$$\mathcal{D}_\nabla
  \;=\;
  q^{-1}\,\nabla \;+\; (1 - q^{-1})\,\iota_\xi\,\nabla
  \;\colon\; A \to \Omega^1(A).$$*

*When $q = 1$ this reduces to $\mathcal{D}_\nabla = \nabla$, the undeformed covariant derivative. The $q$-deformation interpolates between the full connection and its projection onto the Reeb direction: as $q \to \infty$ we obtain $\mathcal{D}_\nabla \to \iota_\xi\nabla$, the purely contact component.*

</div>

<div id="def:categorical-lagrangian" class="definition">

**Definition 2.43** (Categorical Lagrangian). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.CategoricalLagrangian)*

*Let $(\mathbf{C}, A, \tau)$ be a ([quantum observable universe](#def:quantum-observable-universe)) with categorical Dirac operator $\mathcal{D}_\nabla$ ([categorical Dirac operator](#def:categorical-dirac-operator)) and a state $\psi \colon \mathbf{1} \to A$. The *categorical Lagrangian* is the endomorphism*

*$$\mathcal{L}_q(\nabla, \psi)
  \;=\;
  \mathcal{D}_\nabla^{\,2}
  \;+\;
  \psi^* \otimes \mathcal{D}_\nabla\,\psi
  \;\;\in\; \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A),$$*

*where $\psi^* = \int_A \!\circ\, S(\psi) \colon A \to \mathbf{1}$ is the adjoint section (antipode composed with the Frobenius form).*

*$$\label{eq:categorical-lagrangian-diagram}
\begin{tikzcd}[row sep=2.5em, column sep=3em]
  A \ar[r, "\mathcal{D}_\nabla"]
    \ar[dr, "\mathcal{L}_q(\nabla{,}\,\psi)"']
  & \Omega^1(A) \otimes A \ar[d, "\mathcal{D}_\nabla \,+\, \psi^* \otimes (-)"] \\
  & \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A)
\end{tikzcd}
\qquad\text{(Lagrangian)}$$*

*The Lagrangian is an endomorphism of $A$ — the categorical analog of a Lagrangian *density* $\mathscr{L}(x)$ before integration over spacetime. Its first summand $\mathcal{D}_\nabla^2$ encodes the bosonic sector (gravity + gauge curvature); the second summand encodes the fermionic coupling of the state to the connection.*

</div>

<div id="def:categorical-action" class="definition">

**Definition 2.44** (Categorical action). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.CategoricalAction)*

*Let $(\mathbf{C}, A, \tau)$ be a ([quantum observable universe](#def:quantum-observable-universe)). A *categorical action* on $(\mathbf{C}, A, \tau)$ is a morphism $\mathcal{S} \colon \mathbf{1} \to \mathbf{1}$ of the form*

*$$\label{eq:categorical-action}
  \mathcal{S}
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{ev}_A
    \;\circ\;
    \bigl(\mathrm{id}_{A^\vee} \otimes \Phi\bigr)
    \;\circ\;
    \mathrm{coev}_A,$$*

*where $\Phi \in \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A)$ is called the *physics endomorphism*.*

*$$\label{eq:categorical-action-diagram}
\begin{tikzcd}[row sep=2.5em, column sep=3em]
  \mathbf{1}
    \ar[r, "\mathrm{coev}_A"]
    \ar[rr, bend right=25, "\mathcal{S}"']
  & A \otimes A^{\vee}
    \ar[r, "\Phi \otimes \mathrm{id}"]
  & A \otimes A^{\vee}
    \ar[r, "\mathrm{ev}_A"]
  & \mathbf{1}
\end{tikzcd}
\qquad\text{(categorical action)}$$*

*The evaluation $\mathrm{ev}_A \colon A^\vee \otimes A \to \mathbf{1}$ and coevaluation $\mathrm{coev}_A \colon \mathbf{1} \to A \otimes A^\vee$ are the structure maps of the rigid duality on $A$ ([rigid monoidal category](#def:rigid-monoidal-category)). Composing them with an inserted endomorphism produces the categorical trace:*

*$$\mathcal{S} = \mathrm{tr}(\Phi).$$*

*As a string diagram, the action is a single closed loop with $\Phi$ inserted — the morphism $\mathbf{1} \to \mathbf{1}$ obtained by "tracing out" the internal degrees of freedom of $A$. The rigid structure provides the integration; the physics endomorphism encodes the dynamics.*

</div>

Let $(\mathbf{C}, A, \tau)$ be a ([quantum observable universe](#def:quantum-observable-universe)) equipped with substrate parameter $q$ ([substrate parameter](#def:substrate-parameter)), $q$-Hodge star $\star_q$ ([$q$-Hodge star](#def:q-hodge-star)), a connection $\nabla$ ([categorical connection](#def:categorical-connection)), and a section $\psi \colon \mathbf{1} \to A$ (a "state"). The following notation is used in [categorical action](#def:categorical-action):

- $\mathrm{tr} \colon \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A) \to R$ is the *categorical trace* (the composition $\mathrm{coev} \to \mathrm{id} \to \mathrm{ev}$ via the rigid structure).

- $R_{\int} \in \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A)$ is the *Frobenius–Ricci endomorphism*: the curvature of the Frobenius form $\int_A$ itself, defined by $R_{\int} = (\mathrm{id}_A \otimes \int_A) \circ F_{\nabla_{\int}}$, where $\nabla_{\int}$ is the canonical connection on $A$ induced by $\int_A$ via $\nabla_{\int}(a) = \int_A(a_{(1)}) \otimes a_{(2)} - a \otimes 1$ (Sweedler notation: $\Delta(a) = a_{(1)} \otimes a_{(2)}$, summation suppressed).

- $\mathrm{tr}_A \colon \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A \otimes \Omega^{\bullet}(A)) \to \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(\Omega^{\bullet}(A))$ is the *partial trace* over the $A$ factor.

- $\psi^* = \int_A \circ S(\psi) \colon A \to \mathbf{1}$ is the *adjoint section* (antipode composed with the Frobenius form).

- $D_\nabla = q^{-1}\,\nabla + (1 - q^{-1})\,\iota_\xi\,\nabla$ is the *$q$-deformed covariant derivative*, where $\xi$ is the Reeb derivation of $A$ ([Reeb decomposition](#ex:reeb-decomposition)).

<div id="ex:categorical-action-notation-su2" class="example">

**Example 2.45** (Categorical-action notation for $\mathrm{SU}(2)$).

*Continuing [connection on SU(2)](#ex:connection-su2), take $A = \mathcal{O}(\mathrm{SU}(2))$ with Haar integral $\int_A = \int_G$, connection $\nabla f = df + \mathcal{A} \cdot f$, and a state $\psi \in A$ (a function on the group).*

- **Categorical trace.* For $T \in \mathrm{End}(V_j)$, $\mathrm{tr}(T) = \sum_m \langle j,m \mid T \mid j,m \rangle$ is the usual matrix trace.*

- **Frobenius–Ricci.* $R_{\int}$ measures curvature of the Haar integral itself: on $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ (flat Haar measure), $R_{\int} = 0$ in the classical limit $q = 1$.*

- **Adjoint section.* For $\psi \colon \mathbb{C} \to A$, the adjoint is $\psi^*(f) = \int_G \overline{\psi(g)}\,f(g)\,dg$, i.e. the inner product with $\psi$ under the Haar integral.*

- **$q$-deformed derivative.* At $q = 1$, $D_\nabla = \nabla$ (ordinary covariant derivative). For $q \neq 1$, the Reeb component is re-weighted, coupling the connection to the contact geometry.*

</div>

<div id="prop:qou-canonical-action" class="proposition">

**Proposition 2.46** (Canonical action of a quantum observable universe). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.qou_canonical_action)*

*Let $(\mathbf{C}, A, \tau)$ be a ([quantum observable universe](#def:quantum-observable-universe)) equipped with connection $\nabla$ ([categorical connection](#def:categorical-connection)), substrate parameter $q$ ([substrate parameter](#def:substrate-parameter)), $q$-Hodge star $\star_q$ ([$q$-Hodge star](#def:q-hodge-star)), and state $\psi \colon \mathbf{1} \to A$. Then $(\mathbf{C}, A, \tau)$ determines a ([categorical action](#def:categorical-action)), unique up to a scalar $\lambda \in R^{\times}$,*

*$$\mathcal{S}_q
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{L}_q),$$*

*where $\mathcal{L}_q = \mathcal{L}_q(\nabla, \psi)$ is the categorical Lagrangian ([categorical Lagrangian](#def:categorical-lagrangian)). The physics endomorphism is $\Phi_q = \mathcal{L}_q$.*

*The square of the Dirac operator ([categorical Dirac operator](#def:categorical-dirac-operator)) decomposes via the Frobenius–Hopf structure as*

*$$\mathcal{D}_\nabla^{\,2}
  \;=\;
  q \cdot R_{\int} \;+\; \mathrm{tr}_A\!\bigl(
    F_\nabla \wedge_q \star_q F_\nabla
  \bigr),$$*

*so the categorical action expands to three terms:*

*$$\label{eq:canonical-action-decomposition}
  \mathcal{S}_q[\nabla,\, \textstyle\int_A,\, \psi]
  \;=\;
  \underbrace{\mathrm{tr}\bigl(q \cdot R_{\int}\bigr)
  }_{\text{gravity}}
  \;+\;
  \underbrace{\int_A \!\circ\, \mathrm{tr}_A\bigl(
      F_\nabla \wedge_q \star_q F_\nabla
    \bigr)
  }_{\text{gauge}}
  \;+\;
  \underbrace{\int_A\!\bigl(\psi^* \cdot \mathcal{D}_\nabla\,\psi\bigr)
  }_{\text{matter}},$$*

*with notation as in [categorical action notation](#rem:categorical-action-notation). Here $\mathrm{tr} = \mathrm{ev}_A \circ (\mathrm{id}_{A^\vee} \otimes {-}) \circ \mathrm{coev}_A$ is the categorical trace, which plays the role of spacetime integration; $R_{\int}$ is the Frobenius–Ricci endomorphism; and $F_\nabla = \nabla^2$ is the curvature.*

**Uniqueness up to scalar.* The evaluation and coevaluation maps are determined up to unique isomorphism by the duality data, and the Frobenius–Hopf axioms fix the decomposition of $\mathcal{D}_\nabla^2$ into curvature terms. The residual ambiguity is a single scalar $\lambda \in R^{\times}$: the normalization of the Frobenius form $\int_A$. Replacing $\int_A$ by $\lambda\!\int_A$ sends $\mathcal{S}_q \mapsto \lambda\,\mathcal{S}_q$. This is the categorical analog of the choice of physical units — it corresponds to the freedom in choosing $G$, $g^2$, and $\hbar$ in the archimedean realization ([Remark](#rem:physicist-translation)).*

*The scalar ambiguity is controlled by the same obstruction that governs the forgetful functor $\tau$: the observability axiom $\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbf{C}}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0$ ([QOU axiom 2](#def:quantum-observable-universe)) ensures that the trace $\mathrm{tr} \colon \mathrm{End}(A) \to R$ is faithful — no endomorphism is "invisible" to integration. Relaxing this condition (allowing hidden symmetries, $\mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)) \neq 0$) introduces a nontrivial kernel in the trace, and the obstruction to recovering a well-defined action is classified by the same cohomology class $\kappa \in H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathcal{B})$ that obstructs lifting in the Yekutieli sense ([Yekutieli lifting condition](#def:yekutieli-lifting-condition); [Yekutieli–Stokes remark](#rem:yekutieli-stokes)).*

</div>

<div id="rem:physicist-translation" class="remark">

**Remark 2.47** (Archimedean realization of the categorical action).

*In the archimedean realization ([archimedean QOU](#ex:c-quantum-observable-universe)) where $\mathbf{C} = \mathbf{Vect}_{\mathbb{R}}$, $A = C^{\infty}(M)$ for a Riemannian manifold $M$, and $\nabla$ is an Ehresmann connection on a principal $G$-bundle $P \to M$, the three constituents of the ([categorical action](#def:categorical-action)) acquire their classical meanings:*

1.  *The *categorical trace* $\mathrm{tr} = \mathrm{ev}_A \circ (\mathrm{id}_{A^\vee} \otimes {-}) \circ \mathrm{coev}_A$ becomes integration against the volume form: $\mathrm{tr}(\cdot) \to \int_M (\cdot)\,\mathrm{dvol}$.*

2.  *The *physics endomorphism* $\Phi_q = \mathcal{L}_q$ becomes the Lagrangian density $\mathscr{L}(x)$, a section of the density bundle.*

3.  *The *categorical Dirac operator* $\mathcal{D}_\nabla$ reduces to the gauge-covariant Dirac operator $D\!\!\!\!/\, = \gamma^\mu D_\mu$.*

*The three-term decomposition ([Proposition](#prop:qou-canonical-action)) then reads*

*$$\mathcal{S}_q
  \;\longrightarrow\;
  \frac{1}{16\pi G}\!\int_M R\,\mathrm{dvol}
  \;-\;
  \frac{1}{4g^2}\!\int_M \mathrm{Tr}(F \wedge \star F)
  \;+\;
  \int_M \bar\psi\, D\!\!\!\!/\;\psi\,\mathrm{dvol},$$*

*the Einstein–Hilbert + Yang–Mills + Dirac action, with $q \to 1$. The coupling constants $G$, $g$ emerge from the normalization of the Frobenius form $\int_A$ and the substrate parameter $q$ respectively; they are not free parameters of the categorical theory but are determined by the choice of archimedean realization.*

</div>

<div id="prop:variational-equations" class="proposition">

**Proposition 2.48** (Variational equations of the categorical action). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.variational_equations)*

*Let $\mathcal{S}_q$ be the ([categorical action](#def:categorical-action)). The three variational equations are:*

1.  **Gravity (vary $\int_A$)*: $\delta\mathcal{S}_q / \delta\!\int_A = 0$ yields the *categorical Einstein equation*: $$R_{\int} - \tfrac{1}{2}\,\mathrm{tr}(R_{\int})\,\mathrm{id}_A
      \;=\; T_q[\nabla, \psi],$$ where $T_q$ is the stress-energy endomorphism constructed from the gauge and matter terms.*

2.  **Gauge (vary $\nabla$)*: $\delta\mathcal{S}_q / \delta\nabla = 0$ yields the *categorical Yang–Mills equation*: $$\nabla \star_q F_\nabla + q \cdot [F_\nabla,\, \star_q F_\nabla]
      \;=\; J_\psi,$$ where $J_\psi = \psi^* \otimes D_\nabla\psi - D_\nabla\psi^* \otimes \psi$ is the matter current.*

3.  **Matter (vary $\psi$)*: $\delta\mathcal{S}_q / \delta\psi = 0$ yields the *categorical transport equation*: $$D_\nabla\,\psi \;=\; 0.$$*

*$$\label{eq:variational-equations-diagram}
\begin{tikzcd}[row sep=2.5em, column sep=3em]
  \mathcal{S}_q \ar[r, "\delta/\delta\!\int_A"]
    \ar[d, "\delta/\delta\nabla"']
    \ar[dr, "\delta/\delta\psi"]
  & R_{\int} - \tfrac{1}{2}\mathrm{tr}(R_{\int})\,\mathrm{id} = T_q \\
  \nabla \star_q F + q[F, \star_q F] = J_\psi
  & D_\nabla \psi = 0 \ar[from=ul, crossing over]
\end{tikzcd}
\qquad\text{(variational equations)}$$*

</div>

<div class="proof">

*Proof of Variational equations of the categorical action.* <span id="prf:variational-equations" label="prf:variational-equations"></span>

Each equation is obtained by computing $\delta\mathcal{S}_q = 0$ with respect to the indicated variable, using the non-degeneracy of $\int_A$.

*Item (1): Vary $\int_A$.* The gravity term $\mathrm{tr}(q \cdot R_{\int})$ depends on $\int_A$ through the Frobenius–Ricci endomorphism $R_{\int}$. Varying $\int_A \mapsto \int_A + \delta\!\int_A$ and requiring $\delta\mathcal{S}_q = 0$ for all $\delta\!\int_A$ gives, by non-degeneracy of the categorical trace, $R_{\int} - \tfrac{1}{2}\,\mathrm{tr}(R_{\int})\,\mathrm{id}_A = T_q[\nabla, \psi]$, where the stress-energy $T_q$ collects the $\int_A$-dependence of the gauge and matter terms. The trace subtraction ensures $\mathrm{tr}(T_q) = \tfrac{1}{2}\,\mathrm{tr}(R_{\int})$ (the contracted Bianchi identity).

*Item (2): Vary $\nabla$.* The gauge term $\int_A \circ \mathrm{tr}_A(F_\nabla \wedge_q \star_q F_\nabla)$ depends on $\nabla$ through $F_\nabla = \nabla^2$. A standard computation using $\delta F_\nabla = \nabla(\delta\nabla)$ and integration by parts (via non-degeneracy of $\int_A$) yields $\nabla \star_q F_\nabla + q \cdot [F_\nabla,\, \star_q F_\nabla] = J_\psi$. The commutator term $q \cdot [F_\nabla, \star_q F_\nabla]$ arises from the non-commutativity of the $q$-deformed wedge product; it vanishes when $q = 1$ (the abelian/classical limit).

*Item (3): Vary $\psi$.* The matter term $\int_A(\psi^* \cdot D_\nabla\,\psi)$ is linear in $\psi$. Varying $\psi \mapsto \psi + \delta\psi$ and using $(\delta\psi)^* \cdot D_\nabla\,\psi = 0$ for all $\delta\psi$ gives $D_\nabla\,\psi = 0$ by non-degeneracy of $\int_A$ and the dagger structure ([positive definite dagger](#prop:positive-definite-dagger)). ◻

</div>

<div id="ex:photon-wavefront" class="example">

**Example 2.49** (Continuing example: photon wavefront through a double slit).

*We trace the wavefront propagation equation $\mathcal{D}_\nabla\psi = 0$ ([wavefront propagation](#rem:wavefront-propagation)) through the concrete geometry of a double-slit experiment, with the photon ($K = \varnothing$, the empty knot) as the test particle.*

***Setup.** A photon source emits a state $\psi \colon \mathbf{1} \to A$ with $\psi \in \mathcal{H}_{q,H}^k$ (purely horizontal, [boson](#def:fermion-boson-decomposition): $\alpha_V = 0$). The photon travels through three regions:*

1.  ***Free propagation** (source $\to$ barrier). The connection is the flat instanton: $F_\nabla = 0$, so $c_2 = 0$. The Dirac operator reduces to $$\mathcal{D}_\nabla\psi
      \;=\;
      q^{-1}\,\nabla\psi + (1-q^{-1})\,\iota_\xi\,\nabla\psi
      \;=\; 0.$$ Since $\psi$ is horizontal ($\pi_V\psi = 0$), the Reeb contraction $\iota_\xi\nabla\psi$ extracts only the vertical part of the connection’s action on $\psi$. On a flat background this produces a Gaussian spreading: the beam waist $w_0$ is set by $q$ and the source geometry. As $q \to 1$, $\hbar_q \to 0$ and $w_0 \to 0$ (ray limit); as $q$ increases, the beam spreads.*

2.  ***Slit interaction** (barrier). The barrier material consists of localized knots ([localized knot](#def:localized-knot)) with knot type $K_{\mathrm{mat}}$ (e.g. Borromean rings $6_2^3$ for nucleons). At the slit walls the connection $\nabla$ is no longer flat: $F_\nabla \neq 0$, and the instanton condition $\star_q F_\nabla = F_\nabla$ constrains the curvature to be self-dual with topological charge determined by $K_{\mathrm{mat}}$. The photon wavefront encounters two openings (slits of width $d$, separation $D$). At each slit wall, the Reeb term $(1-q^{-1})\iota_\xi\nabla$ imparts a *torsion phase*: $$\tau(y)
      \;=\;
      \hbar_q \cdot \mathrm{Vol}(K_{\mathrm{mat}}) \cdot \eta(y)^2 \cdot k w,$$ where $\eta = |y|/(d/2)$ is the normalized slit coordinate, $k = 2\pi/\lambda$ is the wavenumber, and $w$ is the slit thickness. This is the $q$-deformed Huygens–Fresnel correction: the torsion is strongest at the slit walls ($\eta = 1$) and vanishes at center ($\eta = 0$).*

3.  ***Post-slit propagation** (barrier $\to$ screen). After passing through the slits, $\psi$ again satisfies $\mathcal{D}_\nabla\psi = 0$ on a flat background, but now with boundary conditions set by the two slit openings. The wavefront from each slit interferes, producing the intensity pattern $$I(x)
      \;=\;
      \left|
        \sum_{s=1}^{2}\;
        \int_{-d/2}^{d/2}
        e^{ik(r_1+r_2)}\;
        e^{i\,\tau(y)}\;
        e^{-y_s^2/w_0^2}\;
        dy
      \right|^2,$$ where $r_1, r_2$ are the source-to-slit and slit-to-screen distances, $y_s$ is the slit coordinate measured from slit center $s$, and the Gaussian factor $e^{-y_s^2/w_0^2}$ is the beam envelope determined by the free-propagation solution.*

***QOU prediction.** The torsion correction $\tau(y)$ is absent in the classical ($q = 1$) double-slit formula. Its magnitude depends on $\mathrm{Vol}(K_{\mathrm{mat}})$, the hyperbolic volume of the barrier material’s knot type. Different slit materials (silicon vs. gold vs. carbon) have different dominant knot types and hence different $\mathrm{Vol}(K_{\mathrm{mat}})$, producing *material-dependent fringe shifts* — a signature absent in standard quantum mechanics, testable with current technology.*

</div>

## Particles, fermions, bosons, and observation

<div id="def:categorical-q-ext-deriv" class="definition">

**Definition 2.50** (Categorical $q$-deformed exterior derivative). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.CategoricalQExtDeriv)*

*Let $(\mathbf{C}, A, \tau)$ be a quantum observable universe with connection $\nabla$ ([categorical connection](#def:categorical-connection)), substrate parameter $q$ ([substrate parameter](#def:substrate-parameter)), and weight decomposition $\pi_H, \pi_V$ ([weight decomposition](#def:weight-decomposition)). The *$q$-deformed exterior derivative* $d_q \colon \Omega^k(A) \to \Omega^{k+1}(A)$ is*

*$$d_q \;=\; q^{-1}\,d + (1 - q^{-1})\,\pi_V \circ d,$$*

*where $d \colon \Omega^k(A) \to \Omega^{k+1}(A)$ is the differential of the non-commutative de Rham complex. Equivalently, $d_q$ acts as $q^{-1}\,d$ on horizontal forms and as $d$ on vertical forms:*

*$$\label{eq:categorical-dq-cd}
\begin{tikzcd}[row sep=2.5em, column sep=2.5em]
  \Omega^k_H(A) \ar[r, "d"] \ar[d, hook]
  & \Omega^{k+1}(A) \ar[r, "q^{-1}"]
  & \Omega^{k+1}(A) \\
  \Omega^k(A) \ar[rru, "d_q"']
\end{tikzcd}$$*

*The *$q$-adjoint* $\delta_q \colon \Omega^{k+1}(A) \to \Omega^k(A)$ is the adjoint of $d_q$ with respect to the dagger structure ([positive definite dagger](#prop:positive-definite-dagger)).*

</div>

<div id="def:q-harmonic-form" class="definition">

**Definition 2.51** (Particle ($q$-harmonic form)). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.QHarmonicForm)*

*Let $(\mathbf{C}, A, \tau)$ be a quantum observable universe with $q$-deformed exterior derivative $d_q$ ([categorical $q$-exterior derivative](#def:categorical-q-ext-deriv)). The *$q$-Laplacian* on $\Omega^k(A)$ is $\Delta_q = d_q\,\delta_q + \delta_q\,d_q$. A *particle* is an element $\alpha \in \Omega^k(A)$ that is $q$-harmonic:*

*$$\label{eq:q-harmonic-diagram}
\begin{tikzcd}[row sep=2.5em, column sep=3em]
  \Omega^{k-1}(A)
    \ar[r, "d_q"]
  & \Omega^k(A)
    \ar[r, "d_q"]
    \ar[d, "\delta_q"'{near start}, "{\scriptstyle \Delta_q \alpha = 0}"{description, near end}]
  & \Omega^{k+1}(A)
  \\
  & \Omega^{k-1}(A)
\end{tikzcd}$$*

</div>

<div id="def:fermion-boson-decomposition" class="definition">

**Definition 2.52** (Fermion–Boson decomposition). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.Fermion)*

*Let $\mathcal{H}_q^k = \ker\Delta_q \subset \Omega^k(A)$ denote the space of particles ([$q$-harmonic form](#def:q-harmonic-form)). The weight decomposition ([weight decomposition](#def:weight-decomposition)) restricts to a short exact sequence*

*$$\label{eq:fermion-boson-ses}
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=2.5em]
  0 \ar[r]
  & \mathcal{H}_{q,H}^k \ar[r, hook]
  & \mathcal{H}_q^k \ar[r, "\pi_V"]
  & \mathcal{H}_{q,V}^k \ar[r]
  & 0
\end{tikzcd}$$*

*where $\mathcal{H}_{q,H}^k = \mathcal{H}_q^k \cap \Omega^k_H(A)$ and $\mathcal{H}_{q,V}^k = \pi_V(\mathcal{H}_q^k)$. A *boson* is a particle in the kernel $\mathcal{H}_{q,H}^k$ (purely horizontal: $\alpha_V = 0$). A *fermion* is a particle with $\alpha_V \neq 0$, i.e. one whose image under $\pi_V$ is non-zero.*

*The sequence splits via $\pi_H$:*

*$$\label{eq:fermion-boson-split}
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=2.5em]
  \mathcal{H}_q^k
    \ar[r, "\pi_H \oplus \pi_V", "\sim"']
  & \mathcal{H}_{q,H}^k \;\oplus\; \mathcal{H}_{q,V}^k
\end{tikzcd}
\qquad
\text{(bosons $\oplus$ fermion vertical parts).}$$*

</div>

<div id="def:categorical-point" class="definition">

**Definition 2.53** (Categorical point). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.CategoricalPoint)*

*Let $(\mathbf{C}, A, \tau)$ be a ([quantum universe](#def:quantum-universe)). A *categorical point* of $A$ is a morphism*

*$$\label{eq:categorical-point}
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=3em]
  \mathbf{1} \ar[r, "p"] & A
\end{tikzcd}
\qquad\text{(categorical point)}$$*

</div>

In the archimedean realisation $A = \mathcal{O}(G)$, a categorical point $p \colon \mathbf{1} \to A$ is a character $\mathrm{ev}_g \colon f \mapsto f(g)$ for some $g \in G$; equivalently, a point of the group $G$. For a manifold $M$ with $A = C^{\infty}(M)$, a point $p$ corresponds to evaluation at $p \in M$:

$$\label{eq:point-diagram}
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=2.5em]
  \{*\} \ar[r, "p"]
  & M
\end{tikzcd}
\qquad\longleftrightarrow\qquad
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=2.5em]
  \mathbf{1} \ar[r, "p"]
  & A
\end{tikzcd}$$

The *augmentation ideal* at $p$ is $\mathfrak{m}_p = \ker(p^* \colon A \to \mathbf{1})$, where $p^* = \int_A \circ \mu(p \otimes -)$. The *germ* of $A$ at $p$ is the quotient $A / \mathfrak{m}_p^2$, which captures the first-order behaviour of $A$ near $p$.

<div id="def:observation" class="definition">

**Definition 2.54** (Observation). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.Intent)*

*Let $(\mathbf{C}, A, \tau)$ be a quantum observable universe with state bundle $\mathcal{S} \to M$, let $q$ denote the ([substrate parameter](#def:substrate-parameter)), let $p \colon \mathbf{1} \to A$ be a ([categorical point](#def:categorical-point)), and let $U \subset M$ be an open causal neighbourhood of $p$.*

*An *intent on $U$* is a pair $(\mathfrak{I}, \epsilon)$ where $\epsilon \in \{+1, -1\}$ is the **direction** and*

*$$\mathfrak{I} \;\in\;
  \Gamma\bigl(U,\; \mathrm{Ad}(J^1 \mathcal{S})\bigr)$$*

*is a section of the adjoint bundle of the $1$-jet prolongation of $\mathcal{S}$. The sign $\epsilon$ determines the arrow of time: $\epsilon = +1$ (braiding, $\sigma_i$, forward under $\prec_c$) or $\epsilon = -1$ (unbraiding, $\sigma_i^{-1}$, backward).*

*The section $\mathfrak{I}$ satisfies:*

1.  ***Frobenius compatibility.** The observation preserves the Frobenius form on $U$: $$\label{eq:observation-frobenius}
    \begin{tikzcd}[row sep=2.5em, column sep=3em]
      A / \mathfrak{m}_p^2 \ar[r, "\mathfrak{I}_p"] \ar[dr, "\int_{A,p}"']
      & A / \mathfrak{m}_p^2 \ar[d, "\int_{A,p}"] \\
      & \mathbf{1}
    \end{tikzcd}$$ at every $p \in U$, where $\int_{A,p}$ is the germ of the Frobenius form. Measurement is consistent: the trace is preserved.*

2.  ***Adjoint backreaction.** The observation acts on the colour fibre via the adjoint representation of $G$. At each point $p$, the section $\mathfrak{I}_p$ conjugates by $G$: it rotates the colour degrees of freedom, shifting the substrate parameter $q \mapsto q' = q + \delta q$ via the Hopf coaction: $$\label{eq:observation-substrate}
    \begin{tikzcd}[row sep=2.5em, column sep=3em]
      A \ar[r, "\Delta"] \ar[d, "\mathfrak{I}_p"']
      & A \otimes A \ar[r, "\mathfrak{I}_p \otimes S"]
      & A \otimes A \ar[d, "\mu"] \\
      A \ar[rr, "\int_A"']
      & & \mathbf{1}
    \end{tikzcd}$$ with $\delta q(p) = \int_A(\mathfrak{I}_p(a_{(1)})\,S(a_{(2)}))$. Observing the universe changes it: the act of reading the field feeds back through the colour fibre into the Reeb flow.*

*An intent at a **point** is the restriction $\mathfrak{I}_p = \mathfrak{I}|_p$, recovering the germ-level endomorphism $\mathfrak{I}_p \colon A / \mathfrak{m}_p^2 \to A / \mathfrak{m}_p^2$. The sign $\epsilon$ determines whether the crossing injected at $p$ is $\sigma_i$ (forward, $\epsilon = +1$) or $\sigma_i^{-1}$ (backward, $\epsilon = -1$) in the braiding-induced ordering $\prec_c$.*

</div>

<div id="prop:observation-energy" class="proposition">

**Proposition 2.55** (Observation increases quantum energy and deforms the action).

***Proposition.** *Let $\mathfrak{I}\in \Gamma(U, \mathrm{Ad}(J^1 \mathcal{S}))$ be an observation ([observation](#def:observation)) with substrate perturbation $\delta q$. Then:**

1.  ***(Quantum energy increases.)** *The quantum Planck constant $\hbar_q = 1 - q^{-1}$ ([quantum Planck constant](#def:quantum-planck-constant)) satisfies* $$\hbar_{q + \delta q} - \hbar_q
      \;=\; \frac{\delta q}{q(q + \delta q)}
      \;>\; 0$$ *for $\delta q > 0$. Every observation with positive substrate perturbation strictly increases the quantum energy of the system.**

2.  ***(Action deformation.)** *The categorical action $S_q[\nabla, \lambda, \psi]$ ([categorical action](#def:categorical-action)) evaluated at the perturbed parameter $q' = q + \delta q$ satisfies* $$S_{q'}
      \;=\;
      S_q \;+\; \delta q \cdot \frac{\partial S_q}{\partial q}
      \;+\; O((\delta q)^2)$$ *The first-order shift $\partial S_q / \partial q$ is the **observation cost**: the rate at which the action changes per unit of substrate perturbation.**

3.  ***(Classical energy is unconstrained in sign.)** *The classical energy (the $q \to 1$ shadow of the action) can increase or decrease under observation, provided the change is continuous. Only the quantum energy (the $\hbar_q$-dependent terms) is monotonically increased.**

</div>

<div class="proof">

*Proof of Observation increases quantum energy and deforms the action.* <span id="prf:observation-energy" label="prf:observation-energy"></span> (1) $\hbar_q = 1 - q^{-1}$ is strictly increasing in $q$ for $q > 0$. Its derivative $d\hbar_q/dq = q^{-2} > 0$. Hence $\delta q > 0$ implies $\delta\hbar_q > 0$.

\(2\) Direct Taylor expansion of $S_{q'}$ about $q$.

\(3\) The classical action $S_1 = \lim_{q \to 1} S_q$ depends on $\nabla, \lambda, \psi$ but not on $q$. An observation that changes $\nabla$ or $\psi$ while holding $q$ fixed modifies the classical energy by the variational equations (Einstein, Yang–Mills, transport). The sign of this modification is unconstrained — it depends on the observer’s choice of how to act on the state bundle. The continuity requirement is the Frobenius compatibility axiom: the observation must preserve the trace. $\square$ ◻

</div>

## Geometric interpretations

<div id="prop:q-codifferential-formula" class="proposition">

**Proposition 2.56** (Closed formula for the $q$-codifferential $\delta_q$). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.QuantumGeometry.q_codifferential_formula)*

*Let $d_q = q^{-1}\,d + (1 - q^{-1})\,\theta \wedge \mathcal{L}_\xi$ be the $q$-exterior derivative ([categorical $q$-exterior derivative](#def:categorical-q-ext-deriv)). The formal adjoint of $d_q$ with respect to the Webster inner product $\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle_\theta$ is*

*$$\delta_q \;=\; q^{-1}\,\delta
  \;+\; (1 - q^{-1})\,\mathcal{L}_\xi^* \circ \iota_\xi,$$*

*characterised uniquely by the adjoint relation*

*$$\langle d_q\,\alpha,\, \beta \rangle_\theta
  \;=\;
  \langle \alpha,\, \delta_q\,\beta \rangle_\theta$$*

*for all compactly supported forms $\alpha, \beta$.*

</div>

## Categorical instanton and self-duality

<div id="def:categorical-instanton" class="definition">

**Definition 2.57** (Categorical instanton). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.CategoricalInstanton)*

*Let $(\mathbf{C}, A, \tau)$ be a ([quantum observable universe](#def:quantum-observable-universe)) with connection $\nabla$ ([categorical connection](#def:categorical-connection)) and $q$-Hodge star $\star_q$ ([$q$-Hodge star](#def:q-hodge-star)). The connection $\nabla$ is an *instanton* if its curvature $F_\nabla \in \Omega^2(A)$ is $\star_q$-self-dual:*

*$$\star_q\, F_\nabla \;=\; F_\nabla.$$*

*Equivalently, the curvature factors through the self-dual projection:*

*$$\label{eq:instanton-cd}
\begin{tikzcd}[row sep=2.5em, column sep=3em]
  A \otimes A \ar[r, "\nabla \circ \nabla"]
    \ar[dr, "0"']
  & \Omega^2(A) \ar[d, "\pi^-"] \\
  & \Omega^-(A)
\end{tikzcd}$$*

*where $\pi^- = \tfrac{1}{2}(\mathrm{id} - \star_q)$ is the anti-self-dual projector and $\Omega^-(A) = \ker(\mathrm{id} + \star_q)$.*

</div>

<div id="lem:categorical-irreducible" class="lemma">

**Lemma 2.58** (Irreducibility from observability). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.categorical_irreducible)*

*Let $(\mathbf{C}, A, \tau)$ be a quantum observable universe. Any categorical instanton $\nabla$ ([categorical instanton](#def:categorical-instanton)) is irreducible: $\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbf{C}}(\mathbf{1},\,\mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0$.*

*$$\label{eq:categorical-irreducible-diagram}
\begin{tikzcd}[column sep=2.5em]
  \mathbf{1} \ar[r, "0"] & \mathrm{Ad}(A)
\end{tikzcd}
\qquad\text{(the only morphism is zero)}$$*

</div>

<div class="proof">

*Proof of Irreducibility from observability.* <span id="prf:categorical-irreducible" label="prf:categorical-irreducible"></span> [<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.categorical_irreducible)

Suppose $s \colon \mathbf{1} \to \mathrm{Ad}(A)$ is a non-zero invariant morphism. The following diagram commutes:

Since $\mathrm{Ad}(A)$ is the trace-free part of $A \otimes A^*$, the Frobenius form $\int_A$ vanishes on it: $\int_A \circ s = 0$. But $\int_A$ is non-degenerate by the observability axiom, so $s = 0$. ◻

</div>

<div id="prop:categorical-self-duality" class="proposition">

**Proposition 2.59** (Categorical self-duality). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.categorical_self_duality)*

*Let $(\mathbf{C}, A, \tau)$ be a quantum observable universe with volume form $\mathrm{vol} \in \Omega^n(A)$ ([$q$-Hodge star](#def:q-hodge-star)). Every connection $\nabla$ that is a critical point of the categorical Yang–Mills functional*

*$$S[\nabla] \;=\; \int_A\!\bigl(\star_q(F_\nabla) \cdot F_\nabla\bigr)$$*

*is an instanton ([categorical instanton](#def:categorical-instanton)). That is, the following diagram commutes:*

*$$\label{eq:self-duality-cd}
\begin{tikzcd}[row sep=2.5em, column sep=3.5em]
  \Omega^2(A) \ar[r, "\star_q"] \ar[d, "\int_A(\,\cdot\, {*}\, \cdot\,)"']
  & \Omega^2(A) \ar[d, "\int_A(\,\cdot\, {*}\, \cdot\,)"] \\
  \mathbf{1} \ar[r, "\mathrm{id}"']
  & \mathbf{1}
\end{tikzcd}
\qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
F_\nabla \in \Omega^+(A).$$*

</div>

<div class="proof">

*Proof of Categorical self-duality.* <span id="prf:categorical-self-duality" label="prf:categorical-self-duality"></span> [<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.categorical_self_duality)

By the Bogomolny decomposition in the dagger category,

$$\int_A(F_\nabla^* \cdot F_\nabla)
  \;=\; 2\,\int_A({F_\nabla^-}^* \cdot F_\nabla^-)
        + \int_A(F_\nabla \wedge_q F_\nabla),$$

where the second term is topological (determined by the class $[F_\nabla] \in \Omega^2(A)/\mathrm{exact}$). Minimising $S[\nabla]$ forces $F_\nabla^- = 0$, which is exactly the self-duality condition. ◻

</div>

## Non-vanishing of $d_q^2$ and jet prolongation

<div id="prop:categorical-dq-squared" class="proposition">

**Proposition 2.60** (Non-vanishing of $d_q^2$). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.categorical_dq_squared)*

*Let $d_q$ be the categorical $q$-deformed exterior derivative ([categorical $q$-exterior derivative](#def:categorical-q-ext-deriv)). The composition $d_q^2 = d_q \circ d_q \colon \Omega^k(A) \to \Omega^{k+2}(A)$ is given by*

*$$d_q^2\,\alpha
  \;=\; q^{-1}(1 - q^{-1})\;\omega_V \wedge_q [\xi,\, \alpha],$$*

*where $\omega_V \in \Omega^2(A)$ is the curvature of the weight decomposition (the image of the unit $1_A$ under $\pi_V \circ d \circ d$) and $[\xi, \alpha]$ is the Lie derivative along the generator $\xi$ of the $T$-action ([weight decomposition](#def:weight-decomposition)).
