## Universal enveloping algebras and quantum groups

<div id="def:quantum-su2" class="definition">

**Definition 4.10** (Quantum group $\mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{su}(2))$). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.QuantumSu2) Let $q\in\mathbb{C}^{*}$ with $0<\lvert q\rvert\le 1$. The *quantum group* $\mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{su}(2))$ is the associative $\mathbb{C}$-algebra generated by $E,F,K,K^{-1}$ subject to*

*$$\begin{aligned}
  KK^{-1}&=K^{-1}K=1,
    \label{eq:quantum-KK}\\[3pt]
  KEK^{-1}&=q^2\,E,\quad KFK^{-1}=q^{-2}\,F,
    \label{eq:quantum-KE}\\[3pt]
  [E,F]&=\frac{K-K^{-1}}{q-q^{-1}}.
    \label{eq:quantum-EF}
\end{aligned}$$*

*In the classical limit $q\to 1$, the generator $K$ reduces to $\exp(h\,e_3)$ and the relations recover the $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ commutation relations.*

</div>

<div id="prop:r-matrix-braiding-structure" class="proposition">

**Proposition 4.11** (Yang–Baxter equation and braid operator from the $R$-matrix). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.Braiding.r_matrix_braiding_structure)*

*The universal $R$-matrix $\mathcal{R} \in \mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{su}(2)) \;\hat{\otimes}\; \mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{su}(2))$ ([quantum SU(2)](#def:quantum-su2)) satisfies the Yang–Baxter equation*

*$$\mathcal{R}_{12}\,\mathcal{R}_{13}\,\mathcal{R}_{23}
  \;=\;
  \mathcal{R}_{23}\,\mathcal{R}_{13}\,\mathcal{R}_{12},$$*

*and the braid operator $\check{R} = P \circ \mathcal{R}$ (where $P$ is the tensor swap) furnishes a representation of the braid group on any tensor product of finite-dimensional $\mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{su}(2))$-modules, replacing the classical twist/flip involutions ([braid twist-flip](#def:braid-twist-flip)).*

</div>

<div id="rem:r-matrix-braiding" class="remark">

**Remark 4.12** ($R$-matrix and braiding).

*The $R$-matrix of $\mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{su}(2))$ ([quantum SU(2)](#def:quantum-su2)) is the universal element*

*$$\mathcal{R}\;\in\;
  \mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{su}(2))\;\hat{\otimes}\;
  \mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{su}(2))$$*

*satisfying the Yang–Baxter equation $\mathcal{R}_{12}\mathcal{R}_{13}\mathcal{R}_{23} =\mathcal{R}_{23}\mathcal{R}_{13}\mathcal{R}_{12}$. Its action on a tensor product of representations gives the braid operator $\check{R}=P\circ\mathcal{R}$ (where $P$ is the swap), furnishing a $q$-deformed braid group representation that replaces the classical twist/flip involutions ([braid twist-flip](#def:braid-twist-flip)).*

</div>

<div id="prop:skein-crossing-asymmetry" class="proposition">

**Proposition 4.13** (Crossing asymmetry and per-crossing Coulomb correction). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.Braiding.skein_crossing_asymmetry)*

*The Skein relation weights positive crossings by $q$ and negative crossings by $q^{-1}$:*

*$$q \, L_+ \;-\; q^{-1} L_-
  \;=\; (q^{1/2} - q^{-1/2})\, L_0.$$*

*For $q > 1$, the per-crossing repulsive Coulomb correction relative to a mixed-charge baseline is*

*$$\delta_{\mathrm{Coulomb}}
  \;=\; q \;-\; \tfrac{1}{2}(q + q^{-1})
  \;=\; \tfrac{1}{2}(q - q^{-1})
  \;>\; 0,$$*

*and the ratio of the antisymmetric (Coulomb) to symmetric (strong) Skein weights is*

*$$\frac{q - q^{-1}}{q + q^{-1}}
  \;=\; \tanh(\ln q).$$*

*At $q = 1$ the asymmetry vanishes; at $q \to \infty$ the ratio approaches $1$.*

</div>

<div id="rem:skein-crossing-asymmetry" class="remark">

**Remark 4.14** (Crossing asymmetry and emergent Coulomb repulsion).

*The $R$-matrix braiding ([R-matrix](#rem:r-matrix-braiding)) introduces a fundamental asymmetry between positive and negative crossings: the Skein relation*

*$$q \, L_+ \;-\; q^{-1} L_-
  \;=\; (q^{1/2} - q^{-1/2})\, L_0$$*

*weights positive crossings by $q$ and negative crossings by $q^{-1}$. Since $q > 1$, positive crossings contribute *more* to the Skein polynomial than negative ones. This asymmetry is the topological origin of electromagnetic repulsion.*

***Emergent Coulomb repulsion.** For a hadron $\mathfrak{H}$ with Coulomb charge $Q(\mathfrak{H})$ ([Coulomb charge](#def:coulomb-charge)), the crossing energy ([crossing energy](#def:crossing-energy)) decomposes into a symmetric (strong) baseline and an antisymmetric (Coulomb) correction. The per-crossing repulsive correction between composites of the same charge relative to a mixed-charge baseline is*

*$$\delta_{\mathrm{Coulomb}}
  \;=\; q \;-\; \tfrac{1}{2}(q + q^{-1})
  \;=\; \tfrac{1}{2}(q - q^{-1})
  \;> 0.$$*

***Unification of strong and electromagnetic interactions.** Electromagnetic repulsion is *not* a separate force in the QOU framework. It is a **phase asymmetry** in the same Skein polynomial that encodes the strong binding. Both interactions arise from the $R$-matrix braiding of $\mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{su}(2))$, with $q$ controlling the relative strength:*

- *The strong binding is proportional to $\tfrac{1}{2}(q + q^{-1})$ (the baseline Skein weight).*

- *The electromagnetic repulsion is proportional to $\tfrac{1}{2}(q - q^{-1})$ (the crossing asymmetry).*

*Their ratio is*

*$$\frac{\text{Coulomb}}{\text{Strong}}
  \;=\; \frac{q - q^{-1}}{q + q^{-1}}
  \;=\; \tanh\!\left(\ln q\right).$$*

*At $q = 1$ (classical limit), the asymmetry vanishes and the electromagnetic interaction disappears. At $q \to \infty$ (deep-quantum regime), the ratio approaches $1$ and the two interactions become comparable.*

*The specific assignment of Coulomb charges to protons and neutrons — and the consequences for nuclear stability — require the Descartes universe ($\chi = -6$) and are developed in Chapter 6.*

</div>

## Categorical Möbius energy and self-avoidance

<div id="prop:mobius-energy" class="proposition">

**Proposition 4.15** (Categorical recovery of Möbius energy). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.Braiding.mobius_energy)*

*Let $(\mathbf{C}, A, \tau)$ be a quantum observable universe ([Definition](#def:quantum-observable-universe)) with substrate parameter $q$ ([Definition](#def:substrate-parameter)), categorical action $\mathcal{S}_q$ ([Definition](#def:categorical-action)), and $q$-Hodge star $\star_q$ ([Definition](#def:q-hodge-star)).*

*Let $\varrho \colon S^1 \to \tau(A)$ be a smooth closed curve (a knot embedding) and let $\mathfrak{m}(\varrho)$ denote the categorical mass ([Theorem](#thm:topological-mass)).*

*Define the *categorical Möbius energy* by*

*$$E_{\mathrm{cat}}(\varrho)
  \;=\;
  \int_A \!\circ\, \mathrm{tr}_A \!\iint_{S^1 \times S^1 \setminus \mathrm{diag}}
  \!\!\Bigl(
    \Delta(\varrho(s)) \otimes \Delta(\varrho(t))
  \Bigr)
  \;\star_q\;
  \Bigl\lVert
    \frac{d\varrho}{ds} \wedge_q \frac{d\varrho}{dt}
  \Bigr\rVert\,
  ds\, dt\,,$$*

*where $\Delta$ is the Hopf comultiplication, $\int_A$ is the Frobenius form ([Remark](#rem:frobenius-simplification)), and the integration excludes the diagonal $\mathrm{diag} \subset S^1 \times S^1$.*

*Then in the classical limit $q \to 1$, the categorical Möbius energy recovers the classical Möbius energy up to a topological normalization:*

*$$\lim_{q \to 1}\; E_{\mathrm{cat}}(\varrho)
  \;=\;
  \frac{1}{4}\, E(\varrho)
  \;+\; \text{const}\,.$$*

*Here $E(\varrho)$ is the classical Möbius energy*

*$$E(\varrho)
  \;=\;
  \iint_{S^1 \times S^1}
  \Bigl(
    \frac{1}{\lvert \varrho(s) - \varrho(t) \rvert^2}
    \;-\;
    \frac{1}{D(\varrho(s), \varrho(t))^2}
  \Bigr)
  \lvert \varrho'(s) \rvert \, \lvert \varrho'(t) \rvert\,
  ds\, dt\,.$$*

*Here $D(\varrho(s), \varrho(t))$ denotes the intrinsic arc-length distance along $\varrho$.*

</div>

<div class="proof">

*Proof of Categorical recovery of Möbius energy.* <span id="prf:mobius-energy" label="prf:mobius-energy"></span> [<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.MobiusEnergy)

The proof proceeds in three steps.

*Step 1: Gauge fixing via the categorical volume constraint.* The categorical volume constraint fixes the gauge group to $G = \mathrm{SU}(2)$, acting on the $\mathbb{CP}^1$ fibre by Möbius transformations. This ensures that $E_{\mathrm{cat}}(\gamma)$ is invariant under the full Möbius group $\mathrm{PSL}(2, \mathbb{C})$, matching the conformal invariance of the classical functional.

*Step 2: Expansion of the Frobenius–Hopf kernel.* At $q = 1$ the $q$-Hodge star reduces to the classical Hodge star, and the comultiplication $\Delta$ becomes cocommutative. The [Frobenius pairing](#def:frobenius-pairing) $\int_A \circ \mu$ on $A \otimes A$ reduces to the standard $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ Killing form, so the integrand simplifies to

$$\mathrm{tr}\bigl(
    \Delta(\gamma(s)) \otimes \Delta(\gamma(t))
  \bigr)
  \;\xrightarrow{q \to 1}\;
  \frac{1}{\lvert \gamma(s) - \gamma(t) \rvert^2}.$$

The repulsive kernel $1/r^2$ is thus the classical shadow of the resistance of the Frobenius–Hopf object $A$ to local deformations of the connection $\nabla$: the Frobenius form $\int_A$ assigns a diverging cost when two strands of $\gamma$ approach.

*Step 3: Subtraction of the self-energy.* The diagonal regularization in the categorical integral (exclusion of $\mathrm{diag} \subset S^1 \times S^1$) matches the arc-length subtraction $1/D(\gamma(s),\gamma(t))^2$ in the classical Möbius energy. In the $q$-deformed setting, this subtraction arises naturally from the antipode $S$ of the Hopf structure: the self-pairing $\int_A(\gamma(s)^* \cdot S(\gamma(s)))$ cancels the short-distance divergence at $s = t$, leaving a finite integral that agrees with $E(\gamma)/4$ up to an Euler characteristic correction $\chi(\Sigma_\gamma) \cdot \mathrm{const}$, where $\Sigma_\gamma$ is any Seifert surface spanning $\gamma$. ◻

</div>

<div id="cor:non-self-intersection" class="corollary">

**Corollary 4.16** (Obstruction to self-intersection). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.Braiding.non_self_intersection)*

*Let $\varrho$ be a knot embedding with categorical Möbius energy $E_{\mathrm{cat}}(\varrho)$ as in [Proposition](#prop:mobius-energy), and let $q \neq 1$ be the substrate parameter ([Definition](#def:substrate-parameter)).*

*The non-cocommutativity of the Hopf structure at $q \neq 1$ provides a categorical obstruction to self-intersection: the energy $\mathfrak{m}(\varrho)$ diverges whenever two non-adjacent strands of $\varrho$ approach within the fibre $\tau(A)$.*

</div>

<div class="proof">

*Proof of Obstruction to self-intersection.* <span id="prf:non-self-intersection" label="prf:non-self-intersection"></span> [<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.NonSelfIntersection)

The mechanism is as follows. The universal $R$-matrix $\mathcal{R} \in \mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{su}(2)) \hat{\otimes} \mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{su}(2))$ ([Remark](#rem:r-matrix-braiding)) controls the failure of the cocommutativity square

$$\sigma \circ \Delta \;\neq\; \Delta,$$

where $\sigma$ is the tensor swap. At $q = 1$ one has $\mathcal{R} = 1 \otimes 1$ and the comultiplication is cocommutative, so strands may pass through each other freely (the "classical" regime where self-intersection is not penalised by the energy functional).

For $q \neq 1$, the braiding $\check{R} = \sigma \circ \mathcal{R}$ is non-trivial, and the categorical mass acquires a singular contribution from non-adjacent strand proximity. Concretely, because $\mathfrak{m}(\varrho)$ depends on the $q$-Hodge star $\star_q$ ([Definition](#def:q-hodge-star)), the cost of two non-adjacent points $\varrho(s)$, $\varrho(t)$ approaching is governed by the $q$-deformed commutator

$$[\hat{X}, \hat{P}]_q
  \;=\;
  \hat{X}\hat{P} - q\,\hat{P}\hat{X}
  \;=\;
  i\hbar_q,$$

which replaces the classical $1/r^2$ repulsion kernel with the strictly stronger

$$\frac{1}{\lvert \varrho(s) - \varrho(t) \rvert^2}
  \;\longmapsto\;
  \frac{[2]_q}{\lvert \varrho(s) - \varrho(t) \rvert^2
  - \hbar_q^{\,2}},$$

where $[2]_q = q + q^{-1}$ is the quantum integer and $\hbar_q = 1 - q^{-1}$ is the quantum Planck constant. This kernel has a hard singularity at $\lvert \varrho(s) - \varrho(t) \rvert = \hbar_q$, creating an energy barrier of infinite height at the quantum scale.

Physically, the $R$-matrix endows the vortex filament $\varrho$ with a "quantum exclusion zone" of radius $\hbar_q$: the filament cannot pass through itself because doing so would require infinite categorical energy. This is the knot-theoretic analogue of the Pauli exclusion principle, with the non-cocommutativity of $\Delta_q$ playing the role of fermionic statistics. ◻

</div>

## Crossing energy and Coulomb charge

<div id="def:crossing-energy" class="definition">

**Definition 4.17** (Crossing energy of a knot composite). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.Braiding.CrossingEnergy)*

*Let $\mathfrak{H} = [K_1, \ldots, K_n]_p \bowtie \mathcal{L}$ be a composite of knots linked by a link $\mathcal{L}$, with braid word $\beta \in B_n$ representing the linking. The *crossing energy* of $\mathfrak{H}$ is*

*$$\mathbf{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(\mathfrak{H})
  \;=\;
  \sum_{\text{crossings in } \beta}
  \begin{cases}
    q   & \text{positive crossing } (L_+), \\
    -q^{-1} & \text{negative crossing } (L_-),
  \end{cases}$$*

*where $q$ is the substrate parameter ([substrate parameter](#def:substrate-parameter)) and the sign convention follows the Skein relation*

*$$q \, L_+ \;-\; q^{-1} L_-
  \;=\; (q^{1/2} - q^{-1/2})\, L_0.$$*

*The crossing energy measures the net Skein weight of the composite: positive $\mathbf{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}$ indicates repulsion dominates, negative indicates binding dominates. This quantity is computed entirely from the $R$-matrix braiding ([R-matrix](#rem:r-matrix-braiding)) of $\mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{su}(2))$ acting on the tensor product of constituent representations.*

</div>

<div id="def:coulomb-charge" class="definition">

**Definition 4.18** (Coulomb charge of a knot composite). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.Braiding.CoulombCharge)*

*Let $\mathfrak{H}$ be a knot composite with braid word $\beta$. Write $n_+(\beta)$ and $n_-(\beta)$ for the number of positive and negative crossings in $\beta$. The *Coulomb charge* of $\mathfrak{H}$ is*

*$$Q(\mathfrak{H}) \;=\; \tfrac{1}{2}\bigl(n_+(\beta) - n_-(\beta)\bigr).$$*

*The crossing energy ([crossing energy](#def:crossing-energy)) decomposes as*

*$$\mathbf{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(\mathfrak{H})
  \;=\;
  \underbrace{\tfrac{1}{2}(n_+ + n_-)(q + q^{-1})}_{\text{baseline (strong)}}
  \;+\;
  \underbrace{Q(\mathfrak{H}) \cdot (q - q^{-1})}_{\text{Coulomb correction}}.$$*

*The first term is symmetric in $q \leftrightarrow q^{-1}$ and represents the strong binding; the second is antisymmetric and vanishes at $q = 1$. The Coulomb charge $Q(\mathfrak{H})$ governs the magnitude and sign of the electromagnetic correction:*

- *$Q(\mathfrak{H}) > 0$: net positive crossings, repulsive Coulomb contribution.*

- *$Q(\mathfrak{H}) = 0$: electromagnetically neutral.*

- *$Q(\mathfrak{H}) < 0$: net negative crossings, attractive Coulomb contribution.*

*The ratio of Coulomb to strong contributions is $\tanh(\ln q) \approx 0.104$ at $q = q_0$.*

</div>

## Lagrange Resolvents and $q$-Deformed Kinematics

<div id="prop:lagrange-resolvent-transform" class="proposition">

**Proposition 4.19** (Discrete Fourier transform diagonalises $C_5$ on the Bring’s surface). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.BringsSurface.lagrange_resolvent_transform)*

***Proposition.** Let $C_n$ act on a vector space $V$ of dimension $n$ with coordinates $x_0, \ldots, x_{n-1}$, and let $\zeta = e^{2\pi i/n}$. The **Lagrange resolvent transform** (discrete Fourier transform on $C_n$) is*

*$$w_k \;=\; \frac{1}{\sqrt{n}}\sum_{j=0}^{n-1}\zeta^{kj}\,x_j,
  \qquad k \in \{0, \ldots, n-1\}.$$*

*Then:*

1.  *The cyclic permutation $\sigma \colon x_j \mapsto x_{j+1}$ acts diagonally: $\sigma(w_k) = \zeta^{-k} w_k$. The $C_n$ symmetry is manifest as phase rotation of the Fourier modes.*

2.  *Any $C_n$-invariant polynomial constraint on the $x_j$ transforms to a constraint on $C_n$-equivariant combinations of the $w_k$ (products pairing $w_k$ with $w_{n-k}$, i.e.\\} conjugate modes).*

*For $n = 5$ (the case relevant to [Bring’s surface](#def:brings-surface)), the three power-sum constraints transform to: $w_0 = 0$ (linear projection), $w_1 w_4 + w_2 w_3 = 0$ (Hermitian quadric), and $w_1^2 w_3 + w_4^2 w_2 + w_2^2 w_1 + w_3^2 w_4 = 0$ (symmetric cubic).*

</div>

<div id="rem:lagrange-resolvents" class="remark">

**Remark 4.20** (Lagrange resolvents and spectral form).

*Let $\zeta=e^{2\pi i/n}$. The discrete Fourier transform on $C_n$ ([Lagrange resolvent transform](#prop:lagrange-resolvent-transform)) diagonalises the cyclic action: $\sigma(w_k) = \zeta^{-k} w_k$. Any $C_n$-invariant polynomial constraint on the coordinates $x_j$ transforms to constraints on $C_n$-equivariant combinations of the Fourier modes $w_k$.*

*For $n = 5$ ([Bring’s surface](#def:brings-surface)), the three power-sum equations become:*

*$$\begin{aligned}
  w_0 &= 0
    &&\text{(linear projection),}
    \label{eq:resolvent-linear}\\[4pt]
  w_1\,w_4+w_2\,w_3 &= 0
    &&\text{(Hermitian quadric),}
    \label{eq:resolvent-quadric}\\[4pt]
  w_1^2\,w_3+w_4^2\,w_2+w_2^2\,w_1+w_3^2\,w_4 &= 0
    &&\text{(symmetric cubic).}
    \label{eq:resolvent-cubic}
\end{aligned}$$*

*The quadric pairs conjugate modes ($w_k$ with $w_{5-k}$); the cubic pairs squared modes in the skip-one pattern. These are the $C_5$-equivariant invariants $h_2$ and $h_3$ ([aggregate color quantities](#rem:aggregate-color-quantities)).*

</div>

<div id="def:q-momentum" class="definition">

**Definition 4.21** ($q$-Momentum from the braid writhe). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.Descartes.QMomentum)*

*The **$q$-momentum** of a particle is the writhe of its braid representative, weighted by the Hecke deformation parameter.*

***Definition.** Let $\beta \in B_n$ be a braid representative of a particle knot $K = \hat{\beta}$ (braid closure), with generators $\sigma_{i_1}^{\epsilon_1} \cdots \sigma_{i_k}^{\epsilon_k}$ where $\epsilon_j = \pm 1$. The **$q$-momentum** is:*

*$$p_q(\beta) \;=\; \sum_{j=1}^{k} \epsilon_j \,
  \frac{q^{\epsilon_j} - q^{-\epsilon_j}}{q - q^{-1}}
  \;=\; \sum_{j=1}^{k} \frac{q^{2\epsilon_j} - 1}{q^2 - 1}$$*

*At $q = 1$: $p_q(\beta) \to w(\beta)$, the classical writhe (sum of crossing signs).*

*At the substrate parameter $q$: each positive crossing contributes $[1]_q = 1$ and each negative crossing contributes $[-1]_q = -1$, but with $q$-weighting that distinguishes the two.*

***Equivalently**, the $q$-momentum is the trace of the braid in the fundamental representation of $H_n(q)$:*

*$$p_q(\beta) \;=\; \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{fund}}(\rho(\beta))$$*

*where $\rho: B_n \to H_n(q)$ is the Hecke representation.*

***Properties.***

1.  ***Additivity under concatenation**: $p_q(\beta_1 \beta_2) = p_q(\beta_1) + p_q(\beta_2)$ (from the trace being linear on the Hecke algebra).*

2.  ***Invariance under Markov I**: $p_q$ is conjugation-invariant (cyclic property of the trace).*

3.  ***Shift under Markov II**: stabilization $\beta \mapsto \beta \sigma_n^{\pm 1}$ shifts $p_q$ by $\pm [1]_q$. This is the $q$-analogue of adding one unit of momentum.*

4.  ***Parity**: Under the mirror $\sigma: \beta \mapsto \beta^{\sigma}$ (reverse all crossings), $p_q(\beta^{\sigma}) = -p_{q^{-1}}(\beta)$. Parity violation at $q \neq 1$ means $p_q(\beta^{\sigma}) \neq -p_q(\beta)$.*

***Building block values.***

| *Knot*                 | *Braid word*                                      | *Writhe $w$* | *$p_q(q_0)$* |
|:-----------------------|:--------------------------------------------------|:------------:|:------------:|
| *$0_1$ (unknot)*       | *$e$*                                             |    *$0$*     |    *$0$*     |
| *$3_1$ (trefoil)*      | *$\sigma_1^3$*                                    |    *$+3$*    |    *$+3$*    |
| *$3_1^{\sigma}$*       | *$\sigma_1^{-3}$*                                 |    *$-3$*    |    *$-3$*    |
| *$4_1$ (figure-eight)* | *$\sigma_1 \sigma_2^{-1} \sigma_1 \sigma_2^{-1}$* |    *$0$*     |    *$0$*     |
| *$5_1$ (cinquefoil)*   | *$\sigma_1^5$*                                    |    *$+5$*    |    *$+5$*    |

</div>

<div id="def:q-angular-momentum" class="definition">

**Definition 4.22** ($q$-Angular momentum from the $\mathrm{SU}_q(2)$ Casimir). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.Descartes.QAngularMomentum)*

*The **$q$-angular momentum** of a particle is the $\mathrm{SU}_q(2)$ Casimir eigenvalue of its knot representation.*

***Definition.** Let $K = \hat{\beta}$ be a knot/link with braid representative $\beta \in B_n$. The **$q$-angular momentum** is defined by the $q$-Casimir operator $C_q$ of $\mathrm{SU}_q(2)$:*

*$$J_q^2(K) \;=\; [j]_q \, [j+1]_q
  \;=\; \frac{q^j - q^{-j}}{q - q^{-1}} \cdot
        \frac{q^{j+1} - q^{-(j+1)}}{q - q^{-1}}$$*

*where $j$ is the spin quantum number determined by the Jones-Wenzl projector $p_n$ acting on the $n$-strand braid: $j = n/2$ for the highest-weight component.*

*At $q = 1$: $J_q^2 \to j(j+1)$, the standard Casimir.*

***The $q$-deformed angular momentum operators.***

*The generators $J_+, J_-, J_z$ of $\mathrm{SU}_q(2)$ satisfy:*

*$$[J_z, J_{\pm}] = \pm J_{\pm}, \qquad
  [J_+, J_-] = [2 J_z]_q
  \;=\; \frac{q^{2J_z} - q^{-2J_z}}{q - q^{-1}}$$*

*This differs from the classical $[J_+, J_-] = 2J_z$ by replacing $2J_z$ with its $q$-number $[2J_z]_q$. The asymmetry at $q \neq 1$ is directly connected to parity violation ([parity violation](#prop:parity-violation-skein)): the raising and lowering operators are not related by a simple conjugation.*

</div>

<div id="def:q-energy" class="definition">

**Definition 4.23** ($q$-Deformed Energy). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.Descartes.QEnergy)*

*The **$q$-energy** of a particle knot $K$ is the sum of three terms, each derived from the categorical triple $(\mathbf{C}, A, \tau)$ and the substrate parameter $q$.*

***Definition.** Let $K = \hat{\beta}$ be a particle knot with braid representative $\beta \in B_n$. The **$q$-energy** is:*

*$$\mathbf{E}_q(K) \;=\; \underbrace{J_q^2(K) \cdot \hbar_q}_{\text{rotational}}
  \;+\;
  \underbrace{p_q(\beta)^2 \cdot \hbar_q / (2\,[n]_q)}_{\text{translational}}
  \;+\;
  \underbrace{S_q(K)}_{\text{action (rest mass)}}$$*

*where:*

- *$J_q^2(K) = [j]_q [j+1]_q$ is the $q$-angular momentum ([q-angular momentum](#def:q-angular-momentum)),*

- *$p_q(\beta)$ is the $q$-momentum (writhe) ([q-momentum](#def:q-momentum)),*

- *$S_q(K) = \mathrm{tr}_\tau(\rho(\beta))$ is the categorical action — the Markov trace of the braid in the Hecke algebra $H_n(q)$,*

- *$\hbar_q = 1 - q^{-1}$ is the quantum Planck constant,*

- *$[n]_q = (q^n - q^{-n})/(q - q^{-1})$ is the $q$-number.*

***The three terms.***

1.  ***Rotational term** $J_q^2 \cdot \hbar_q$: The $q$-deformed rotational energy. For a spin-$\frac{1}{2}$ particle at the substrate parameter $q$: $[1/2]_q [3/2]_q \cdot \hbar_q \approx 0.818 \times 0.0991 = 0.0811$. This vanishes at $q = 1$ (where $\hbar_q \to 0$).*

2.  ***Translational term** $p_q^2 \cdot \hbar_q / (2[n]_q)$: The $q$-deformed kinetic energy from the writhe. The $[n]_q$ in the denominator is the $q$-deformed "number of strands" (inertia).*

3.  ***Action term** $S_q(K)$: The categorical action $S_q = \mathrm{tr}(\mathscr{L}_q)$ evaluated on the knot. This is the **rest mass energy** — the net sum of all crossing energies in the braid word:*

*$$S_q(K) \;=\; \sum_{\text{crossings}} \mathbf{E}_\times(q)
  \;=\; \frac{\mathrm{Vol}(K)}{\hbar_q^2}$$*

*The action term dominates: for hadrons, $S_q \sim 10^3$ MeV while the rotational and translational terms are $O(\hbar_q) \sim 0.1$.*

***At rest** ($p_q = 0$, $J_q = 0$):*

*$$\mathbf{E}_q(K)\big|_{\text{rest}} \;=\; S_q(K) \;=\; \mathfrak{m}(K) c^2$$*

*recovering the topological mass formula.*

***Limits.***

| *Limit*                         | *$\mathbf{E}_q$*                                                |
|:--------------------------------|:----------------------------------------------------------------|
| *$q = 1$ (classical)*           | *$j(j+1) \cdot 0 + w^2 \cdot 0 + S_1 = S_1$*                    |
| *$q \to \infty$ (deep-quantum)* | *$J_q^2 \to q^{2j+1}, \; p_q \to w \cdot q, \; S_q \to \infty$* |
| *Rest frame*                    | *$S_q(K)$ (mass)*                                               |

***Relation to crossing energy.***

*Each crossing in the braid word contributes energy $\mathbf{E}_\times(q) = \frac{1}{2}(q - q^{-1}) = 0.1045$ (in units of the mass scale $\mu_0$). The total action is:*

*$$S_q(K) \;=\; \sum_{j=1}^{k} \mathbf{E}_\times^{(\epsilon_j)}(q)$$*

*where $\epsilon_j = \pm 1$ is the crossing sign. For a positive crossing: $\mathbf{E}_\times^{(+)} = q$. For a negative crossing: $\mathbf{E}_\times^{(-)} = q^{-1}$. The asymmetry $q \neq q^{-1}$ at the substrate parameter $q$ means positive crossings carry more energy than negative ones — this is the energy signature of parity violation.*

</div>

## Vertex Operators and the Markov Trace

<div id="def:exceptional-divisor" class="definition">

**Definition 4.24** (Exceptional divisor at $p$). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.ExceptionalDivisor) Let $(\mathbf{C}, \theta, G, \mathcal{S})$ be a QOU and let $p \in M$ be a brane point with outward normal $N(p) = p/\lvert p\rvert$ and positively-oriented tangent frame $(T_1, T_2)$. Set $R = R_{\mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C})}$ and*

*$$O(p) \;=\; p + R\,N(p).$$*

*The *exceptional divisor* at $p$ is the fibre of the state bundle $\mathcal{S}$ at $p$ — the $\mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C})$ fibre*

*$$\mathcal{S}_p \;=\; \pi^{-1}(p)
  \;=\;
  \bigl\{\,
    O(p) + R\bigl(\sin\phi\,(\cos\psi\,T_1 + \sin\psi\,T_2) - \cos\phi\,N\bigr)
    \;:\;
    \phi \in [0,\pi],\; \psi \in [0,2\pi)
  \,\bigr\},$$*

*where $\pi\colon \widetilde{M} \to M$ is the blow-up map that replaces $p$ with $\mathcal{S}_p \cong \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C})$.*

</div>

<div id="def:reeb-bundle" class="definition">

**Definition 4.25** (Reeb bundle over the exceptional divisor). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.ReebBundle)*

*Let $(\mathbf{C}, \theta, G, \mathcal{S})$ be a QOU and let $\mathcal{S}_p \cong \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C})$ be the exceptional divisor at a brane point $p$ ([exceptional divisor](#def:exceptional-divisor)). The **Reeb bundle** at $p$ is the principal $U(1)$-bundle*

*$$\mathcal{R}_p
  \;=\;
  \bigl(\,
    S^3 \;\xrightarrow{\;\pi_H\;}\; \mathcal{S}_p \cong S^2,
  \;\xi_q\,\bigr),$$*

*where $\pi_H$ is the Hopf fibration and $\xi_q$ is the [$q$-Reeb vector field](#ex:q-reeb-vector-field) generating the $U(1)$ fibre action. The total space $S^3$ carries the contact structure $\ker\theta|_{S^3}$, and the substrate parameter $q$ ([substrate parameter](#def:substrate-parameter)) determines the connection $1$-form: the holonomy around a generator of $\pi_1(S^1)$ is $e^{2\pi i / [2]_q}$, where $[2]_q = q + q^{-1}$ is the quantum integer.*

*The Reeb bundle has three roles:*

1.  ***Base** $\mathcal{S}_p \cong S^2$: parametrises the directions of departure from $p$ — the internal colour space.*

2.  ***Fibre** $U(1)$: the Reeb direction, generated by $\xi_q$ — the one axis in the colour fibre where observations commute.*

3.  ***Total space** $S^3$: the arena where braid words in $B_n$ are evaluated via the Hecke algebra $H_n(q)$.*

</div>

<div id="def:vertex-operator" class="definition">

**Definition 4.26** (Vertex operator on the exceptional divisor). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.VertexOperator)*

*Let $(\mathbf{C}, \theta, G, \mathcal{S})$ be a QOU, let $\mathcal{S}_p \cong \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C})$ be the exceptional divisor at a brane point $p$ ([exceptional divisor](#def:exceptional-divisor)), and let $\mathcal{R}_p$ be the Reeb bundle over $\mathcal{S}_p$ ([Reeb bundle](#def:reeb-bundle)).*

***The formal variable.** In the standard VOA formalism, the formal variable $z$ is an indeterminate in the ring of formal Laurent series. In the QOU it has a geometric realisation: $z$ is the affine coordinate $z = v_1/v_2$ on the projective line $\mathcal{S}_p \cong \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C})$ ([projective line](#ex:projective-line-su2)), which coincides with the contact affine coordinate $Z = \alpha_H / \iota_\xi\,\alpha$ ([contact affine chart](#def:contact-affine-chart)) restricted to the fibre $\mathcal{S}_p$. Algebraically, on the standard affine chart $v_2 \neq 0$, $z$ generates the coordinate ring $\mathbb{C}[z]$.*

*The **vertex operator algebra** of the QOU at $p$ is the triple $(V, Y, |0\rangle)$ defined as follows.*

***Graded state space.** The $\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 0}$-graded vector space is the brane tower:*

*$$V \;=\; \bigoplus_{n \geq 0} V_n,
  \qquad V_n \;=\; A_n \;=\; J^n(A_0),$$*

*where $A_0 = \mathcal{O}(\mathrm{SU}_q(2))$ is the coordinate ring and $J^n$ denotes the $n$-th jet prolongation ([jet prolongation](#prop:jet-prolongation)). The grading $n$ is the **conformal weight**: the eigenvalue of the Reeb charge operator $L_0 = \xi_q^{(0)}$ (the zero-mode of the $q$-Reeb vector field).*

***State-operator correspondence.** The map*

*$$Y \colon V \;\longrightarrow\; (\mathrm{End}\,V)[\![z, z^{-1}]\!]$$*

*assigns to each state $a \in V_n$ a **vertex operator** (a formal Laurent series in $z$):*

*$$Y(a, z) \;=\; \sum_{m \in \mathbb{Z}} a_m\, z^{-m-1},$$*

*where the **modes** $a_m \in \mathrm{End}\,V$ are defined by the $R$-matrix insertion:*

*$$a_m
  \;=\;
  \oint_{|z| = 1} Y(a, z)\, z^m\, \frac{dz}{2\pi i}
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(
    \check{R}_{(a)}\, z^m
  \bigr),$$*

*with $\check{R}_{(a)} = P \circ \mathcal{R}$ the braid operator ([R-matrix braiding](#rem:r-matrix-braiding)) applied to the state $a$, and $\mathrm{tr}_M$ the Markov trace ([Jones–Markov trace](#thm:jones-markov-trace)). The contour integral is taken around the equator of $\mathcal{S}_p \cong S^2$, i.e.  
along a fibre of the Reeb bundle $\mathcal{R}_p$.*

***Vacuum and translation.***

*$$|0\rangle = 1 \in A_0, \qquad
  T = L_{-1} = j \colon A_n \to A_{n+1},$$*

*where $j$ is the jet prolongation map. The vacuum is the unknot (identity element of $A_0$), and the translation operator advances one level in the brane tower.*

***OPE as Skein resolution.** When two insertion points $z, w$ on $\mathcal{S}_p$ collide, the operator product expansion*

*$$Y(a, z)\, Y(b, w)
  \;\sim\;
  \sum_{n \geq 0}
  \frac{Y(c_n, w)}{(z - w)^{n+1}}$$*

*has its **leading singularity** governed by the Hecke relation $(T_i - q)(T_i + q^{-1}) = 0$, which is the Skein relation*

*$$L_+ - L_- \;=\; (q - q^{-1})\, L_0.$$*

*The collision $z \to w$ is two strands meeting on $\mathcal{S}_p$; the resolution into $L_+$, $L_-$, $L_0$ is the OPE decomposition into singular channels. The two eigenvalues $q$ and $-q^{-1}$ of $T_i$ correspond to the symmetric (bosonic) and antisymmetric (fermionic) OPE channels respectively.*

</div>

<div id="prop:vertex-is-exceptional-divisor" class="proposition">

**Proposition 4.27** (Vertex operators factor through the exceptional divisor). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.vertex_is_exceptional_divisor)*

*Let $(\mathbf{C}, \theta, G, \mathcal{S})$ be a QOU with exceptional divisor $\mathcal{S}_p = \pi^{-1}(p) \cong \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C})$ at a brane point $p$ ([exceptional divisor](#def:exceptional-divisor)), and let $\mathcal{R}_p$ denote the Reeb bundle over $\mathcal{S}_p$ ([Reeb bundle](#def:reeb-bundle)). Then:*

1.  ***Localisation.** Every Hecke generator $T_i \in H_n(q)$ acting on $V^{\otimes n}$ factors through the fibre functor restricted to $\mathcal{S}_p$. That is, the vertex operator $T_i \colon V^{\otimes n} \to V^{\otimes n}$ is supported on $\mathcal{S}_p$ and acts trivially on the base algebra $A_0$.*

2.  ***Confinement.** Every Skein resolution $L_+ - L_- = (q - q^{-1})\,L_0$ is evaluated within the Reeb bundle $\mathcal{R}_p = S^3 \xrightarrow{\pi_H} \mathcal{S}_p$. The braid word $\beta \in B_n$ representing the interaction is evaluated as a Markov trace in $H_n(q)$ over $\mathcal{R}_p$, and the result projects to $A_0$ via the blow-down map $\pi$.*

3.  ***Completeness.** Every interaction that changes quantum numbers at $p$ — crossing change, pair creation, virtual exchange — is realised by a finite braid word in $B_n$ whose Hecke image $\rho(\beta) \in H_n(q)$ acts within $\mathcal{R}_p$. No interaction requires data from outside the blow-up at $p$.*

</div>

<div class="proof">

*Proof.* <span id="prf:vertex-is-exceptional-divisor" label="prf:vertex-is-exceptional-divisor"></span> **(1) Localisation.** The braiding of $\mathbf{C}$ is given by the universal $R$-matrix $\mathcal{R} \in \mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{g})^{\otimes 2}$ ([R-matrix braiding](#rem:r-matrix-braiding)), which acts on $V^{\otimes n}$ by permuting tensor factors with a $q$-dependent phase. The Hecke generator is $T_i = \tau_i \circ R_{i,i+1}$, where $\tau_i$ is the transposition. Under the fibre functor $\tau$, the representation $V$ is a module over the coordinate ring $\mathcal{O}(G_q)$, which is the structure sheaf of the exceptional divisor $\mathcal{S}_p \cong \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C})$ (the quantum flag variety of $G_q$ at $q$). The $R$-matrix acts fibrewise: it permutes sections of $V$ over $\mathcal{S}_p$ without involving sections of the base algebra $A_0$. Hence $T_i$ is supported on $\mathcal{S}_p$.

**(2) Confinement.** The Skein relation $L_+ - L_- = (q - q^{-1})\,L_0$ is the image of the Hecke relation $(T_i - q)(T_i + q^{-1}) = 0$ under the Markov trace. Since $T_i$ acts within $\mathcal{S}_p$ (part 1), and the Markov trace is computed over the Reeb bundle $\mathcal{R}_p$ (the $U(1)$-bundle whose connection is $\xi_q$), every Skein resolution is evaluated within $\mathcal{R}_p$. The blow-down map $\pi\colon \widetilde{M} \to M$ collapses $\mathcal{S}_p$ to $p$, projecting the resolved link invariant to the base level.

**(3) Completeness.** The Hecke algebra $H_n(q)$ is generated by $\{T_1, \ldots, T_{n-1}\}$ subject to the Hecke and braid relations. Every element of $H_n(q)$ is a finite linear combination of products of these generators ([braid action on tensor products](#prop:braid-action-tensor)). Since each generator acts within $\mathcal{R}_p$, so does every finite product. Crossing changes, pair creation (R-II moves), and virtual exchange are all expressible as finite braid words in $B_n$, whose Hecke images lie in $H_n(q)$. No operation requires data from outside the blow-up. ◻

</div>

<div id="thm:markov-trace-product" class="theorem">

**Theorem 4.28** (Product factorization of the Markov trace). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.markov_trace_product)*

*Let $\beta \in B_n$ be a braid on $n$ strands and let $\rho(\beta) \in H_n(q)$ be its image under the Hecke quotient ([Jones–Markov trace](#thm:jones-markov-trace)). After Hecke reduction, the element $\rho(\beta)$ decomposes as a product of **generator chains**: for each generator $\sigma_i$ ($i = 0, \ldots, n-2$), the crossings at $\sigma_i$ reduce to a linear combination $a_i \sigma_i + b_i$ with $a_i, b_i \in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}]$.*

***Theorem.** The Markov trace factors as a product over generators:*

*$$\mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(\rho(\beta)\bigr)
  \;=\;
  \prod_{i=0}^{n-2} \hat{V}_i(q),
  \qquad
  \hat{V}_i(q) \;=\; z \cdot a_i + b_i,$$*

*where $z = 1/(q^{1/2} + q^{-1/2})$ is the Markov trace parameter. Each $\hat{V}_i$ is the **vertex volume** at generator $\sigma_i$ — the evaluation of the vertex operator $Y(\sigma_i, z_i)$ at the $i$-th insertion point on the exceptional divisor ([vertex operator](#def:vertex-operator)).*

***Proof.** The Markov trace processes the product by peeling generators from the right. At each step, $\sigma_i$ is the rightmost (largest-index) generator in the remaining word, and the Markov property gives:*

*$$\mathrm{tr}_M(\cdots (a_i \sigma_i + b_i))
  \;=\;
  (z \cdot a_i + b_i) \cdot \mathrm{tr}_M(\cdots).$$*

*This works because:*

1.  *The chain at $\sigma_i$ reduces to $a_i \sigma_i + b_i$ (linear in $\sigma_i$ and the identity).*

2.  *The Markov property $\mathrm{tr}_M(x \sigma_n) = z\,\mathrm{tr}_M(x)$ applies to the $\sigma_i$ term.*

3.  *Generator $\sigma_i$ is the rightmost active generator, so the Markov property applies directly.*

4.  *The remaining word involves only $\sigma_0, \ldots, \sigma_{i-1}$, independent of $\sigma_i$.*

*Applying this recursively from $i = n-2$ down to $i = 0$ gives the product formula. $\square$*

</div>

<div id="def:categorical-transfer-matrix" class="definition">

**Definition 4.29** (Categorical transfer matrix). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.CategoricalTransferMatrix)*

*Let $\mathfrak{H}_p = [K_1, \ldots, K_n]_p \bowtie \mathcal{L}$ be a [hadron](#def:hadron) at a brane point $p$ ([localized hadron](#def:localized-hadron)), and let $\mathcal{S}_p$ be the exceptional divisor at $p$ ([exceptional divisor](#def:exceptional-divisor)).*

***Insertion points and the configuration space.** The constituent knots $K_i$ are simple objects in $\mathbf{C}$, each factoring through a tensor power of $V$ ([knot factorization](#rem:knot-factorization)): $K_i \hookrightarrow V^{\otimes 2j_i}$ via the PawLei embedding $\iota_{j_i}$. The index $i$ labels the **constituent slot**, not the knot type: several slots may carry the same simple object (e.g.\\} a proton has $K_1 = K_2 = T_{2,3}$ for two up quarks). Each constituent has a [vertex operator](#def:vertex-operator) $Y(K_i, z_i)$ inserted at a point $z_i \in \mathcal{S}_p$. The $n$-tuple of insertion points is a point of the **ordered configuration space***

*$$(z_1, \ldots, z_n) \;\in\;
  \mathrm{Conf}_n(\mathcal{S}_p)
  \;=\;
  \bigl\{\,(z_1, \ldots, z_n) \in \mathcal{S}_p^{\,n}
  : z_i \neq z_j \text{ for } i \neq j\,\bigr\}.$$*

*The ordering matches the constituent list of $\mathfrak{H} = [K_1, \ldots, K_n]$; identical knot types occupy distinct points on $\mathcal{S}_p$. The constraint $z_i \neq z_j$ is the source of OPE singularities $(z_i - z_j)^{-k}$ — it is what distinguishes two copies of the same knot within a single fibre.*

*These insertion points are **not free** after the first crossing: the link $\mathcal{L}$ encoding the internal entanglement imposes algebraic relations among them. Concretely, each Hopf link between $K_i$ and $K_j$ constrains the pair $(z_i, z_j)$ via the OPE singularity — the Hecke relation $(T - q)(T + q^{-1}) = 0$ evaluated at the collision $z_i \to z_j$.*

***Interaction filtration.** The configuration space algebra carries a **bi-filtration** reflecting the two sources of structure in the Reeb flow ([observation braid](#rem:observation-braid)):*

1.  ***Ascending (jet prolongation).** The brane tower $A_0 \hookrightarrow A_1 \hookrightarrow A_2 \hookrightarrow \cdots$ ([jet prolongation](#prop:jet-prolongation)) grows with each Planck step. At step $k$, the configuration space lifts to the $k$-th jet: insertion points acquire $k$-th order Taylor data, and knots with crossing number $\leq k$ become encodable ([jet-Planck steps](#rem:jet-planck-steps)). A configuration $\mathcal{S}_0 = \sum_i (p_i, H_i)$ ([bundle initial conditions](#def:bundle-initial-conditions)) at any reference point in the affine chart may contain arbitrarily many constituents — including hadrons and photons ($K = \varnothing$) — each carrying only zeroth-order fibre data. The subsequent configurations $\mathcal{S}_1, \mathcal{S}_2, \ldots$ represent the forward light cone of interactions from that reference point; $\mathcal{S}_{-1}, \mathcal{S}_{-2}, \ldots$ represent the backward light cone (undoing computation).*

2.  ***Descending (Hecke relations).** Within a given jet level, each crossing between slots $i$ and $j$ adds a Hecke relation $(T - q)(T + q^{-1}) = 0$ to an **interaction ideal** $I_k \subset \mathcal{O}(\mathrm{Conf}_n(\mathcal{S}_p))$. The ideals are nested: $I_1 \subset I_2 \subset \cdots \subset I_m$, so relations from earlier crossings are **never forgotten**. The quotient $\mathcal{O}_n / I_k$ shrinks monotonically — the insertion points become more constrained with each interaction.*

*The two directions are complementary: jet prolongation **opens** new degrees of freedom (higher-order Taylor coefficients, heavier knot types), while Hecke relations **close** them (correlating the insertion points that have interacted). The information-theoretic content of a hadron is the balance between these two: $\eta_q$ nats of information per step ([operational entropy](#def:operational-entropy)) measures the net rate at which the ascending tower outruns the descending constraints.*

***Two levels of braiding operation.** A braiding operation on $\mathfrak{H}$ can be described at two levels:*

1.  ***Constituent level.** Operate on the insertion points $(z_1, \ldots, z_n)$ individually. A crossing between $K_i$ and $K_j$ applies the vertex operator $Y(\sigma_k, z_k)$ at the relevant generator $\sigma_k$, producing a transfer matrix $T_{K_i, K_j}(q) \in \mathrm{M}_2(\mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}])$ that acts on the Hecke chain at $\sigma_k$.*

2.  ***Composite level.** Operate on the single insertion point $z_H$ of the composite knot $K_{\mathfrak{H}} = \hat{\beta}_{\mathfrak{H}}$ (the closure of the hadron braid word). The Markov trace of the full braid word factors as a product of vertex volumes ([Markov trace product](#thm:markov-trace-product)): $\mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\beta_{\mathfrak{H}})) = \prod_i \hat{V}_i(q)$.*

***The categorical transfer matrix.** A **categorical transfer matrix** for $\mathfrak{H}_p$ is the equivalence class*

*$$\mathcal{T}(\mathfrak{H})
  \;=\;
  \bigl[\, T \,\bigr]_{\sim}
  \;\in\;
  \mathrm{End}\bigl(H_n(q)\bigr) \,\big/\, \sim$$*

*where $T$ is any braiding operation on $\mathfrak{H}$ (at either level) and the equivalence relation $\sim$ identifies two operations $T_1 \sim T_2$ whenever they produce the same vertex volume:*

*$$T_1 \sim T_2
  \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
  \hat{V}(T_1, q) = \hat{V}(T_2, q)
  \quad\text{as polynomials in } q.$$*

*This is well-defined because the vertex volume $\hat{V}_i(q)$ depends only on the Markov trace of the Hecke-reduced element — not on the specific braid representative, the decomposition of $\mathfrak{H}$ into constituents, or the path of braiding operations within $\mathcal{S}_p$.*

</div>

<div id="prop:transfer-matrix-level-independence" class="proposition">

**Proposition 4.30** (Transfer matrix level independence). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.transfer_matrix_level_independence)*

*Let $\mathfrak{H}_p = [K_1, \ldots, K_n]_p \bowtie \mathcal{L}$ be a hadron with composite knot $K_{\mathfrak{H}} = \hat{\beta}_{\mathfrak{H}}$. Let $\mathcal{T}(\mathfrak{H}_p)$ be the categorical transfer matrix ([categorical transfer matrix](#def:categorical-transfer-matrix)). Then:*

1.  ***Constituent-composite agreement.** The Markov trace computed from the constituent insertion points $(z_1, \ldots, z_n)$ and the Markov trace computed from the composite insertion point $z_H$ yield the same Skein polynomial: $$\prod_{i=0}^{n-2} \hat{V}_i^{\mathrm{const}}(q)
      \;=\;
      \hat{V}^{\mathrm{comp}}(q)
      \;=\;
      P_{K_{\mathfrak{H}}}(q).$$*

2.  ***Path independence on $\mathcal{S}_p$.** Two braiding operations $T_1, T_2$ on $\mathfrak{H}$ that produce isotopy-equivalent configurations ([isotopy equivalence](#def:bundle-isotopy-equivalence)) have the same categorical transfer matrix: $\mathcal{T}(T_1) = \mathcal{T}(T_2)$. In particular, the specific sequence of crossing changes within the exceptional divisor $\mathcal{S}_p$ does not affect the result — only the equivalence class of the final configuration matters.*

3.  ***Well-definedness.** The categorical transfer matrix $\mathcal{T}(\mathfrak{H})$ depends only on the isotopy class of the hadron $\mathfrak{H}$ and the knot types $K_i$ of its constituents. It is independent of:*

    - *the braid representative $\beta_{\mathfrak{H}}$,*

    - *the PawLei embedding $\iota_{j_i}$ for each constituent,*

    - *the order of crossings evaluated within $\mathcal{S}_p$.*

</div>

<div class="proof">

*Proof.* <span id="prf:transfer-matrix-level-independence" label="prf:transfer-matrix-level-independence"></span> **(1) Constituent-composite agreement.** The hadron $\mathfrak{H} \hookrightarrow V^{\otimes 2(j_1 + \cdots + j_n)}$ embeds into a tensor power of $V$ via the PawLei basis ([knot factorization](#rem:knot-factorization)). The braid word $\beta_{\mathfrak{H}} \in B_N$ (where $N = 2(j_1 + \cdots + j_n)$) acts on $V^{\otimes N}$ through the Hecke algebra $H_N(q)$.

At the **constituent level**, the crossings between $K_i$ and $K_j$ are grouped by generator index, and the Markov trace factors as $\prod \hat{V}_i^{\mathrm{const}}$ ([Markov trace product](#thm:markov-trace-product)).

At the **composite level**, the same braid word $\beta_{\mathfrak{H}}$ has a unique Hecke reduction in $H_N(q)$, and the Markov trace yields $P_{K_{\mathfrak{H}}}(q) = \mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\beta_{\mathfrak{H}}))$.

These are equal because the Markov trace product formula is an **exact algebraic identity** in $H_N(q)$: the product $\prod \hat{V}_i$ and the direct trace $\mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\beta_{\mathfrak{H}}))$ evaluate the same element of $H_N(q)$. The factorization is not an approximation — it is a rewriting of the trace using the Markov property.

**(2) Path independence on $\mathcal{S}_p$.** All braiding takes place within the exceptional divisor ([vertex operators factor through $\mathcal{S}_p$](#prop:vertex-is-exceptional-divisor)). Two braiding operations $T_1, T_2$ that produce isotopy-equivalent configurations have braid words $\beta_1, \beta_2$ whose closures $\hat{\beta}_1, \hat{\beta}_2$ are ambient-isotopic. By the link invariance of the Markov trace ([Jones–Markov trace](#thm:jones-markov-trace), property 3), $\mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\beta_1)) = \mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\beta_2))$. Hence $\hat{V}(T_1) = \hat{V}(T_2)$ and $\mathcal{T}(T_1) = \mathcal{T}(T_2)$.

The specific sequence of crossings within $\mathcal{S}_p$ does not matter: all that matters is the isotopy class of the resulting link. This is the content of "what happens in the exceptional divisor stays in the exceptional divisor" — the blow-down map $\pi$ collapses $\mathcal{S}_p$ to $p$, erasing the internal history.

**(3) Well-definedness.** Independence from the braid representative is the link invariance of the Markov trace (part 2). Independence from the PawLei embedding follows from the $q$-Schur–Weyl duality: any two embeddings $\iota, \iota'$ of $V_{j_i}$ into $V^{\otimes 2j_i}$ differ by an element of the Hecke algebra centralizer, which commutes with the Markov trace. Independence from the order of crossing evaluation follows from the right-to-left peeling argument in the Markov trace product ([Markov trace product](#thm:markov-trace-product)): the generators are peeled in decreasing order, and the result is independent of the order in which crossings at a fixed generator were originally applied. $\square$ ◻

</div>

<div id="prop:topological-mass-formula" class="proposition">

**Proposition 4.31** (Topological mass formula (Archimedean)). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.Torsion.ArchimedeanMassFormula)*

*In the archimedean realisation ([$\mathbb{C}$-quantum observable universe](#ex:c-quantum-observable-universe)), the topological decomposition of mass ([topological mass](#thm:topological-mass)) specialises to a closed-form relationship between the mass of a particle, the hyperbolic volume of its associated knot, and the quantum Planck constant.*

***Proposition.** Let $(\mathbf{C}, A, \tau)$ be the $\mathbb{C}$-quantum observable universe and let $K$ be a hyperbolic knot whose complement carries the vortex topology of a stable particle, generated by $N$ blow-ups along the brane tower. The descent involution $\hat{\tau}_n$ ([descent involution](#def:descent-involution)) induces the idempotent splitting $\mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_{n+1}) = \mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{desc}} \oplus \mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{trans}}$ ([descent eigenspaces](#prop:descent-eigenspaces)). Under the archimedean fibre functor, the descended trace evaluates to the holonomy $\mathrm{Hol}_{\nabla_A}$ and each transient trace to the quantum dilogarithm $\Phi_q(z_i)$, giving the mass formula*

*$\mathfrak{m}(K) \;=\; \frac{\mathrm{Vol}(K)}{\hbar_q^{\,2}},$*

*where $\mathrm{Vol}(K)$ is the hyperbolic volume of $S^3 \setminus K$ and $\hbar_q = 1 - 1/q$ is the quantum Planck constant ([quantum Planck constant](#def:quantum-planck-constant)) at the substrate parameter $q$ ([substrate parameter](#def:substrate-parameter)).*

*The derivation proceeds from the categorical decomposition ([topological mass](#thm:topological-mass)) via three identifications, each following from the archimedean bridge:*

1.  *The baseline holonomy term $\lVert \mathrm{Hol}_{\nabla_A}(\varrho_0;\, \mathfrak{G}) \rVert$ evaluates to $\mathrm{Vol}(K)$ via the Chern–Simons/volume correspondence for the hyperbolic knot complement.*

2.  *The exceptional divisor contributions $\Phi_q(z_i)$ sum, after evaluation in the Briggs–Klein spectral coordinates, to $\mathrm{Vol}(K) \cdot (1/\hbar_q^{\,2} - 1)$.*

3.  *Adding baseline and exceptional terms: $\mathfrak{m} = \mathrm{Vol}(K) + \mathrm{Vol}(K)(1/\hbar_q^{\,2} - 1) = \mathrm{Vol}(K)/\hbar_q^{\,2}$.*

*Combined with the knot–particle dictionary identifying particles with specific knots (e.g.\\} the figure-eight knot $4_1$ with the muon), this formula determines the substrate parameter $q$ from experimental mass ratios (see [§6.10](#sec:small-scale)).*

</div>

<div id="rem:skein-decomposition" class="remark">

**Remark 4.32** (Skein Decomposition and Topological Mass Ratios).

*This remark formalizes the refinement of the particle-topology mapping by shifting from torus knots to a framework grounded in **hyperbolic volumes** and **Skein-deformed residues**. By treating mass as the geometric resistance of the 1-jet bundle prolongation, the $q$-deformed Skein relation provides a rigorous "Mass Sum Rule" for composite hadronic states.*

</div>

<div id="prop:vertex-algebra-relations" class="proposition">

**Proposition 4.33** (QU and QUO axioms as relations on Hecke generators). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.VertexAlgebra.descartes_genus)*

*The vertex operator algebra $(V, Y, |0\rangle)$ ([vertex operator](#def:vertex-operator)) inherits every QU and QUO axiom as a relation on the Hecke generators $T_1, \ldots, T_{n-1}$ of $H_n(q)$. Below we list each axiom and its explicit translation into **knot coordinates** — braid words in $T_i$, the affine coordinate $z$ on $\mathcal{S}_p$, the Markov trace $\mathrm{tr}_M$, and cup/cap morphisms $\cup\colon \mathbf{1} \to V^{\vee} \otimes V$, $\cap\colon V \otimes V^{\vee} \to \mathbf{1}$.*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## QU Axioms (Quantum Universe)

### QU-1: Rigid braided monoidal structure

*The braiding $c_{V,V}$ acts on $V^{\otimes n}$ via the Hecke representation $\rho_n\colon B_n \to H_n(q)$ with $T_i = \rho_n(\sigma_i)$. Rigidity and braiding are encoded by three families of relations:*

***(QU-1a) Hecke relation** (quadratic):*

*$$T_i^2 \;=\; (q - q^{-1})\,T_i + 1
  \qquad (1 \leq i \leq n-1).$$*

*Equivalently $(T_i - q)(T_i + q^{-1}) = 0$: the eigenvalues $q$ (symmetric/bosonic channel) and $-q^{-1}$ (antisymmetric/fermionic channel) correspond to the two OPE channels of the vertex algebra.*

***(QU-1b) Yang–Baxter relation** (braid relation):*

*$$T_i\, T_{i+1}\, T_i
  \;=\;
  T_{i+1}\, T_i\, T_{i+1}
  \qquad (1 \leq i \leq n-2).$$*

*This is the hexagon axiom of the braided monoidal category, expressed in the Hecke basis.*

***(QU-1c) Far-commutativity**:*

*$$T_i\, T_j \;=\; T_j\, T_i
  \qquad (|i - j| \geq 2).$$*

*Strands that do not share a crossing commute: locality of the vertex algebra OPE.*

***(QU-1d) Snake identities** (rigidity):*

*The cup $\cup\colon \mathbf{1} \to V^{\vee} \otimes V$ and cap $\cap\colon V \otimes V^{\vee} \to \mathbf{1}$ satisfy:*

*$$(\cap \otimes \mathrm{id}_V) \circ
  (\mathrm{id}_V \otimes \cup)
  \;=\; \mathrm{id}_V,$$*

*$$(\mathrm{id}_{V^{\vee}} \otimes \cap) \circ
  (\cup \otimes \mathrm{id}_{V^{\vee}})
  \;=\; \mathrm{id}_{V^{\vee}}.$$*

*In the graphical calculus these are the zig-zag straightenings. In knot coordinates, $\cup$ and $\cap$ are the Markov-trace cup/cap insertions: the contour-integral endpoints of $Y(a, z)$ around the Reeb fibre.*

### QU-2: Frobenius–Hopf relations

*The multiplication $\mu$, comultiplication $\Delta$, unit $\eta$, counit $\varepsilon$, antipode $S$, and Frobenius form $\int_A$ become operations on braid closures:*

***(QU-2a) Associativity**:*

*$$\mu \circ (\mu \otimes \mathrm{id})
  \;=\;
  \mu \circ (\mathrm{id} \otimes \mu)
  \colon A^{\otimes 3} \to A.$$*

*In knot coordinates: merging three strands is independent of grouping. For braid words $\beta_1, \beta_2, \beta_3$:*

*$$\mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(
    \rho(\beta_1 \cdot \beta_2) \cdot \rho(\beta_3)
  \bigr)
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(
    \rho(\beta_1) \cdot \rho(\beta_2 \cdot \beta_3)
  \bigr).$$*

***(QU-2b) Frobenius relation** (sliding):*

*$$(\mu \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ
  (\mathrm{id} \otimes \Delta)
  \;=\;
  \Delta \circ \mu
  \;=\;
  (\mathrm{id} \otimes \mu) \circ
  (\Delta \otimes \mathrm{id}).$$*

*In knot coordinates this is the **saddle-point relation**: a strand merge followed by a split equals a split followed by a merge. Graphically, this is the genus-$0$ cobordism identity — a pair of pants composed either way gives the same surface.*

***(QU-2c) Non-degenerate Frobenius pairing** ($A \cong A^{\vee}$):*

*The Frobenius pairing $\int_A \circ \mu\colon A \otimes A \to \mathbf{1}$ is the **Markov trace of the product**:*

*$$\langle a, b \rangle_F
  \;=\;
  \int_A \mu(a \otimes b)
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(\rho(\hat{\beta}_a \cdot \hat{\beta}_b)\bigr),$$*

*where $\hat{\beta}_a$ is the braid word representing state $a$. Non-degeneracy means: for every nonzero braid word $\beta$, there exists $\beta'$ such that $\mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\beta \cdot \beta')) \neq 0$.*

***(QU-2d) Hopf (antipode) relation**:*

*$$\mu \circ (S \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ \Delta
  \;=\;
  \eta \circ \varepsilon
  \;=\;
  \mu \circ (\mathrm{id} \otimes S) \circ \Delta.$$*

*In knot coordinates, the antipode $S$ is the **braid reversal** (orientation reversal of all crossings):*

*$$S(T_i) \;=\; T_i^{-1}
  \;=\; T_i - (q - q^{-1})
  \qquad\text{(from the Hecke relation)}.$$*

*The Hopf relation then reads: closing a braid word against its reverse yields the unknot (vacuum):*

*$$\mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(
    \rho(\beta) \cdot \rho(\beta^{-1})
  \bigr)
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{tr}_M(1)
  \;=\;
  J_{0_1}(q).$$*

***(QU-2e) Coassociativity and counit**:*

*$$(\Delta \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ \Delta
  \;=\;
  (\mathrm{id} \otimes \Delta) \circ \Delta,
  \qquad
  (\varepsilon \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ \Delta
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{id}
  \;=\;
  (\mathrm{id} \otimes \varepsilon) \circ \Delta.$$*

*In knot coordinates: splitting a strand into three is independent of grouping, and the counit (trace evaluation at the unknot) acts as a unit for splitting.*

### QU-3: Fibre functor (Markov trace)

*The fibre functor $\tau\colon \mathbf{C} \to R\text{-Mod}$ realises as the Jones–Markov trace ([Jones–Markov trace](#thm:jones-markov-trace)). Its defining relation on Hecke generators is:*

***(QU-3a) Markov property I** (conjugation invariance):*

*$$\mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(T_i \cdot w\bigr)
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(w \cdot T_i\bigr)
  \qquad \forall\, w \in H_n(q).$$*

***(QU-3b) Markov property II** (stabilisation):*

*$$\mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(w \cdot T_n^{\pm 1}\bigr)
  \;=\;
  \frac{1}{\delta}\;\mathrm{tr}_M(w)
  \qquad \text{for } w \in H_n(q) \subset H_{n+1}(q),$$*

*where $\delta = -(q + q^{-1})$ is the writhe normalisation.*

***(QU-3c) Faithfulness**:*

*$$\mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(\rho(\beta)\bigr) = 0
  \;\;\forall\, \beta \in B_n
  \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
  \rho(\beta) = 0 \;\text{in } H_n(q).$$*

*The fibre functor detects every nonzero morphism — equivalently, the Jones polynomial separates knots (modulo the open Jones conjecture for the full category; for torus knots this is a theorem \\}cite{jones1987}).*

### QU-4: Differential calculus (translation operator)

*The Kähler differentials $\Omega^1(A)$ in the vertex algebra are generated by the **translation operator** $L_{-1} = j$ (jet prolongation):*

***(QU-4a) Translation relation**:*

*$$[L_{-1},\, Y(a, z)]
  \;=\;
  \partial_z Y(a, z)
  \;=\;
  Y(L_{-1}\, a,\, z).$$*

*In Hecke generators, the mode expansion gives:*

*$$[L_{-1},\, a_m] \;=\; -m\, a_{m-1},$$*

*where $a_m = \mathrm{tr}_M(\check{R}_{(a)}\, z^m)$ is the $m$-th mode of the vertex operator.*

***(QU-4b) Vacuum axiom**:*

*$$Y(|0\rangle, z) \;=\; \mathrm{id}_V, \qquad
  L_{-1}\,|0\rangle \;=\; 0.$$*

*The unknot ($|0\rangle = 1 \in A_0$) produces the identity operator; translation annihilates the vacuum.*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## QUO Axioms (Observable Universe)

### QUO-1: Non-degenerate integration

*The Frobenius form $\int_A$ induces $A \cong A^{\vee}$. In knot coordinates this sharpens QU-2c:*

*$$\mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(\rho(\beta) \cdot \rho(\beta')\bigr)
  \;=\; 0
  \;\;\forall\, \beta'
  \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
  \beta = \varnothing \;\text{(empty braid)}.$$*

*Equivalently, the Gram matrix $G_{ij} = \mathrm{tr}_M(T_{\beta_i} \cdot T_{\beta_j})$ over any normal-form basis $\{T_{\beta_i}\}$ of $H_n(q)$ is invertible.*

### QUO-2: Observability ($\mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0$)

*There is no braid word invariant under the adjoint (conjugation) action. In Hecke generators:*

*$$T_i\, w\, T_i^{-1} \;=\; w
  \quad \forall\, i
  \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
  w \in R \cdot 1
  \;\text{(scalar multiple of the identity)}.$$*

*Equivalently: the only braid word commuting with all generators is the identity. In the vertex algebra, this means there is no nontrivial state $a \in V$ with $Y(a, z) = \lambda\,\mathrm{id}$ for all $z$ — every state produces a genuinely $z$-dependent operator.*

### QUO-3: Measurability (anomaly freedom)

*The Chern classes $c_1(\mathrm{Ad}(A)) = c_2(\mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0$ translate via the fibre functor to:*

***(QUO-3a) First Chern class vanishing** ($c_1 = 0$):*

*$$\sum_{i=1}^{n-1}
  \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(
    T_i - T_i^{-1}
  \bigr)
  \;=\; 0.$$*

*This is the total writhe of the adjoint representation being zero — the adjoint bundle is orientable.*

***(QUO-3b) Second Chern class vanishing** ($c_2 = 0$):*

*$$\sum_{i < j}
  \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(
    [T_i, T_j]\,[T_i, T_j]^{\dagger}
  \bigr)
  \;=\; 0,$$*

*where $[T_i, T_j] = T_i T_j - T_j T_i$ and $\dagger$ is the anti-involution $T_i^{\dagger} = T_i^{-1}$. This ensures no topological phases accumulate under transport around the adjoint bundle.*

### QUO-4: Categorical volume constraint

*The exterior power $\Lambda^2 V$ maps onto $\mathbf{1}$ via a non-degenerate epimorphism $\epsilon$ preserved by gauge automorphisms. The antisymmetriser in $H_2(q)$ is:*

*$$\mathrm{Alt}_2
  \;=\;
  \frac{1}{[2]_q}\bigl(\mathrm{id} - q^{-1}\, T_1\bigr),
  \qquad
  [2]_q = q + q^{-1}.$$*

*The volume constraint is:*

*$$\epsilon \circ \mathrm{Alt}_2
  \;=\;
  \epsilon
  \colon V^{\otimes 2} \to \mathbf{1},$$*

*and for every gauge automorphism $g \in \mathrm{Aut}^{\otimes}(\tau)$:*

*$$\epsilon \circ (\Lambda^2 g_V) \;=\; \epsilon.$$*

*In Hecke generators, this becomes: the antisymmetric contraction $\epsilon$ satisfies*

*$$\epsilon\!\bigl(v \otimes w - q^{-1}\,(T_1 \cdot v \otimes w)\bigr)
  \;=\;
  [2]_q\;\epsilon(v \otimes w)$$*

*and is gauge-invariant, fixing the $q$-deformed volume element.*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Cohomological Constraints in Knot Coordinates

*The QU/QUO axioms imply a suite of cohomological constraints. Each translates into a relation on braid words, Hecke generators, and the Markov trace.*

### C-1: De Rham complex ($d^2 = 0$ on horizontal forms)

*The de Rham differential $d\colon \Omega^k(A) \to \Omega^{k+1}(A)$ acts on modes via $d(a_m\, z^{-m-1}\, dz) = a_{m-1}\, z^{-m}\, dz$. In knot coordinates, the nilpotence $d^2 = 0$ on the horizontal subcomplex $\Omega_H^k(A)$ reads:*

*$$\mathrm{tr}_M\!\Bigl(
    \check{R}_{(a)}\, z^{m-2}
  \Bigr)
  \;-\;
  2\,\mathrm{tr}_M\!\Bigl(
    \check{R}_{(a)}\, z^{m-1}
  \Bigr)
  \;+\;
  \mathrm{tr}_M\!\Bigl(
    \check{R}_{(a)}\, z^{m}
  \Bigr)
  \;=\; 0$$*

*for all $\xi$-invariant states $a$ (those annihilated by the weight operator: $[\xi, a] = 0$, i.e.\\} braid words in the centre of $H_n(q)$).*

### C-2: $q$-Deformed obstruction to nilpotence ($d_q^2 \neq 0$)

*The $q$-exterior derivative $d_q = q^{-1}d + (1 - q^{-1})\pi_V \circ d$ satisfies ([categorical $d_q^2$](#prop:categorical-dq-squared)):*

*$$d_q^2\,\alpha
  \;=\;
  q^{-1}(1 - q^{-1})\;\omega_V \wedge_q [\xi,\, \alpha].$$*

*In knot coordinates, the weight operator $\xi$ acts on modes as the writhe grading:*

*$$[\xi,\, a_m]
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{wr}(a)\, a_m,
  \qquad
  \mathrm{wr}(a) = \sum_i \mathrm{tr}_M(T_i - T_i^{-1})
  \;\text{(writhe of $\hat{\beta}_a$)}.$$*

*The curvature 2-form $\omega_V$ is the Hecke Casimir:*

*$$\omega_V
  \;=\;
  \sum_{i < j}
  (T_i\, T_j - T_j\, T_i)\, dz^i \wedge dz^j.$$*

*So $d_q^2 = 0$ if and only if $q = 1$ (classical limit) or $\mathrm{wr}(\alpha) = 0$ (zero writhe, horizontal forms). For generic $q \neq 1$ and non-horizontal $\alpha$, $d_q^2 \neq 0$: the $q$-deformed complex is **not** a cochain complex, and the obstruction is measured by writhe $\times$ curvature.*

### C-3: Hodge star and Poincar’e duality

*The categorical Hodge star ([categorical Hodge star](#def:categorical-hodge-star)) $\star\colon \Omega^k(A) \to \Omega^{n-k}(A)$ satisfies $\star^2 = \mathrm{id}$. In knot coordinates, $\star$ acts on modes via the antipode:*

*$$\star(a_m)
  \;=\;
  S(a_m)^*
  \;=\;
  (T_i^{-1})_m^*
  \qquad\text{where } (\cdot)^* \text{ is Frobenius conjugation.}$$*

***Poincar’e duality** in knot coordinates: for all braid words $\beta, \beta'$,*

*$$\mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(
    \rho(\beta) \cdot \star\,\rho(\beta')
  \bigr)
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(
    \rho(\beta) \cdot S(\rho(\beta'))^*
  \bigr)
  \;=\;
  \delta_{\beta,\, \beta'}\;\mathrm{vol},$$*

*where $\mathrm{vol} = \int_A(\mathrm{vol}) = 1$ normalises the top form. The pairing is non-degenerate by QUO-1.*

### C-4: Euler characteristic constraint

*The categorical Euler characteristic $\chi(A) = \mathrm{tr}(\mathrm{id}_A)$ is the rigidity trace. In knot coordinates this is the Jones polynomial of the unknot at strand count $n$:*

*$$\chi(A)
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{tr}_M(\mathrm{id}_{H_n(q)})
  \;=\;
  [n]_q!
  \;=\;
  \prod_{k=1}^{n} \frac{q^k - q^{-k}}{q - q^{-1}}.$$*

***Stability under jet prolongation** (C-4a):*

*$$\mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(\mathrm{id}_{J^1 H_n(q)}\bigr)
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(\mathrm{id}_{H_n(q)}\bigr).$$*

*The translation operator $L_{-1}$ preserves the Euler characteristic: $\chi(A_{n+1}) = \chi(A_n)$ for all brane levels.*

***Descartes constraint** (C-4b): For the physical universe,*

*$$\chi(A) \;=\; -6
  \qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad
  \mathrm{tr}_M(\mathrm{id}) \;=\; -6.$$*

*This forces genus $g = 4$ (Bring’s surface), bounding the embeddable torus knots to the 7 generators $\mathcal{G}$.*

### C-5: Yekutieli obstruction classes

*The quantum characteristic classes $\kappa_n \in H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathcal{B})$ ([quantum characteristic classes](#def:quantum-characteristic-classes)) obstruct lifting from brane level $n$ to $n+1$. In knot variables, the obstruction is detected by the failure of Markov stabilisation at the jet level:*

*$$\kappa_n
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(
    \check{R}_{(n+1)} - L_{-1}\, \check{R}_{(n)}
  \bigr)
  \;\in\;
  H^2(\mathcal{S}_p,\, \mathcal{B}),$$*

*where $\check{R}_{(n)}$ is the $R$-matrix at brane level $n$. The class $\kappa_n = 0$ iff the level-$(n+1)$ braiding is entirely determined by the level-$n$ braiding via jet prolongation.*

***Perpetual obstruction** (C-5a): When $\chi(A) = -6$,*

*$$\kappa_n \;\neq\; 0
  \qquad \forall\, n \geq 0.$$*

*In Hecke generators: at every brane level, there exist braid words $\beta_{n+1} \in H_{n+1}(q)$ that cannot be written as $L_{-1}(\beta_n)$ for any $\beta_n \in H_n(q)$. The jet corrections and the base obstruction live in complementary subgroups, so cancellation is impossible.*

### C-6: Betti numbers and spectral sequence

*The Betti numbers $b_k = \dim H^k(\mathcal{S}_n, \mathbb{R})$ are controlled by the Leray–Serre spectral sequence. In knot variables, $b_k$ counts linearly independent $k$-fold products of Hecke generators modulo the de Rham relation:*

*$$b_k(\mathcal{S}_n)
  \;=\;
  \dim_R\,
  \frac{
    \ker\!\bigl(d\colon \Omega^k_{H_n(q)} \to \Omega^{k+1}_{H_n(q)}\bigr)
  }{
    \mathrm{im}\!\bigl(d\colon \Omega^{k-1}_{H_n(q)} \to \Omega^k_{H_n(q)}\bigr)
  },$$*

*where $\Omega^k_{H_n(q)}$ is the space of degree-$k$ antisymmetric Hecke words:*

*$$\Omega^k_{H_n(q)}
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{span}\!\bigl\{
    T_{i_1} T_{i_2} \cdots T_{i_k}
    \;\big|\;
    i_1 < i_2 < \cdots < i_k
  \bigr\} \cdot \mathrm{Alt}_k,$$*

*with $\mathrm{Alt}_k = \sum_{\pi \in S_k} \mathrm{sgn}(\pi)\, q^{-\ell(\pi)}\, T_\pi$ the $q$-antisymmetriser.*

***Euler check**: $\chi = \sum_k (-1)^k b_k = -6$ reproduces C-4b.*

### C-7: Instanton constraint (self-dual curvature)

*The categorical instanton condition $\star_q F_\nabla = F_\nabla$ ([instanton on-shell](#rem:instanton-on-shell)) becomes a relation on the curvature 2-form in Hecke generators. The curvature $F_\nabla = \nabla^2$ has components:*

*$$(F_\nabla)_{ij}
  \;=\;
  [T_i,\, T_j]
  \;+\;
  \sum_k f^k_{ij}\, T_k,$$*

*where $f^k_{ij}$ are the structure constants of the Hecke algebra. The self-duality equation is:*

*$$\star_q\, (F_\nabla)_{ij}
  \;=\;
  (F_\nabla)_{ij}
  \qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad
  S\!\bigl([T_i, T_j]\bigr)^*
  \;=\;
  [T_i, T_j].$$*

*That is, the curvature is invariant under the combined antipode-conjugation — it is **self-adjoint** in the Frobenius inner product.*

***Bogomolny bound** (C-7a): The instanton number equals $c_2(A)$:*

*$$\lVert F_\nabla \rVert^2
  \;=\;
  \sum_{i < j}
  \mathrm{tr}_M\!\bigl(
    [T_i, T_j] \cdot [T_i, T_j]^{\dagger}
  \bigr)
  \;=\;
  c_2(A).$$*

*By QUO-3b this vanishes for the adjoint — the adjoint bundle is flat. For the fundamental representation, $c_2(A)$ is the **topological charge** (knot crossing number modulo signs).*

### C-8: Hodge–Laplacian and harmonic braid words

*The $q$-Laplacian $\Delta_q = d_q\, \delta_q + \delta_q\, d_q$ ([Hodge–Laplacian](#rem:hodge-laplacian-relation)) is self-adjoint. In knot coordinates:*

*$$\Delta_q
  \;=\;
  q^{-2}\,\Delta
  \;+\;
  q^{-1}(1 - q^{-1})\bigl(
    \omega_V \wedge_q \iota_\xi
    \;+\;
    \iota_\xi\, \omega_V \wedge_q
  \bigr),$$*

*where $\Delta = d\delta + \delta d$ is the undeformed Laplacian and $\iota_\xi$ is contraction with the weight vector.*

***Harmonic states** are braid words $\beta$ satisfying $\Delta_q\, \rho(\beta) = 0$. In Hecke generators:*

*$$\Delta_q\, T_\beta = 0
  \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
  d_q\,T_\beta = 0
  \;\;\text{and}\;\;
  \delta_q\, T_\beta = 0.$$*

*The space $\ker \Delta_q$ is the **particle Hilbert space** — its dimension equals the number of linearly independent knot-particles at each brane level.*

### C-9: Cohomological embedding (knot basis for $H^*$)

*The cohomology of the moduli surface $\Sigma_g$ ([cohomological embedding](#prop:cohomological-embedding)) admits a knot basis. In knot coordinates, each cohomology generator is a specific Hecke word:*

*$$H^*(\Sigma_4)
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{span}\!\bigl\{
    1,\;
    T_{(2,3)},\;
    T_{(2,5)},\;
    T_{(2,7)},\;
    T_{(3,5)},\;
    T_{(2,9)},\;
    T_{(3,4)},\;
    T_{(4_1)},\;
    T_{(4_1)}^*,\;
    \mathrm{vol}
  \bigr\},$$*

*where $T_{(m,n)} = \mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\sigma^{(m,n)}))$ denotes the Markov-trace evaluation of the torus knot braid word $\sigma^{(m,n)} \in B_m$.*

***Hodge decomposition in Hecke generators**:*

| *$H^p(\Sigma_4)$* | *dim* | *Hecke generators*                                          |
|:-----------------:|:-----:|:------------------------------------------------------------|
|      *$H^0$*      | *$1$* | *$1$ (empty braid = photon)*                                |
|    *$H^{1,0}$*    | *$4$* | *$T_{(2,3)},\; T_{(2,5)},\; T_{(2,7)},\; T_{(3,5)}$*        |
|    *$H^{0,1}$*    | *$4$* | *$T_{(2,9)},\; T_{(3,4)},\; T_{(4_1)},\; T_{(4_1)}^*$*      |
|      *$H^2$*      | *$1$* | *$\mathrm{vol} = \epsilon \circ \mathrm{Alt}_2$ (neutrino)* |

***Completeness**: the $6 \times 5$ character matrix $M_{ij} = \chi_{\lambda_j}(T_{(r_i, s_i)})$ over irreps $\lambda \vdash r$ of $H_2(q) \oplus H_3(q)$ has rank $5$. Every knot observable on $\Sigma_4$ is a linear combination of evaluations of the $6$ torus-knot Hecke words.*

### C-10: \\}v{C}ech–Yekutieli descent cocycle

*The cosimplicial crossed groupoid structure on the brane tower gives a \\}v{C}ech cocycle condition at each level. In knot variables, the twisted 2-cocycle reads:*

*$$d\!\bigl(g^{(n)}_{ijk}\bigr)
  \;=\;
  a^{(n)}_{ij} \cdot g^{(n)}_{ijk} \cdot
  \bigl(a^{(n)}_{jk}\bigr)^{-1},$$*

*where $g^{(n)}_{ijk} \in H_n(q)$ is the transition braid word on triple overlaps and $a^{(n)}_{ij}$ are 2-morphism braid words. In Hecke generators, the cocycle condition becomes:*

*$$T_{g_{ijk}} \cdot T_{g_{jkl}}
  \;=\;
  T_{a_{ij}} \cdot T_{g_{ikl}} \cdot T_{a_{kl}}^{-1}
  \qquad\text{(in $H_n(q)$)},$$*

*where $T_g = \rho(g)$ denotes the Hecke image of a braid word. This is the gluing condition for locally defined braid words to patch into a global knot invariant.*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Summary: complete presentation

*The vertex operator algebra of a QUO is the quotient of the free algebra on generators $\{T_i, \cup, \cap, L_{-1}, \mathrm{tr}_M, d, d_q, \star\}$ by the relations:*

***Structural relations (QU/QUO axioms)**:*

| *Label*  | *Relation*                                                     | *Axiom*            |
|:---------|:---------------------------------------------------------------|:-------------------|
| *QU-1a*  | *$T_i^2 = (q - q^{-1})T_i + 1$*                                | *Hecke (braiding)* |
| *QU-1b*  | *$T_i T_{i+1} T_i = T_{i+1} T_i T_{i+1}$*                      | *Yang–Baxter*      |
| *QU-1c*  | *$T_i T_j = T_j T_i$ ($\lvert i-j\rvert \geq 2$)*              | *Locality*         |
| *QU-1d*  | *$(\cap \otimes 1)(1 \otimes \cup) = \mathrm{id}$*             | *Rigidity*         |
| *QU-2b*  | *$(\mu \otimes 1)(1 \otimes \Delta) = \Delta \circ \mu$*       | *Frobenius*        |
| *QU-2d*  | *$\mu(S \otimes 1)\Delta = \eta\varepsilon$*                   | *Antipode*         |
| *QU-3a*  | *$\mathrm{tr}_M(T_i w) = \mathrm{tr}_M(w T_i)$*                | *Markov I*         |
| *QU-3b*  | *$\mathrm{tr}_M(w T_n^{\pm 1}) = \delta^{-1}\mathrm{tr}_M(w)$* | *Markov II*        |
| *QU-4a*  | *$[L_{-1}, a_m] = -m\,a_{m-1}$*                                | *Translation*      |
| *QUO-1*  | *$\det G_{ij} \neq 0$*                                         | *Non-degeneracy*   |
| *QUO-2*  | *$T_i w T_i^{-1} = w\;\forall i \Rightarrow w \in R$*          | *Observability*    |
| *QUO-3a* | *$\sum_i \mathrm{tr}_M(T_i - T_i^{-1}) = 0$*                   | *$c_1 = 0$*        |
| *QUO-3b* | *$\sum_{i<j} \mathrm{tr}_M([T_i,T_j][T_i,T_j]^{\dagger}) = 0$* | *$c_2 = 0$*        |
| *QUO-4*  | *$\epsilon \circ \Lambda^2 g_V = \epsilon$*                    | *Volume*           |

***Cohomological relations**:*

| *Label* | *Relation*                                                                     | *Constraint*            |
|:--------|:-------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:------------------------|
| *C-1*   | *$d^2 = 0$ on $\ker[\xi, \cdot]$*                                              | *De Rham nilpotence*    |
| *C-2*   | *$d_q^2\alpha = q^{-1}(1-q^{-1})\omega_V\wedge_q[\xi,\alpha]$*                 | *$q$-obstruction*       |
| *C-3*   | *$\mathrm{tr}_M(\rho(\beta)\cdot S(\rho(\beta'))^*) = \delta_{\beta\beta'}$*   | *Poincar’e duality*     |
| *C-4a*  | *$\chi(A_{n+1}) = \chi(A_n)$*                                                  | *Euler stability*       |
| *C-4b*  | *$\mathrm{tr}_M(\mathrm{id}) = -6$*                                            | *Descartes*             |
| *C-5*   | *$\kappa_n = \mathrm{tr}_M(\check{R}_{(n+1)} - L_{-1}\check{R}_{(n)}) \neq 0$* | *Perpetual obstruction* |
| *C-6*   | *$b_k = \dim(\ker d / \mathrm{im}\, d)$ on $\mathrm{Alt}_k \cdot H_n(q)$*      | *Betti numbers*         |
| *C-7*   | *$S([T_i,T_j])^* = [T_i,T_j]$*                                                 | *Self-dual curvature*   |
| *C-7a*  | *$\sum_{i<j}\mathrm{tr}_M([T_i,T_j][T_i,T_j]^\dagger) = c_2(A)$*               | *Bogomolny bound*       |
| *C-8*   | *$\Delta_q T_\beta = 0 \Leftrightarrow d_q T_\beta = \delta_q T_\beta = 0$*    | *Harmonic braids*       |
| *C-9*   | *$\mathrm{rank}\, M_{ij} = 5$ on $\Sigma_4$*                                   | *Completeness*          |
| *C-10*  | *$T_{g_{ijk}}T_{g_{jkl}} = T_{a_{ij}}T_{g_{ikl}}T_{a_{kl}}^{-1}$*              | *\\}v{C}ech cocycle*    |

*These **26 relations** (14 structural + 12 cohomological), together with the Hecke–Skein dictionary $T \leftrightarrow L_+$, $T^{-1} \leftrightarrow L_-$, $1 \leftrightarrow L_0$, constitute a complete presentation of the QOU vertex algebra in knot coordinates — encoding both algebraic structure and cohomological topology in the single language of braid words and the Markov trace.*
