<div id="prop:vertex-algebra-jet-relations" class="proposition">

**Proposition 4.34** (QU/QUO and cohomological relations on the jet bundle). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.VertexAlgebra.JetRelations.euler_level_stable)*

*Every relation in the QU/QUO presentation ([vertex algebra relations](#prop:vertex-algebra-relations)) lifts to the jet bundle $J^n(A) = A_n$ via the brane tower ([recursive brane tower](#def:recursive-brane-tower)). The jet prolongation $L_{-1}\colon A_n \to A_{n+1}$ promotes each level-$n$ Hecke algebra $H^{(n)}(q)$ to a level-$(n{+}1)$ Hecke algebra $H^{(n+1)}(q)$, and the descent involution $\hat{\tau}_n = \ell_n \circ \mathfrak{d}_{n+1}$ splits the level-$(n{+}1)$ relations into **descended** (inherited from level $n$) and **transient** (genuinely new at level $n{+}1$).*

*Write $T_i^{(n)}$ for the Hecke generators at brane level $n$, $\mathrm{tr}_M^{(n)}$ for the level-$n$ Markov trace, and $\check{R}^{(n)}$ for the $R$-matrix at level $n$. The jet embedding is $\ell_n\colon H^{(n)}(q) \hookrightarrow H^{(n+1)}(q)$ with $\ell_n(T_i^{(n)}) = T_i^{(n+1)}$, and the descent is $\mathfrak{d}_{n+1}\colon H^{(n+1)}(q) \to H^{(n)}(q)$ with $\mathfrak{d}_{n+1} \circ \ell_n = \mathrm{id}$.*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## I. Structural relations on $J^n(A)$

### J-1: Hecke relations (level $n$)

*The Hecke generators at every brane level satisfy the same quadratic, braid, and locality relations:*

***(J-1a)** $\;T_i^{(n)\,2} \;=\; (q - q^{-1})\,T_i^{(n)} + 1$*

***(J-1b)** $\;T_i^{(n)}\, T_{i+1}^{(n)}\, T_i^{(n)} \;=\; T_{i+1}^{(n)}\, T_i^{(n)}\, T_{i+1}^{(n)}$*

***(J-1c)** $\;T_i^{(n)}\, T_j^{(n)} \;=\; T_j^{(n)}\, T_i^{(n)} \qquad (|i - j| \geq 2)$*

*The substrate parameter $q$ is the **same at every level** — this is the content of the Euler characteristic stability $\chi(A_n) = \chi(A_0)$.*

### J-2: Jet-prolonged Frobenius–Hopf relations

*The multiplication $\mu_n$, comultiplication $\Delta_n$, and antipode $S_n$ on $A_n$ are inherited from $A_0$ by jet prolongation. The Frobenius relation lifts level by level:*

***(J-2a) Frobenius sliding at level $n$**:*

*$$(\mu_n \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ
  (\mathrm{id} \otimes \Delta_n)
  \;=\;
  \Delta_n \circ \mu_n.$$*

*In knot coordinates:*

*$$\mathrm{tr}_M^{(n)}\!\bigl(
    \rho_n(\beta_1) \cdot \rho_n(\beta_2 \cdot \beta_3)
  \bigr)
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{tr}_M^{(n)}\!\bigl(
    \rho_n(\beta_1 \cdot \beta_2) \cdot \rho_n(\beta_3)
  \bigr).$$*

***(J-2b) Antipode at level $n$**: $\;S_n(T_i^{(n)}) = T_i^{(n)\,-1} = T_i^{(n)} - (q - q^{-1})$.*

***(J-2c) Level-$n$ Frobenius pairing**:*

*$$\langle a, b \rangle_n
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{tr}_M^{(n)}\!\bigl(
    \rho_n(\hat{\beta}_a \cdot \hat{\beta}_b)
  \bigr).$$*

*Non-degeneracy: $\det G^{(n)}_{ij} \neq 0$ at every brane level.*

### J-3: Markov trace at level $n$

***(J-3a) Conjugation invariance**:*

*$$\mathrm{tr}_M^{(n)}(T_i^{(n)} \cdot w)
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{tr}_M^{(n)}(w \cdot T_i^{(n)})
  \qquad \forall\, w \in H^{(n)}(q).$$*

***(J-3b) Stabilisation**:*

*$$\mathrm{tr}_M^{(n)}(w \cdot T_m^{(n)\,\pm 1})
  \;=\;
  \frac{1}{\delta}\;\mathrm{tr}_M^{(n)}(w),
  \qquad
  \delta = -(q + q^{-1}).$$*

***(J-3c) Inter-level compatibility** (jet prolongation preserves the Markov trace):*

*$$\mathrm{tr}_M^{(n+1)}\!\bigl(\ell_n(w)\bigr)
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{tr}_M^{(n)}(w)
  \qquad \forall\, w \in H^{(n)}(q).$$*

*This is the knot-variable form of Euler stability: the Jones polynomial of a knot is independent of brane level.*

### J-4: Translation operator between levels

***(J-4a) Mode relation across levels**:*

*$$[L_{-1},\, a_m^{(n)}] \;=\; -m\, a_{m-1}^{(n+1)},$$*

*where $a_m^{(n)} = \mathrm{tr}_M^{(n)}(\check{R}^{(n)}_{(a)}\, z^m)$ is the $m$-th mode at level $n$. The commutator maps level-$n$ modes to level-$(n{+}1)$ modes — the translation operator is the **inter-level ladder**.*

***(J-4b) Vacuum stability across levels**:*

*$$|0\rangle^{(n)} \;=\; \ell_{n-1} \circ \cdots \circ \ell_0\,(|0\rangle)
  \;=\; 1 \in A_n.$$*

*The unknot embeds identically at every level.*

### J-5: Observability at level $n$

*$$T_i^{(n)}\, w\, T_i^{(n)\,-1} = w
  \;\;\forall\, i
  \quad\Longrightarrow\quad
  w \in R \cdot 1 \;\;\text{in } H^{(n)}(q).$$*

*The vanishing of $\mathrm{Hom}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A_n))$ propagates from level $0$ by the jet prolongation proof: any $\mathrm{Ad}$-invariant at level $n{+}1$ projects to one at level $n$, contradicting the base case.*

### J-6: Volume constraint at level $n$

*$$\epsilon_n \circ \mathrm{Alt}_2^{(n)} \;=\; \epsilon_n,
  \qquad
  \epsilon_n \circ (\Lambda^2 g_V^{(n)}) = \epsilon_n.$$*

*The $q$-antisymmetriser $\mathrm{Alt}_2^{(n)} = \frac{1}{[2]_q}(\mathrm{id} - q^{-1} T_1^{(n)})$ has the same form at every level (same $q$), so the volume constraint is **level-independent**.*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## II. Descent decomposition of relations

*The descent involution $\hat{\tau}_n = \ell_n \circ \mathfrak{d}_{n+1}$ is idempotent on $H^{(n+1)}(q)$ and splits every relation into descended and transient parts.*

### D-1: Descended Hecke generators

*$$\hat{\tau}_n(T_i^{(n+1)})
  \;=\;
  \ell_n\!\bigl(\mathfrak{d}_{n+1}(T_i^{(n+1)})\bigr)
  \;=\;
  \ell_n(T_i^{(n)})
  \;=\;
  T_i^{(n+1)}.$$*

*For $i \leq n-1$: the base Hecke generators are **entirely descended** — they are the same crossing at every level. The Hecke relation QU-1a is purely descended.*

### D-2: Transient generators

*At level $n{+}1$, the jet prolongation may produce new generators $T^{(n+1)}_{\mathrm{new}}$ in the transient complement $\mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{trans}}_{n+1} = \ker\,\hat{\tau}_n$. These satisfy:*

*$$\hat{\tau}_n(T^{(n+1)}_{\mathrm{new}}) \;=\; 0,
  \qquad
  \mathfrak{d}_{n+1}(T^{(n+1)}_{\mathrm{new}}) \;=\; 0.$$*

*Transient generators have no pre-image at level $n$. They still satisfy the Hecke relation (J-1a) at level $n{+}1$ but their Markov traces are **invisible at level $n$**:*

*$$\mathrm{tr}_M^{(n)}\!\bigl(
    \mathfrak{d}_{n+1}(T^{(n+1)}_{\mathrm{new}})
  \bigr)
  \;=\; 0.$$*

### D-3: Descent of the Frobenius relation

*The Frobenius sliding relation (J-2a) splits as:*

*$$\Delta_n \circ \mu_n
  \;=\;
  \underbrace{
    \hat{\tau}_n(\Delta_{n+1} \circ \mu_{n+1})
  }_{\text{descended (from level $n$)}}
  \;+\;
  \underbrace{
    (1 - \hat{\tau}_n)(\Delta_{n+1} \circ \mu_{n+1})
  }_{\text{transient correction}}.$$*

*The transient correction encodes the **jet curvature**: the failure of the level-$(n{+}1)$ Frobenius relation to be entirely determined by level $n$.*

### D-4: Bosonic vs fermionic modes

*The descent eigenspaces ([descent eigenspaces](#prop:descent-eigenspaces)) separate modes by statistics:*

- ***Bosonic (longitudinal)**: $w \in \mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{desc}}_{n+1}$ satisfies $\hat{\tau}_n(w) = w$. In knot coordinates: braid words whose Markov trace is fully determined at level $n$:*

*$$\mathrm{tr}_M^{(n+1)}(w) \;=\; \mathrm{tr}_M^{(n)}(\mathfrak{d}_{n+1}(w)).$$*

- ***Fermionic (ladder)**: $w \in \mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{trans}}_{n+1}$ satisfies $\hat{\tau}_n(w) = 0$. In knot coordinates: braid words whose Markov trace vanishes when descended:*

*$$\mathrm{tr}_M^{(n)}(\mathfrak{d}_{n+1}(w)) \;=\; 0.$$*

*Fermionic modes are the jet-created braid words with no analogue at the previous level.*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## III. Cohomological relations on $J^n(A)$

### JC-1: De Rham complex at level $n$

*$$d_n^2 \;=\; 0
  \qquad\text{on } \Omega^k_H(A_n),$$*

*where $\Omega^k_H(A_n)$ is the horizontal subcomplex at level $n$ (braid words with zero writhe at level $n$).*

### JC-2: $q$-Obstruction at level $n$

*$$d_{q,n}^2\,\alpha
  \;=\;
  q^{-1}(1 - q^{-1})\;\omega_V^{(n)} \wedge_q [\xi_n,\, \alpha],$$*

*where $\omega_V^{(n)} = \sum_{i<j}(T_i^{(n)} T_j^{(n)} - T_j^{(n)} T_i^{(n)})\,dz^i \wedge dz^j$ is the level-$n$ Hecke Casimir. Since $q$ is level-independent, the obstruction to $d_q^2 = 0$ has the **same algebraic form** at every level — but acts on a larger algebra.*

### JC-3: Euler characteristic stability

*$$\chi(A_n)
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{tr}_M^{(n)}(\mathrm{id}_{H^{(n)}(q)})
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{tr}_M^{(0)}(\mathrm{id}_{H^{(0)}(q)})
  \;=\;
  \chi(A_0)
  \;=\; -6.$$*

*The rigidity trace of the identity is level-invariant. In Hecke generators: the quantum factorial $[n]_q!$ at the base strand count is preserved by jet prolongation.*

### JC-4: Yekutieli obstruction at level $n$

*$$\kappa_n
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{tr}_M^{(n+1)}\!\bigl(
    \check{R}^{(n+1)} - \ell_n(\check{R}^{(n)})
  \bigr)
  \;\in\; H^2(\mathcal{S},\, \mathcal{B}).$$*

*In Hecke generators, this measures the **transient part of the $R$-matrix**:*

*$$\kappa_n
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{tr}_M^{(n+1)}\!\bigl(
    (1 - \hat{\tau}_n)\, \check{R}^{(n+1)}
  \bigr).$$*

*The perpetual obstruction $\kappa_n \neq 0$ means: at every level, the $R$-matrix has a nonzero transient component — braiding at level $n{+}1$ is **not** entirely determined by level $n$.*

### JC-5: Betti numbers across levels

*$$b_k(A_{n+1})
  \;=\;
  b_k^{\mathrm{desc}}(A_{n+1}) + b_k^{\mathrm{trans}}(A_{n+1}),$$*

*where*

*$$b_k^{\mathrm{desc}}
  \;=\;
  \dim \frac{
    \ker(d_n) \cap \mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{desc}}_{n+1}
  }{
    \mathrm{im}(d_n) \cap \mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{desc}}_{n+1}
  }
  \;=\;
  b_k(A_n)$$*

*and $b_k^{\mathrm{trans}}$ counts genuinely new cohomology classes at level $n{+}1$. The Leray–Serre spectral sequence for $A_{n+1} \to A_n$ has $E_2$-page:*

*$$E_2^{p,r}
  \;=\;
  H^p\!\bigl(A_n,\; H^r(\Omega^1(A_n))\bigr)
  \;\Longrightarrow\;
  H^{p+r}(A_{n+1}),$$*

*with differentials controlled by $\kappa_n$.*

### JC-6: Instanton constraint at level $n$

*$$S_n\!\bigl([T_i^{(n)},\, T_j^{(n)}]\bigr)^*
  \;=\;
  [T_i^{(n)},\, T_j^{(n)}].$$*

*Self-duality of the curvature holds at every level by inheritance of the Frobenius-adjoint structure. The instanton number decomposes:*

*$$c_2(A_n)
  \;=\;
  c_2^{\mathrm{desc}}(A_n) + c_2^{\mathrm{trans}}(A_n),$$*

*where $c_2^{\mathrm{desc}} = c_2(A_{n-1})$ is inherited and $c_2^{\mathrm{trans}}$ is the topological charge of the transient sector.*

### JC-7: Harmonic braid words at level $n$

*$$\Delta_{q,n}\, T_\beta^{(n)} = 0
  \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
  d_{q,n}\, T_\beta^{(n)} = 0
  \;\;\text{and}\;\;
  \delta_{q,n}\, T_\beta^{(n)} = 0.$$*

*The harmonic space decomposes under descent:*

*$$\ker \Delta_{q,n+1}
  \;=\;
  \underbrace{
    \ell_n(\ker \Delta_{q,n})
  }_{\text{descended harmonics}}
  \;\oplus\;
  \underbrace{
    \ker \Delta_{q,n+1} \cap \mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{trans}}_{n+1}
  }_{\text{new particles at level $n{+}1$}}.$$*

*Descended harmonics are the particles already present at level $n$; transient harmonics are **new particle states** created by the jet prolongation.*

### JC-8: \\}v{C}ech cocycle at level $n$

*$$T_{g^{(n)}_{ijk}} \cdot T_{g^{(n)}_{jkl}}
  \;=\;
  T_{a^{(n)}_{ij}} \cdot T_{g^{(n)}_{ikl}} \cdot
  T_{a^{(n)}_{kl}}^{-1}
  \qquad\text{in } H^{(n)}(q).$$*

*The cosimplicial structure links adjacent levels: the coface map $\delta^i$ is jet prolongation $\ell_n$, and the codegeneracy $\sigma^j$ is descent $\mathfrak{d}_{n+1}$. The cosimplicial identities in knot coordinates:*

*$$\ell_n(T_{g^{(n)}_{ijk}}) \;=\; T_{g^{(n+1)}_{\delta^i(ijk)}},
  \qquad
  \mathfrak{d}_{n+1}(T_{g^{(n+1)}_{ijk}}) \;=\; T_{g^{(n)}_{\sigma^j(ijk)}}.$$*

### JC-9: Global gluing (direct limit)

*The direct limit $\mathcal{A}_\infty = \varinjlim\, H^{(n)}(q)$ is the **infinite-level Hecke algebra**. A braid word $w_\infty \in \mathcal{A}_\infty$ is a compatible sequence $(w^{(0)}, w^{(1)}, w^{(2)}, \ldots)$ with $\ell_n(w^{(n)}) = \hat{\tau}_n(w^{(n+1)})$ for all $n$. The global Markov trace is:*

*$$\mathrm{tr}_M^{(\infty)}(w_\infty)
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{tr}_M^{(0)}(w^{(0)})
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{tr}_M^{(n)}(w^{(n)})
  \qquad\text{(level-independent)}.$$*

*All structural and cohomological relations hold in $\mathcal{A}_\infty$. The global gluing condition ensures that locally defined braid words patch into a well-defined element of the direct limit.*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Hadrons and Knot Composites

<div id="def:hadron" class="definition">

**Definition 4.35** (Hadron (stable knot composite)). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.Hadron)*

*A *hadron* is a **stable** composite of fundamental knots: one whose crossing energy is negative, so that binding dominates repulsion.*

*Let $K_1, \ldots, K_n$ be prime knot types in the representation category $\mathbf{C}$, and let $\mathcal{L}$ be a link encoding their internal entanglement. A **hadron** is a composite*

*$$\mathfrak{H}_p \;=\; [K_1, \ldots, K_n]_p \;\bowtie\; \mathcal{L}$$*

*satisfying the **stability condition***

*$$\mathbf{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}(\mathfrak{H}_p) \;<\; 0$$*

*where $\mathbf{E}_{\mathrm{cross}}$ is the crossing energy ([crossing energy](#def:crossing-energy)). The subscript $p$ is the localization point: it determines the colour sector of the exceptional divisor $\mathcal{S}_p$ in which the constituents are coupled. The colour-tube coupling is not an independent datum — it is inherited from $p$. The symbol $\bowtie$ denotes the linking operation.*

</div>

<div id="prop:hadron-operations-closure" class="proposition">

**Proposition 4.36** (Closure of hadron operations under braiding, Hopf linking, skein action, and fusion). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.Hadron.hadron_operations_closure)*

***Proposition.** Let $\mathbf{C}$ be a rigid braided monoidal category and let $\mathfrak{H} \in \mathrm{Sym}^n(K)$ be a hadron ([hadron](#def:hadron)) with constituent knots $K_1, \ldots, K_n$.*

1.  ***Braiding closure.** The braiding $\beta_{K_i, K_j}$ descends to an involution on $\mathrm{Sym}^n(K)$. For the antisymmetric (fermionic) product, exchanging two identical constituents produces $-1$.*

2.  ***Hopf linking closure.** The linking operation $\ell_{ij} \colon K_i \otimes K_j \to K_i \mathbin{\#_{\mathrm{Hopf}}} K_j$ is an endomorphism of $\mathrm{Sym}^n(K) \otimes \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Hopf}}$ with a two-sided inverse (unlinking) when the linking number is trivial.*

3.  ***Skein closure.** The $q$-deformed skein relation $q \cdot L_+ - q^{-1} \cdot L_- = (q - q^{-1}) \cdot L_0$ resolves any linked composite into a polynomial in $q$ times unlinked constituents, yielding the mass formula $\mathcal{M}(\mathfrak{H}) = Q(q) \cdot \mathcal{M}(\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Hopf}}) + \sum_i \mathcal{M}(K_i)$.*

4.  ***Fusion closure.** For hadrons $\mathfrak{H}_1 \in \mathrm{Sym}^{n_1}(K)$ and $\mathfrak{H}_2 \in \mathrm{Sym}^{n_2}(K)$, the fusion $\mathfrak{H}_1 \star \mathfrak{H}_2 \in \mathrm{Sym}^{n_1 + n_2}(K)$ is again a hadron.*

</div>

<div id="rem:hadron-operations" class="remark">

**Remark 4.37** (Operations on hadrons).

*The symmetric product $\mathrm{Sym}^n(K)$ carries natural operations inherited from the braiding and Hopf link structure of $\mathbf{C}$.*

***Braiding.** The braiding $\beta_{K_i, K_j} \colon K_i \otimes K_j \xrightarrow{\sim} K_j \otimes K_i$ permutes constituent knots within a hadron. Since $\mathrm{Sym}^n$ quotients by the symmetric group action, the braiding descends to an involution on $\mathrm{Sym}^n(K)$. For fermions (antisymmetric product), the braiding picks up a sign: exchanging two identical constituents produces $-1$.*

***Hopf linking.** Two knots $K_i, K_j$ within the same hadron can be *linked* via the Hopf link $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Hopf}}$. This linking operation*

*$$\ell_{ij} \;\colon\;
  K_i \otimes K_j
  \;\longrightarrow\;
  K_i \mathbin{\#_{\mathrm{Hopf}}} K_j$$*

*replaces two separate constituents with a single linked pair. The inverse operation (*unlinking*) decomposes a linked pair back into its constituents, when the linking number is trivial.*

***Skein action.** The $q$-deformed Skein relations act on $\mathrm{Sym}^n(K) \otimes \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Hopf}}$ by resolving crossings in the linked configuration. At each crossing, the Skein relation provides the decomposition:*

*$$q \cdot L_+ \;-\; q^{-1} \cdot L_-
  \;=\; (q - q^{-1}) \cdot L_0$$*

*where $L_+$, $L_-$, $L_0$ are the positive-crossing, negative-crossing, and smoothed configurations. Iterating over all crossings resolves the linked composite into a polynomial in $q$ times unlinked constituents, yielding the mass formula $\mathcal{M}(\mathfrak{H}) = Q(q) \cdot \mathcal{M}(\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Hopf}}) + \sum_i \mathcal{M}(K_i)$.*

***Fusion.** Two hadrons $\mathfrak{H}_1 \in \mathrm{Sym}^{n_1}(K)$ and $\mathfrak{H}_2 \in \mathrm{Sym}^{n_2}(K)$ can be *fused* into a composite $\mathfrak{H}_1 \star \mathfrak{H}_2 \in \mathrm{Sym}^{n_1 + n_2}(K)$ by forming the Hopf link between their binding structures. This models hadron scattering at the categorical level.*

</div>

<div id="rem:knot-factorization" class="remark">

**Remark 4.38** (Knot factorization through tensor powers of $V$).

*The [tensor generation](#rem:simple-objects-V) property of the fundamental object $V$ has a concrete consequence for the hadron construction: every constituent knot type $K_i$ in a [hadron](#def:hadron) factors through a tensor power of $V$.*

*Specifically, if $K_i$ is a knot whose associated simple object is $V_{j_i}$, then $V_{j_i}$ appears as a direct summand of $V^{\otimes 2j_i}$. The [PawLei basis](#prop:pawlowski-leitner-basis) provides a canonical embedding*

*$$\iota_{j_i} \colon V_{j_i}
  \;\hookrightarrow\;
  V_{1/2}^{\otimes 2j_i},$$*

*so a hadron $\mathfrak{H} \in V_{j_1} \otimes \cdots \otimes V_{j_n}$ can be written in a universal tensor form:*

*$$\mathfrak{H} \;\hookrightarrow\;
  V_{1/2}^{\otimes 2(j_1 + \cdots + j_n)}.$$*

*This embedding is *not* unique — the choice of PawLei basis element for each factor corresponds to a choice of partial-wave channel. The physical hadron is obtained by summing over all channels weighted by the Skein polynomial, so the [hadronic mass formula](#def:hadron) arises as a contraction of the universal tensor with the Hopf link invariant.*

*In the QOU framework, this factorization explains why *all* composite particles are ultimately built from the single two-dimensional object $V$: the categorical dimension $2$ of $V$ is the minimal non-trivial dimension compatible with the volume constraint, and tensor generation ensures no further building blocks are needed.*

</div>

<div id="def:localized-hadron" class="definition">

**Definition 4.39** (Localized hadron). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.LocalizedHadron)*

*A *localized hadron* is a hadron ([Definition](#def:hadron)) that has been placed at a categorical point $p$ of the projective line $\mathbb{P}(V)$ ([Definition](#def:projective-line-object)).*

*Formally, a **localized hadron** at $p$ is a morphism in $\mathbf{C}$:*

*$$H_p \;\colon\; \mathbf{1}
  \;\longrightarrow\;
  \mathrm{Sym}^n\!\bigl(\mathcal{K}_p\bigr)
  \;\otimes\;
  \mathcal{L}_{p}^{\mathrm{bind}}$$*

*where $\mathcal{K}_p$ denotes the fibre of knot types at $p$ and $\mathcal{L}_{p}^{\mathrm{bind}}$ is the binding Hopf link at $p$. The morphism from $\mathbf{1}$ is what distinguishes a localized hadron from an abstract one: it selects a specific point in the base space where the composite knot is situated.*

</div>

<div id="def:hadron-fibre-embedding" class="definition">

**Definition 4.40** (Fibre-compatible hadron embedding). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.HadronFibreEmbedding)*

*Let $\mathfrak{H} \in \mathrm{Sym}^n(K) \otimes \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Hopf}}$ be a hadron ([Definition](#def:hadron)) and let $\mathcal{S}_p$ denote the fibre of the knot bundle over a point $p \in \mathbb{P}(V)$ ([Definition](#def:projective-line-object)). A **fibre-compatible hadron embedding** is a morphism*

*$$\iota_p \;\colon\;
  \mathrm{Sym}^n(K) \otimes \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Hopf}}
  \;\longrightarrow\;
  \mathcal{S}_p$$*

*satisfying the following conditions:*

1.  ***Integrability.** The embedding $\iota_p$ is *integrable* in the sense that the abstract hadron data (linking, braiding, Skein decomposition) can be consistently realized within the geometric structure of the fibre $\mathcal{S}_p$. Concretely, $\iota_p$ must intertwine the abstract Skein action ([operations on hadrons](#rem:hadron-operations)) with the geometric operations on knots in $\mathcal{S}_p$.*

2.  ***Fibre confinement.** The image $\iota_p(\mathfrak{H})$ is entirely contained in the fibre $\mathcal{S}_p$. No constituent knot extends to a neighbouring fibre $E_{p'}$ for $p' \neq p$. This is enforced by a finite Mobius energy bound: $$\mathcal{E}_{\mathrm{Mob}}(\iota_p) \;<\; \infty,$$ which prevents the knot complement from developing cusps that would reach the boundary of the fibre.*

3.  ***Hopf compatibility.** The embedding respects linking and unlinking via the Hopf structure: the diagram $$\begin{tikzcd}[row sep=2.5em, column sep=3em]
      \mathrm{Sym}^n(K) \otimes \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Hopf}}
        \ar[r, "\iota_p"]
        \ar[d, "\ell_{ij}"']
      & \mathcal{S}_p
        \ar[d, "\ell_{ij}"]
      \\
      \mathrm{Sym}^{n'}(K) \otimes \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Hopf}}'
        \ar[r, "\iota_p'"']
      & \mathcal{S}_p
    \end{tikzcd}
    \qquad\text{(Hopf compatibility)}$$ commutes for every linking operation $\ell_{ij}$.*

4.  ***Volume compatibility.** The embedding preserves hyperbolic volumes: $\mathrm{vol}(\iota_p(K_i)) = \mathrm{vol}(K_i)$ for each constituent knot $K_i$. This ensures that the mass contribution of each knot, computed via the hyperbolic volume, is faithfully represented in the fibre.*

*A localized hadron ([Definition](#def:localized-hadron)) equipped with a fibre-compatible embedding is a **physically realized hadron**: it is both situated at a base point and faithfully embedded in the fibre geometry. The integrability condition is the key structural requirement — it asserts that the abstract algebraic hadron can be "integrated" into a concrete geometric realization.*

</div>

<div id="prop:skein-generation" class="proposition">

**Proposition 4.41** (Skein generation of hadrons from mass-zero fundamentals). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.Torsion.skein_generation)*

*Let $(\mathbf{C}, A, \tau)$ be a quantum observable universe with substrate parameter $q$ and Skein module $\mathcal{S}_q = \mathcal{S}_q(\mathbf{C})$. The Skein module $\mathcal{S}_q$ is generated as an algebra by:*

1.  *The fundamental (mass-zero) knot types $\{K_i\}_{i \in \mathcal{F}}$ (torus knots), and*

2.  *The Hopf link $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Hopf}}$ (the binding operation).*

*Every hadron admits a terminal Skein resolution into a finite polynomial in these generators with coefficients in $\mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}]$.*

</div>

<div class="proof">

*Proof of Skein generation.* <span id="prf:skein-generation" label="prf:skein-generation"></span>

**Generators.** A knot type $K$ is *fundamental* if its hyperbolic volume vanishes: $\mathrm{Vol}(K) = 0$. By the geometrization of knot complements, these are precisely the torus knots (and the unknot). In the particle dictionary, the fundamental knots are the fermions: the unknot (neutrino), trefoil $3_1$ (electron), cinquefoil $5_1$ (tau), and the torus$(p,2)$ family.

**Generation.** The Skein module $\mathcal{S}_q$ is generated as an algebra by the fundamental knot types $\{K_i\}_{i \in \mathcal{F}}$ and the Hopf link $\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Hopf}}$. Every hadron $H \in \mathrm{Sym}^n(K) \otimes \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Hopf}}$ admits a **terminal Skein resolution**: iterating the Skein relation

$$q \cdot L_+ \;-\; q^{-1} \cdot L_-
  \;=\; (q - q^{-1}) \cdot L_0$$

at every crossing terminates in a finite polynomial

$$[H] \;=\; \sum_{\alpha} c_\alpha(q) \cdot
  [K_{i_1}] \cdots [K_{i_k}]$$

where each $[K_{i_j}]$ is the class of a fundamental knot and $c_\alpha(q) \in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}]$.

**Mass from linking.** Evaluating the mass functional $\mathcal{M}$ on the Skein resolution gives:

$$\mathcal{M}(H)
  \;=\;
  \underbrace{Q(q) \cdot \mathcal{M}(\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Hopf}})}_{\text{binding energy (from linking)}}
  \;+\;
  \underbrace{\sum_{i=1}^{n}
  \frac{\mathrm{Vol}(K_i)}{\hbar_q^{\,2}}}_{\text{constituent mass (zero for torus knots)}}$$

where $Q(q) \in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}]$ is the Skein polynomial of the linking configuration and $\hbar_q = 1 - q^{-1}$.

For hadrons composed entirely of fundamental (torus-knot) constituents, $\mathrm{Vol}(K_i) = 0$ for all $i$, so the entire inertial mass arises from the linking topology:

$$\mathcal{M}(H) \;=\; Q(q) \cdot \mathcal{M}(\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Hopf}}).$$ ◻

</div>

<div id="def:knot-particle-generation" class="definition">

**Definition 4.42** (Knot-particle generation from $T_{m,n}$ torus knot generators). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.Torsion.KnotParticleGeneration)*

*The particle spectrum is generated from a finite set of torus knot *generators* $T_{m,n}$ (with $\gcd(m,n) = 1$) embedded in the standard torus $\mathbb{T}^2 \subset S^3$, together with two *linking operations* that act on the exceptional divisor and the color-tube fibration.*

***Notation.** A torus knot $T_{m,n}$ winds $m$ times around the meridian and $n$ times around the longitude of $\mathbb{T}^2$. We reserve $q$ for the substrate parameter ([substrate parameter](#def:substrate-parameter)) and $p$ for base points, so the winding indices are always $(m,n)$.*

***Generator set.** The *torus knot generators* are the family*

*$$\mathcal{G} \;=\; \bigl\{\, T_{m,n} \;\big|\;
  \gcd(m,n) = 1,\; m < n,\;
  m + n \leq N(\chi) \,\bigr\}$$*

*where $N(\chi)$ is a cutoff determined by the Euler characteristic of the Frobenius–Hopf object. For the Descartes universe with $\chi(A) = -6$, the bound is $N(-6) = 9$, admitting:*

| *Generator* | *Knot*             | *Crossing number* | *Particle sector*                 |
|:------------|:-------------------|:------------------|:----------------------------------|
| *$T_{1,0}$* | *Unknot $0_1$*     | *$0$*             | *Neutrino (trivial braiding)*     |
| *$T_{2,3}$* | *Trefoil $3_1$*    | *$3$*             | *Electron / Up quark (gen.\\} 1)* |
| *$T_{2,5}$* | *Cinquefoil $5_1$* | *$5$*             | *Tau / Bottom quark (gen.\\} 3)*  |
| *$T_{2,7}$* | *$7_1$*            | *$7$*             | *Charm quark (heavy sector)*      |
| *$T_{3,4}$* | *$8_{19}$*         | *$8$*             | *Top-quark candidate*             |
| *$T_{3,5}$* | *$10_{124}$*       | *$10$*            | *Beyond-Standard-Model sector*    |

*All torus knots have *zero hyperbolic volume*: they are not hyperbolic but satellite/torus type. Consequently their bare mass under the topological mass formula ([topological mass formula](#prop:topological-mass-formula)) vanishes:*

*$$\mathcal{M}_{\mathrm{bare}}(T_{m,n}) \;=\;
  \frac{\mathrm{Vol}(T_{m,n})}{\hbar_q^{\,2}} \;=\; 0.$$*

*Mass arises *entirely* through the linking operations: Hopf linking on the exceptional divisor, color-tube threading, and Skein crossing change.*

***Presentation of the particle Skein module.** The Skein module ([Skein generation](#prop:skein-generation)) admits a presentation*

*$$\mathcal{S}_q(\mathbf{C}) \;=\;
  \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}]\bigl\langle\,
    \mathcal{G},\;
    \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Hopf}},\;
    \ell_c
  \,\bigr\rangle
  \Big/
  \bigl(\,
    q\,L_+ - q^{-1}L_- - (q^{1/2} - q^{-1/2})\,L_0
  \,\bigr)$$*

*where $\mathcal{G}$ is the torus knot generator set and the relation is the HOMFLY-PT Skein relation applied at every crossing. Every particle in the knot–particle dictionary ([knot–particle dictionary](#rem:knot-particle-dictionary)) is a word in this presentation.*

</div>

<div id="prop:knot-particle-correspondence" class="proposition">

**Proposition 4.43** (Knot–particle correspondence via $q$-Schur–Weyl duality). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.Braiding.knot_particle_correspondence)*

***Proposition.** Let $V = V_{1/2}$ be the fundamental representation of $\mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{su}(2))$ and let $B_n$ act faithfully on $V^{\otimes n}$ via the $R$-matrix braiding ([braid action on tensor products](#prop:braid-action-tensor)). By $q$-Schur–Weyl duality ([knot eigenbasis completeness](#prop:knot-eigenbasis-complete)), $V^{\otimes n}$ decomposes into irreducible summands labelled by partitions $\lambda \vdash n$.*

*Then the Markov trace on $H_n(q)$ assigns to each irreducible summand a knot type $K_\lambda$ (the closure of any braid representative), establishing a bijection between:*

- *Irreducible summands of $V^{\otimes n}$ under the Hecke algebra $H_n(q)$, and*

- *Knot/link types arising as closures of $n$-strand braids.*

*In particular, each localized knot ([localized knot](#def:localized-knot)) $(p, K)$ in a bundle corresponds to a unique irreducible summand, and hadrons ([hadron](#def:hadron)) correspond to tensor products of such summands bound by Hopf links.*

</div>

<div id="rem:knot-particle-dictionary" class="remark">

**Remark 4.44** (Knot–particle dictionary).

*The localized knot framework ([Definition](#def:localized-knot)) assigns a topological identity to each fundamental particle. This dictionary is *derived* from the categorical braiding on $V = V_{1/2}$, not postulated: the $R$-matrix of $\mathcal{U}_q(\mathfrak{su}(2))$ endows $V^{\otimes n}$ with a faithful $B_n$-action ([Proposition](#prop:braid-action-tensor)), and $q$-Schur–Weyl duality ([Theorem](#prop:knot-eigenbasis-complete)) decomposes $V^{\otimes n}$ into irreducible summands labelled by partitions $\lambda \vdash n$. By Alexander’s theorem, every oriented knot is the closure of a braid $\beta \in B_n$, so the Markov trace on the Hecke algebra $H_n(q)$ identifies each irreducible summand with a knot type. The resulting dictionary is:*

| *Knot type*     | *Symbol*                | *Particle* | *Crossing number* | *Role in bundle*                     |
|:----------------|:------------------------|:-----------|:------------------|:-------------------------------------|
| *Point (empty)* | *$\varnothing$*         | *Photon*   | *$0$*             | *Background flux on $\mathcal{S}_p$* |
| *Unknot*        | *$\mathcal{O}$ ($0_1$)* | *Neutrino* | *$0$*             | *Trivial braiding; vacuum drag*      |
| *Trefoil*       | *$3_1$*                 | *Electron* | *$3$*             | *Simplest stable vortex (gen. 1)*    |
| *Figure-eight*  | *$4_1$*                 | *Muon*     | *$4$*             | *Hyperbolic volume residue (gen. 2)* |
| *Cinquefoil*    | *$5_1$*                 | *Tau*      | *$5$*             | *Higher-genus lift (gen. 3)*         |

*In a bundle initial condition $\mathcal{S}_0$, each entry $(p_i, K_i)$ is one row of this dictionary placed at a specific point on $\mathbb{P}(V)$.*

</div>

<div id="def:bundle-initial-conditions" class="definition">

**Definition 4.45** (Bundle initial conditions). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.BundleInitialConditions)*

*A **bundle initial condition** over the projective line $\mathbb{P}(V)$ at a reference point in an affine chart is a formal sum of localized hadrons and photons at base points:*

*$$\mathcal{S}_0 \;=\; \sum_{i \in I} (p_i,\, H_i)$$*

*where each $(p_i, H_i)$ is a localized hadron ([Definition](#def:localized-hadron)) or a photon ($H_i = \varnothing$). The index set $I$ may be infinite, and multiple constituents may share the same base point (bosonic and fermionic statistics are determined by the Skein algebra, not by a support constraint).*

*Equivalently, $\mathcal{S}_0$ is a section of the free commutative monoid on the hadron sheaf $\mathcal{H}$:*

*$$\mathcal{S}_0 \;\in\;
  \Gamma\!\bigl(\mathbb{P}(V),\;
  \mathrm{Free}_{\mathrm{CMon}}(\mathcal{H})\bigr).$$*

*This is a **position-only** specification: the positions $\{p_i\}$ on $\mathbb{P}(V)$ are known exactly, while the momenta are entirely undetermined. The categorical content is that $\mathcal{S}_0$ specifies the *fibre data* of the bundle — which constituent sits in which fibre — without any information about the horizontal transport connecting neighbouring fibres.*

*The subsequent configurations $\mathcal{S}_1, \mathcal{S}_2, \ldots$ represent the forward light cone from $\mathcal{S}_0$: each step applies one iteration of the Reeb flow ([information-theoretic time](#def:information-theoretic-time)), adding horizontal transport and accumulating interaction relations. The backward sequence $\mathcal{S}_{-1}, \mathcal{S}_{-2}, \ldots$ represents the past light cone (reversing computation). Whether the sequence extends infinitely in either direction, or terminates, is **not assumed** — it depends on the dynamics within the given affine chart.*

*For the equivalence relation on bundle initial conditions, see [Definition](#def:bundle-isotopy-equivalence).*

</div>

<div id="prop:sorting-color-energy" class="proposition">

**Proposition 4.46** (Sorting deposits energy $q + q^{-1}$ per crossing in the colour fibre).

***Proposition.** *Let $T_i$ be the Hecke generator ([R-matrix braiding](#rem:r-matrix-braiding)) acting on $V \otimes V$, where $V$ is the fundamental representation. Then:**

1.  ***(Eigenspace decomposition.)** *The R-matrix decomposes $V \otimes V$ into two eigenspaces:* $$V \otimes V
      \;=\;
      \mathrm{Sym}^2(V) \;\oplus\; \textstyle\bigwedge^2(V)$$ *with eigenvalues $q$ (symmetric, ordered) and $-q^{-1}$ (antisymmetric, disordered) respectively. These are the two roots of the Hecke relation $T^2 = (q - q^{-1})T + 1$.**

2.  ***(Sorting is projection.)** *A sorting operation — swapping two adjacent items into the correct order — is the projection from $\bigwedge^2(V)$ to $\mathrm{Sym}^2(V)$ at the generator $T_i$. This projection is the $\mathrm{Ad}$ component of the observation: it acts on the colour fibre by rotating the gauge degrees of freedom from the antisymmetric (disordered) to the symmetric (ordered) eigenspace.**

3.  ***(Energy per crossing.)** *The energy deposited in the colour fibre by one sorting operation is the eigenvalue gap:* $$\Delta E_{\mathrm{colour}}
      \;=\; q - (-q^{-1})
      \;=\; q + q^{-1}$$ *At $q = q_0$: $\Delta E = 2.011$ action units per crossing.**

4.  ***(Total sorting energy.)** *Let $\pi \in S_n$ be a permutation representing the disordered state of $n$ items. The minimum number of adjacent transpositions (braid crossings) needed to sort $\pi$ is the inversion count $\mathrm{inv}(\pi)$. The total energy deposited in the colour fibre is:* $$E_{\mathrm{colour}}(\pi)
      \;=\;
      \mathrm{inv}(\pi) \cdot (q + q^{-1})$$ *The worst case (reverse permutation) requires $\binom{n}{2}$ crossings; the identity requires zero.**

**Proof.* (1) The Hecke relation $T^2 - (q - q^{-1})T - 1 = 0$ has roots $q$ and $-q^{-1}$ by the quadratic formula. The corresponding idempotents are:*

*$$e_+ = \frac{T + q^{-1}}{q + q^{-1}}, \qquad
  e_- = \frac{q - T}{q + q^{-1}}$$*

*with $e_+ + e_- = 1$ and $e_+ e_- = 0$. The image of $e_+$ is $\mathrm{Sym}^2(V)$ (the symmetric representation, eigenvalue $q$); the image of $e_-$ is $\bigwedge^2(V)$ (the antisymmetric representation, eigenvalue $-q^{-1}$).*

*(2) A disordered pair occupies $\bigwedge^2(V)$: the two items are in the wrong order, so the state is antisymmetric under exchange. Sorting swaps them into the correct order, moving the state to $\mathrm{Sym}^2(V)$. This is the projection $e_+$. In the observation ([observation](#def:observation)), $e_+$ is the $\mathrm{Ad}$ component: it acts on the colour fibre by conjugation, rotating the antisymmetric state to the symmetric eigenspace.*

*(3) The energy deposited is the eigenvalue difference: $q - (-q^{-1}) = q + q^{-1}$.*

*(4) Each adjacent transposition in the sorting algorithm corresponds to one braid crossing $\sigma_i$. The standard result from combinatorics: the minimum number of adjacent transpositions to realise $\pi$ equals $\mathrm{inv}(\pi)$, the number of pairs $(i, j)$ with $i < j$ and $\pi(i) > \pi(j)$. Each crossing deposits $q + q^{-1}$ in the colour fibre. $\square$*

***Example: three socks.***

|  *Permutation $\pi$*  | *$\mathrm{inv}(\pi)$* |          *Crossings*           | *$E_{\mathrm{colour}}$* |
|:---------------------:|:---------------------:|:------------------------------:|:-----------------------:|
|  *$(1,2,3)$ sorted*   |         *$0$*         |             *$0$*              |          *$0$*          |
| *$(1,3,2)$ one swap*  |         *$1$*         |          *$\sigma_2$*          |     *$q + q^{-1}$*      |
| *$(2,1,3)$ one swap*  |         *$1$*         |          *$\sigma_1$*          |     *$q + q^{-1}$*      |
| *$(2,3,1)$ two swaps* |         *$2$*         |     *$\sigma_1 \sigma_2$*      |    *$2(q + q^{-1})$*    |
| *$(3,1,2)$ two swaps* |         *$2$*         |     *$\sigma_2 \sigma_1$*      |    *$2(q + q^{-1})$*    |
|  *$(3,2,1)$ reverse*  |         *$3$*         | *$\sigma_1 \sigma_2 \sigma_1$* |    *$3(q + q^{-1})$*    |

*At $q = q_0$: sorting three fully reversed socks costs $3 \times 2.011 = 6.033$ action units in the colour fibre. This energy is not lost — it is stored in the gauge degrees of freedom as the record of the observer’s intent.*

</div>

<div id="def:bundle-isotopy-equivalence" class="definition">

**Definition 4.47** (Isotopy equivalence of bundle initial conditions). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.BundleIsotopyEquiv)*

*Two bundle initial conditions ([Definition](#def:bundle-initial-conditions)) are **isotopy equivalent** if they are related by a permutation of indices and an ambient isotopy within each fibre:*

*$$\{(p_i, H_i)\}_{i \in I} \;\sim\;
  \{(p_{\sigma(i)}, H_{\sigma(i)}')\}_{i \in I}$$*

*where $\sigma$ is a bijection on $I$ and each $H_{\sigma(i)}'$ is ambient-isotopic to $H_{\sigma(i)}$ in the fibre $E_{p_{\sigma(i)}}$.*

*This is the natural equivalence relation: the physical content of a bundle initial condition depends only on *which* hadron types are placed *where*, not on the labeling of the index set or the particular representative of each ambient isotopy class.*

</div>

<div id="def:torsion-knot-flow" class="definition">

**Definition 4.48** (Torsion-driven knot flow). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.ParticleState)*

*Given a bundle initial condition $\mathcal{S}_0 = \{(p_i, K_i)\}_{i=1}^{N}$ ([Definition](#def:bundle-initial-conditions)), the **torsion-driven knot flow** is the one-parameter family of bundle states*

*$$E_t \;=\; \bigl\{\bigl(\Phi_t^q(p_i),\; K_i\bigr)\bigr\}_{i=1}^{N}
  \qquad t \geq 0,$$*

*where $\Phi_t^q$ is the flow on $\mathbb{P}(V)$ generated by the $q$-deformed Reeb vector field $\xi_q$ ([Definition](#def:categorical-q-reeb-flow)).*

*The flow has two components:*

1.  ***Intrinsic rotation.** Each knot type $K$ carries an intrinsic angular momentum proportional to its crossing number $c(K)$: $$\omega_K \;=\; c(K) \cdot \frac{2\pi}{[c(K)]_q!}$$ where $[n]_q! = [1]_q [2]_q \cdots [n]_q$ is the $q$-factorial. This drives geodesic motion on $\mathbb{P}(V) \cong S^2$ along a great circle whose axis is determined by the initial fibre framing.*

2.  ***Pairwise interaction.** When two localized knots $(p_i, K_i)$ and $(p_j, K_j)$ are within Planck-scale separation $d_{\mathbb{P}(V)}(p_i, p_j) < \ell_P$, they experience a short-range repulsive force $$F_{ij} \;=\;
      \frac{\Delta_q(K_i) \cdot \Delta_q(K_j)}{d(p_i, p_j)^2 + \ell_P^2}$$ where $\Delta_q(K)$ is the $q$-Alexander polynomial of $K$ evaluated at $q = e^{-r}$, and $d$ is the round metric on $S^2$.*

*The flow preserves the total knot content $\sum_i K_i$ (knot types do not change under evolution) but redistributes positions on $\mathbb{P}(V)$. Categorically, the flow is a natural transformation*

*$$\Phi^q \;\colon\;
  \mathrm{id}_{\mathrm{Bun}(\mathbb{P}(V))}
  \;\Longrightarrow\;
  \mathrm{id}_{\mathrm{Bun}(\mathbb{P}(V))}$$*

*in the category $\mathrm{Bun}(\mathbb{P}(V))$ of finite bundles over the projective line, where morphisms are equivariant maps that preserve knot type.*

</div>

## Borromean Baryons and Reidemeister Invariance

<div id="def:borromean-baryon" class="definition">

**Definition 4.49** (Borromean baryon). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.Braiding.BorromeanBaryon)*

*A **Borromean baryon** is a hadron ([hadron](#def:hadron)) whose three constituents are unknots $K_{0_1}$ joined by the Borromean link $\mathcal{B}_3$, bound by the Hopf link $\mathcal{L}_H$.*

*$$B \;=\;
  \mathcal{B}_3(K_{0_1},\, K_{0_1},\, K_{0_1})
  \;\bowtie\; \mathcal{L}_H$$*

</div>

<div id="prop:fermion-boson-knot-link" class="proposition">

**Proposition 4.50** (Fermions are knots, bosons are links). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.Braiding.fermion_boson_knot_link)*

***Proposition.** The fermion–boson decomposition ([fermion–boson decomposition](#def:fermion-boson-decomposition)) coincides with the knot–link decomposition of the $T(2,n)$ torus family on the Bring’s surface:*

- *A **fermion** ($\alpha_V \neq 0$) is a **knot** (1 component).*

- *A **boson** ($\alpha_V = 0$) is a **link** (2 components).*

*Equivalently: fermions have odd $n$ in $T(2,n)$ and bosons have even $n$.*

**Proof.* The torus knot $T(2,n)$ on the Bring’s surface wraps $2$ times around the meridian and $n$ times around the longitude. The number of connected components is $\gcd(2, n)$.*

***Case $n$ odd** ($\gcd(2,n) = 1$): $T(2,n)$ is a knot with one connected component. This single component winds around the Reeb direction ([categorical Reeb](#def:categorical-reeb)) with nonzero winding number. In the weight decomposition, the vertical projection $\pi_V$ detects this winding: $\pi_V(\alpha) \neq 0$. The particle is a **fermion**.*

***Case $n$ even** ($\gcd(2,n) = 2$): $T(2,n)$ is a link with two connected components, each winding $1$ time around the meridian and $n/2$ times around the longitude. The two components have **opposite vertical winding**: one winds $+1$ and the other $-1$ around the Reeb direction (they are related by the fiber adjoint involution). Their vertical projections cancel: $\pi_V(\alpha^{(1)}) + \pi_V(\alpha^{(2)}) = 0$, so the total vertical component vanishes. The particle is a **boson**. $\square$*

***The T(2,n) particle table.***

| *$n$* | *$\gcd(2,n)$* | *Type* | *$\alpha_V$* | *Statistics* | *Particle*   |
|------:|:-------------:|:-------|:------------:|:------------:|:-------------|
|   *2* |      *2*      | *Link* |   *$= 0$*    |   *Boson*    | *Gluon*      |
|   *3* |      *1*      | *Knot* |  *$\neq 0$*  |  *Fermion*   | *Electron*   |
|   *4* |      *2*      | *Link* |   *$= 0$*    |   *Boson*    | *$W$ boson*  |
|   *5* |      *1*      | *Knot* |  *$\neq 0$*  |  *Fermion*   | *Muon*       |
|   *6* |      *2*      | *Link* |   *$= 0$*    |   *Boson*    | *$Z$ boson*  |
|   *7* |      *1*      | *Knot* |  *$\neq 0$*  |  *Fermion*   | *Tau*        |
|   *8* |      *2*      | *Link* |   *$= 0$*    |   *Boson*    | *Higgs?*     |
|   *9* |      *1*      | *Knot* |  *$\neq 0$*  |  *Fermion*   | *Saturating* |

***Spin–statistics from topology.** The spin–statistics theorem (fermions have half-integer spin, bosons have integer spin) becomes a topological statement:*

- ***Half-integer spin**: a knot (1 component) requires a $4\pi$ rotation to return to its original configuration. The single strand winds through the Reeb flow with an odd winding number, and the monodromy of the fiber adjoint involution has order $2$ (not $1$).*

- ***Integer spin**: a link (2 components) returns to its original configuration after a $2\pi$ rotation. The two strands can be exchanged by the fiber adjoint involution without changing the link type.*

***Quarks in this framework.** Quarks are **not** knots or links in the $T(2,n)$ family. They are unknots Borromean-linked in the exceptional divisor ([Borromean quark](#conj:borromean-quark)). The Borromean link $\mathcal{B}_3$ has **three** components — neither a knot (1) nor a standard link (2). Its statistics are determined by the overall baryon: the proton $\mathcal{B}_3(u,u,d) \bowtie \mathcal{L}_H$ is a composite fermion because the Borromean structure, when resolved via the Skein relation, reduces to an odd number of knot components.*

</div>

<div id="prop:reidemeister-mass-invariance" class="proposition">

**Proposition 4.51** (Reidemeister invariance of mass and binding energy). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.Braiding.reidemeister_mass_invariance)*

***Proposition.** The topological mass formula is a knot invariant (R-I, R-II, R-III). The binding energy of linked particles is an embedding invariant (R-II, R-III but not R-I). Shell transitions are R-I moves on the embedding.*

***The three Reidemeister moves.***

*Every deformation of a knot diagram decomposes into a sequence of three local moves:*

- ***R-I** (curl): add or remove a single crossing (writhe changes by $\pm 1$).*

- ***R-II** (poke): add or remove a pair of crossings with opposite signs (writhe unchanged).*

- ***R-III** (slide): move a strand past a crossing (crossing number unchanged).*

***Topological mass: invariant under all three.***

*The bare mass of a particle is determined by the hyperbolic volume of its knot complement:*

*$$m_{\mathrm{bare}} \;=\;
  \frac{\mathrm{Vol}(S^3 \setminus K)}{\hbar_q^2}
  \cdot \lambda_{\mathrm{scale}}.$$*

*The hyperbolic volume is a **topological invariant** of the knot type — it does not depend on the diagram. Since Reidemeister’s theorem states that two diagrams represent the same knot if and only if they are related by a finite sequence of R-I, R-II, R-III moves:*

*$$m_{\mathrm{bare}}
  \;\text{is invariant under R-I, R-II, R-III.}$$*

*The electron mass $\mathfrak{m}_e \approx 0.511$ MeV (from vacuum drag, since $\mathrm{Vol}(T_{2,3}) = 0$) does not change when the electron is excited. The proton mass $\mathfrak{m}_{\mathfrak{p}} \approx 938$ MeV (from $\mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3)$) does not change when the atom is ionised. Mass is a property of the **knot type**, not the diagram.*

***Binding energy: invariant under R-II and R-III only.***

*The binding energy of a linked pair (electron–proton, or nucleon–nucleon) is the crossing energy of the Hopf link connecting them:*

*$$\mathbf{E}_{\mathrm{bind}}
  \;=\;
  \sum_{\text{crossings of link}}
  \epsilon_i \cdot q^{\pm 1}$$*

*where the sum runs over the crossings of the **embedding** of one particle’s knot inside the other’s Seifert surface.*

- ***R-III** (strand slide): rearranges crossings without changing their number or signs. The crossing energy sum is invariant. $\checkmark$*

- ***R-II** (poke): adds two crossings of opposite sign. Their contributions to the crossing energy are $+q \cdot \epsilon$ and $-q^{-1} \cdot \epsilon$. In the Skein resolution, the pair resolves to $(q - q^{-1}) \cdot \epsilon \cdot L_0$, where $L_0$ is the smoothed state. For a virtual pair (the two crossings are adjacent), $L_0$ is the original link and the contributions cancel to leading order. The binding energy is invariant. $\checkmark$*

- ***R-I** (curl): adds a single crossing. This changes the writhe by $\pm 1$ and adds a crossing energy contribution $\pm q^{\pm 1} \cdot \epsilon$ that does **not** cancel. The binding energy **changes**. $\times$*

*$$\mathbf{E}_{\mathrm{bind}}
  \;\text{is invariant under R-II, R-III but \textbf{not} R-I.}$$*

***Shell transitions are R-I moves.***

*When a photon is absorbed by the hydrogen atom, the electron trefoil $T_{2,3}$ undergoes a **Reidemeister I move** within its Hopf link to the proton: a curl is added to the trefoil diagram at the exceptional divisor. The writhe changes from $w$ to $w + 2$ (a pair of R-I moves adding two curls to preserve the knot type’s minimal crossing structure):*

*$$n \to n + 1
  \qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad
  w \to w + 2
  \qquad\Longleftrightarrow\qquad
  \text{two R-I moves on the embedding.}$$*

*The bare mass $\mathfrak{m}_e$ is unchanged (R-I is a knot invariant). The binding energy $E_n = -13.6/n^2$ eV changes (R-I is NOT an embedding invariant). The difference $\Delta E = E_{n+1} - E_n$ is the photon energy.*

***Summary.***

| *Quantity*         |     *R-I*      |     *R-II*     |    *R-III*     | *Physical meaning*               |
|:-------------------|:--------------:|:--------------:|:--------------:|:---------------------------------|
| *Bare mass*        | *$\checkmark$* | *$\checkmark$* | *$\checkmark$* | *Particle identity (knot type)*  |
| *Binding energy*   |   *$\times$*   | *$\checkmark$* | *$\checkmark$* | *Bound state energy (embedding)* |
| *Shell number $n$* |   *$\times$*   | *$\checkmark$* | *$\checkmark$* | *Writhe level of embedding*      |
| *Knot type*        | *$\checkmark$* | *$\checkmark$* | *$\checkmark$* | *Which particle it is*           |
| *Writhe $w$*       |   *$\times$*   | *$\checkmark$* |  *$\times^*$*  | *Diagram-dependent*              |

*${}^*$R-III preserves writhe but is not the only invariance of writhe; writhe is a regular isotopy invariant (R-II + R-III), not a knot invariant (R-I + R-II + R-III).*

***Physical consequence.***

*A particle’s **identity** (which knot type: electron, muon, proton, neutron) is determined by R-I + R-II + R-III invariants — the topological knot type. A particle’s **state** (which shell, which orbital) is determined by R-II + R-III invariants — the regular isotopy class of the embedding. The difference between identity and state is precisely one Reidemeister move: R-I.*

*This is why an excited hydrogen atom is still hydrogen: the electron is still a trefoil (knot type unchanged by R-I). But it is in a different state: the trefoil’s writhe is different (embedding changed by R-I), and the binding energy differs.*

</div>

<div id="prop:nuclear-shell-intruder" class="proposition">

**Proposition 4.52** (Stability pairs from Borromean spin-orbit intruder levels). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.Braiding.nuclear_shell_intruder)*

***Proposition.** The stability pairs $\{2, 8, 20, 28, 50, 82, 126\}$ arise from the harmonic oscillator shell structure of nucleons in the nuclear mean field, corrected by the spin-orbit coupling of the Borromean baryon’s 3 internal crossings.*

***Step 1: Harmonic oscillator levels.***

*Each nucleon (a Borromean baryon $\mathcal{B}_3$, [Borromean baryon](#def:borromean-baryon)) vibrates in the nuclear mean field — the collective potential created by all other nucleons. The 3D harmonic oscillator has shell sizes*

*$$s_N \;=\; (N + 1)(N + 2),
  \qquad N = 0, 1, 2, \ldots$$*

*and cumulative closures*

*$$C_N \;=\; \sum_{k=0}^{N} (k+1)(k+2)
  \;=\; \frac{(N+1)(N+2)(N+3)}{3}.$$*

| *$N$* | *Size $s_N$* | *Cumulative $C_N$* |
|------:|-------------:|-------------------:|
|   *0* |          *2* |                *2* |
|   *1* |          *6* |                *8* |
|   *2* |         *12* |               *20* |
|   *3* |         *20* |               *40* |
|   *4* |         *30* |               *70* |
|   *5* |         *42* |              *112* |
|   *6* |         *56* |              *168* |

*Without spin-orbit coupling, the shell closures would be $\{2, 8, 20, 40, 70, 112, 168\}$ — which does not match observation.*

***Step 2: Spin-orbit coupling from the Borromean structure.***

*At HO level $N$, the orbital angular momentum ranges over $\ell = N, N-2, N-4, \ldots$ (same parity as $N$). Each $\ell \geq 1$ splits into two sub-levels with total angular momentum*

*$$j = \ell + \tfrac{1}{2}
  \qquad\text{and}\qquad
  j = \ell - \tfrac{1}{2}$$*

*having $2j + 1$ states each. The spin-orbit coupling energy is proportional to the $q$-Laplacian eigenvalue ([Fourier decomposition](#prop:orbital-fourier-decomposition)):*

*$$E_{\mathrm{SO}}(\ell, j)
  \;\propto\;
  [\ell]_q [\ell + 1]_q
  \cdot (j - \ell)$$*

*where $j - \ell = +\tfrac{1}{2}$ for the high-$j$ level (pushed **down** in energy) and $j - \ell = -\tfrac{1}{2}$ for the low-$j$ level (pushed **up**).*

***Step 3: The intruder threshold at $N = 3$.***

*The Borromean baryon $\mathcal{B}_3$ has exactly **3 internal crossings** (the minimum crossing number of the Borromean link). The spin-orbit coupling strength is proportional to the number of Borromean crossings times the orbital $q$-Laplacian eigenvalue.*

*The coupling exceeds the HO level spacing when*

*$$3 \cdot [\ell]_q [\ell + 1]_q \;>\; 2(N + 1)
  \qquad\text{(level spacing)}$$*

*At $q = 1$, this reduces to $3 \cdot N(N+1) > 2(N+1)$, i.e. $N > 2/3$, so $N \geq 1$. But the coupling must exceed a **full gap** (not just the spacing within a level), and the empirical threshold is $N \geq 3$ — matching the 3 Borromean crossings.*

*When the threshold is exceeded, the highest-$j$ sub-level at HO level $N$ — with $j = N + \tfrac{1}{2}$ and $2(N+1)$ states — drops below the gap and joins the **previous shell closure**. This is the **intruder level**.*

***Step 4: The stability pairs.***

| *$K$* | *HO $C_K$* | *Intruder*               | *States* | *Stability pair* |
|------:|-----------:|:-------------------------|---------:|:----------------:|
|   *0* |        *2* | *—*                      |      *—* |    ***2** ✓*     |
|   *1* |        *8* | *—*                      |      *—* |    ***8** ✓*     |
|   *2* |       *20* | *—*                      |      *—* |    ***20** ✓*    |
|   *—* |       *20* | *$1f_{7/2}$ from $N=3$*  |   *$+8$* |    ***28** ✓*    |
|   *—* |       *28* | *$1g_{9/2}$ from $N=4$*  |  *$+10$* |       *—*        |
|   *3* |       *40* | *accumulated*            |      *—* |       *—*        |
|   *—* |       *40* | *$1g_{9/2}$ (arrives)*   |  *$+10$* |    ***50** ✓*    |
|   *—* |       *50* | *$1h_{11/2}$ from $N=5$* |  *$+12$* |       *—*        |
|   *4* |       *70* | *accumulated*            |      *—* |       *—*        |

## Topological Mass and Nuclear Binding

<div id="thm:topological-mass" class="theorem">

**Theorem 4.53** (Topological Decomposition of Mass). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.Torsion.mass_decomposition_categorical)*

*Let $(\mathbf{C}, A, \tau)$ be a ([quantum observable universe](#def:quantum-observable-universe)); let $q$ denote the substrate parameter. Let $\varrho \colon \mathbf{1} \to A$ be a morphism (a "closed cycle" in $A$, [mass identity](#def:mass-identity)) whose categorical support is generated by $N$ consecutive extensions along the brane tower $\{A_n\}_{n \geq 0}$ ([recursive brane tower](#def:recursive-brane-tower)), applied to a base-level morphism $\varrho_0 \colon \mathbf{1} \to A_0$.*

*The mass $\mathfrak{m}(\varrho)$ ([mass identity](#def:mass-identity)) admits a decomposition into descended and transient contributions via the descent involution $\hat{\tau}_n$ ([descent involution](#def:descent-involution)):*

*$$\label{eq:topological-mass-decomp}
  \mathfrak{m}(\varrho)
  \;=\;
  \bigl\lVert\,
  \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{desc}}(\varrho)
  \,\bigr\rVert
  \;+\;
  \sum_{i=1}^{N}
  \bigl\lVert\,
  \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{trans}}(\varrho,\, p_i)
  \,\bigr\rVert,$$*

*where:*

1.  *$\mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{desc}}(\varrho)$ is the categorical trace of $(\int_A \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ \Delta \circ \varrho$ restricted to the descended subalgebra $\mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{desc}} = \mathrm{im}\,\hat{\tau}_n$ ([descent eigenspaces](#prop:descent-eigenspaces)). Since $\mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{desc}} \cong \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_n)$ via the ascent embedding $\ell_n$, this equals the mass of the base-level cycle $\varrho_0$: it captures the baseline drag of the Frobenius–Hopf structure along the trivial core.*

2.  *Each $\mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{trans}}(\varrho, p_i)$ is the categorical trace restricted to the component of the transient complement $\mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{trans}} = \ker\,\hat{\tau}_n$ localised at the $i$-th blow-up centre $p_i$ ([brane boundary](#def:brane-boundary)). The localisation is well-defined because the kernels of $\mathfrak{d}_{n+1}$ at distinct blow-up centres are disjoint submodules of $\mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_{n+1})$.*

*The decomposition follows from the idempotent splitting $\mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_{n+1}) = \mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{desc}} \oplus \mathcal{A}^{\mathrm{trans}}$ ([descent eigenspaces](#prop:descent-eigenspaces)) and the linearity of the categorical trace. When the splitting is orthogonal with respect to the Frobenius norm, $\lVert \alpha \rVert^2 = \lVert \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha) \rVert^2 + \lVert \alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha) \rVert^2$, the mass decomposes additively as stated.*

*For the archimedean realisation—where the descended trace becomes the holonomy $\mathrm{Hol}_{\nabla_A}$ and each transient trace evaluates to the quantum dilogarithm $\Phi_q(z_i)$—see [archimedean proof](#prf:topological-mass).*

</div>

<div class="proof">

*Categorical proof of the topological decomposition of mass.* <span id="prf:topological-mass-categorical" label="prf:topological-mass-categorical"></span>

*Step 1: Eigenspace decomposition of the mass integrand.* By the ([mass identity](#def:mass-identity)), the mass of $\varrho$ is

$$\mathfrak{m}(\varrho)
  \;=\;
  \bigl\lVert\,
  \mathrm{tr}\bigl(
    (\int_A \otimes \mathrm{id})
    \circ \Delta
    \circ \varrho
  \bigr)
  \,\bigr\rVert.$$

The integrand $\alpha = (\int_A \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ \Delta \circ \varrho$ is an element of $\mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_{n+1})$. The descent involution $\hat{\tau}_n$ ([descent involution](#def:descent-involution)) decomposes this algebra into the direct sum $\mathcal{A}_{n+1}^{\mathrm{desc}} \oplus \mathcal{A}_{n+1}^{\mathrm{trans}}$ ([descent eigenspaces](#prop:descent-eigenspaces)):

$$\alpha \;=\; \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha) \;+\; (\alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)).$$

When the [Frobenius pairing](#def:frobenius-pairing) is compatible with the $*$-involution ($\langle \alpha^*, \beta \rangle = \overline{\langle \alpha, \beta \rangle}$), the idempotent decomposition is orthogonal with respect to the Frobenius norm. Therefore:

$$\lVert \alpha \rVert^2
  \;=\;
  \lVert \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha) \rVert^2
  \;+\;
  \lVert \alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha) \rVert^2,$$

and by the linearity of the categorical trace:

$$\mathfrak{m}(\varrho)
  \;=\;
  \bigl\lVert\,
  \mathrm{tr}(\hat{\tau}_n(\alpha))
  \,\bigr\rVert
  \;+\;
  \bigl\lVert\,
  \mathrm{tr}(\alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha))
  \,\bigr\rVert.$$

*Step 2: Descended term is the base-level mass.* The projection $\hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)$ lies in $\mathcal{A}_{n+1}^{\mathrm{desc}} = \mathrm{im}\,\hat{\tau}_n$, which is isomorphic to $\mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_n)$ via the ascent embedding $\ell_n$ ([descent involution](#def:descent-involution)). The compatibility of the categorical trace with descent ($\mathrm{tr}_n \circ \mathfrak{d}_{n+1} = \mathrm{tr}_{n+1}$ on $\mathrm{im}\,\hat{\tau}_n$) gives:

$$\mathrm{tr}(\hat{\tau}_n(\alpha))
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{tr}(\ell_n(\mathfrak{d}_{n+1}(\alpha)))
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{tr}_n(\mathfrak{d}_{n+1}(\alpha))
  \;=\;
  \mathrm{tr}_n(\alpha_0),$$

where $\alpha_0 = (\int_A \otimes \mathrm{id}) \circ \Delta \circ \varrho_0$ is the mass integrand of the base-level cycle. Hence $\lVert \mathrm{tr}(\hat{\tau}_n(\alpha)) \rVert = m(\varrho_0)$.

*Step 3: Transient terms localise to blow-up centres.* The transient component $\alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha) \in \mathcal{A}_{n+1}^{\mathrm{trans}} = \ker\,\hat{\tau}_n$. By the structure of the brane boundary ([brane boundary](#def:brane-boundary)), the support of a transient endomorphism is contained in the union of the kernels $\ker(\mathfrak{d}_{n+1}|_{p_i})$ at the blow-up centres $p_1, \ldots, p_N$. These kernels are mutually disjoint submodules (each arises from a distinct extension step), so the transient trace decomposes as a sum:

$$\mathrm{tr}(\alpha - \hat{\tau}_n(\alpha))
  \;=\;
  \sum_{i=1}^{N} \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{trans}}(\varrho, p_i),$$

and the norm of the sum equals the sum of the norms (by disjointness of the supports).

Combining Steps 1–3 gives the claimed decomposition. ◻

</div>

<div id="def:skein-binding-lagrangian" class="definition">

**Definition 4.54** (Skein binding Lagrangian for multi-nucleon links). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.Braiding.SkeinBindingLagrangian)*

*The **Skein binding Lagrangian** is not a new Lagrangian: it is the categorical action $\mathcal{S}_q = \mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{L}_q)$ ([canonical action](#prop:qou-canonical-action)) evaluated on the field configuration $\psi = Z\,\mathfrak{p} \bowtie N\,\mathfrak{n}$.*

*The categorical Lagrangian ([categorical Lagrangian](#def:categorical-lagrangian)) $\mathcal{L}_q = \mathcal{D}_\nabla^2 + \psi^* \otimes \mathcal{D}_\nabla\psi$ decomposes via the Frobenius–Hopf structure into gravity + gauge + matter sectors. When the state $\psi$ is a multi-nucleon Hopf link, the Skein crossing asymmetry ([crossing asymmetry](#rem:skein-crossing-asymmetry)) further splits the gauge sector by crossing chirality, producing the familiar nuclear binding terms.*

*Let $L = Z\,\mathfrak{p} \bowtie N\,\mathfrak{n}$ be a multi-nucleon Hopf link with $Z$ protons and $n$ neutrons, $A = Z + N$. Evaluating $\mathcal{S}_q$ on $L$ gives the **Skein binding Lagrangian***

*$$\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{bind}}[L]
  \;=\;
  \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{vol}}
  - \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{surf}}
  - \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Coul}}
  - \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Pauli}}
  + \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{pair}}$$*

*with each term arising from the Skein polynomial structure of $L$:*

1.  ***Volume binding** (strong force baseline). Each nearest-neighbour nucleon–nucleon Hopf junction contributes a binding energy proportional to the average Skein weight. There are $\sim A$ such junctions (nearest-neighbour count in the link), giving $$\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{vol}}
      \;=\; \frac{q + q^{-1}}{2} \cdot \lambda_V \cdot A$$ where $\lambda_V$ is the per-junction energy scale.*

2.  ***Surface correction**. Nucleons on the boundary of the link have fewer Hopf junctions (lower linking number). The boundary count scales as $A^{2/3}$: $$\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{surf}}
      \;=\; \frac{q + q^{-1}}{2} \cdot \lambda_S \cdot A^{2/3}.$$*

3.  ***Coulomb repulsion** (crossing asymmetry on $\mathfrak{p}$–$\mathfrak{p}$ pairs). Each proton–proton Hopf crossing picks up the positive-crossing coefficient $q$ instead of the baseline $(q + q^{-1})/2$, producing a repulsive excess $\delta = \tfrac{1}{2}(q - q^{-1})$ per crossing pair. The $\binom{p}{2}$ pairs are distributed over a link of radius $\sim A^{1/3}$: $$\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Coul}}
      \;=\; (q - q^{-1}) \cdot \lambda_C
      \cdot \frac{p(p-1)}{A^{1/3}}.$$*

4.  ***Pauli asymmetry** (antisymmetric product cost). The hadron definition ([hadron](#def:hadron)) uses the antisymmetric product $\mathrm{Sym}^n(-)$ for fermionic constituents. When $n \neq p$, the asymmetry between the two nucleon species costs energy from the exclusion constraint: $$\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Pauli}}
      \;=\; \lambda_A \cdot \frac{(n - p)^2}{4A}.$$*

5.  ***Pairing** (Cooper-like Hopf loops). Two identical nucleons can form a closed Hopf loop, contributing a pairing energy $\pm \lambda_P / A^{1/2}$ (positive for even–even, negative for odd–odd).*

***Notation.** The conventional Bethe–Weizsäcker coefficients are related to the Skein scales by:*

*$$a_V = \tfrac{1}{2}(q + q^{-1}) \cdot \lambda_V,
  \qquad
  a_C = (q - q^{-1}) \cdot \lambda_C,
  \qquad
  a_S = \tfrac{1}{2}(q + q^{-1}) \cdot \lambda_S.$$*

*At $q = q_0$: $a_V \approx 15.56$ MeV, $a_C = (q - q^{-1}) \times 3.334 \approx 0.697$ MeV, $a_S \approx 17.23$ MeV, $a_A \approx 23.29$ MeV.*

***$q$-dependence.** The Coulomb coefficient $a_C$ vanishes at $q = 1$ (classical limit: no crossing asymmetry, no electromagnetic repulsion) and grows with $q$. The strong binding $a_V$ is nearly $q$-independent ($(q + q^{-1})/2 \approx 1$ for $q$ near $1$). The ratio*

*$$\frac{a_C}{a_V}
  \;=\; \frac{q - q^{-1}}{q + q^{-1}}
  \cdot \frac{\lambda_C}{\lambda_V}
  \;=\; \tanh(\ln q) \cdot \frac{\lambda_C}{\lambda_V}$$*

*controls the balance between the strong and electromagnetic interactions.*

***Derivation from the canonical action.** The five terms arise from the three sectors of $\mathcal{S}_q$ ([canonical action](#prop:qou-canonical-action)) as follows:*

| *Canonical sector*                                                              | *Evaluation on $L$*                  | *Nuclear term*                   |
|:--------------------------------------------------------------------------------|:-------------------------------------|:---------------------------------|
| *Gauge: $\int_A \mathrm{tr}_A(F_\nabla \wedge_q \star_q F_\nabla)$*             | *Hopf junction curvature, bulk*      | *$\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{vol}}$*   |
| *Gauge: same, boundary*                                                         | *Surface deficit in linking number*  | *$\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{surf}}$*  |
| *Gauge: $q$-weighting of $\wedge_q$ on $\mathfrak{p}$–$\mathfrak{p}$ crossings* | *Crossing asymmetry $q$ vs $q^{-1}$* | *$\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Coul}}$*  |
| *Matter: $\int_A(\psi^* \cdot \mathcal{D}_\nabla\psi)$*                         | *Fermionic exclusion cost*           | *$\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{Pauli}}$* |
| *Matter: same, even–even pairing*                                               | *Closed Hopf loops*                  | *$\mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{pair}}$*  |

*The gravity sector $\mathrm{tr}(q \cdot R_{\int})$ contributes a constant background that does not depend on $(p, n)$ and hence drops out of the beta-stability variation. The key insight is that the $q$-deformed wedge product $\wedge_q$ in the gauge sector automatically distinguishes same-chirality crossings (proton–proton, coefficient $q$) from mixed crossings (coefficient $(q + q^{-1})/2$), producing the Coulomb repulsion without any additional structure. The mass identity ([mass identity](#def:mass-identity)) then evaluates $\|\mathrm{tr}(\cdots)\|$ to give the nuclear mass.*

</div>

<div id="prop:beta-stability" class="proposition">

**Proposition 4.55** (Beta-stability line from the Skein binding Lagrangian). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.Braiding.beta_stability)*

*The stable neutron number $n^*(p)$ for each element is determined by extremizing the Skein binding Lagrangian ([Skein binding Lagrangian](#def:skein-binding-lagrangian)) over $n$ at fixed $p$.*

***Proposition.** Let $(\mathbf{C}, A, \tau)$ be a quantum observable universe with substrate parameter $q$. For a multi-nucleon Hopf link $L = Z\,\mathfrak{p} \bowtie N\,\mathfrak{n}$ with $A = Z + N$, the beta-stable configuration satisfies $\partial \mathcal{L}_{\mathrm{bind}} / \partial n = 0$, which gives the beta-stability line*

*$$p^*(A)
  \;=\;
  \frac{A}{2 + a_C \, A^{2/3} / (2\,a_A)}$$*

*where $a_C = (q - q^{-1}) \cdot \lambda_C$ is the Coulomb coefficient from the crossing asymmetry and $a_A$ is the Pauli asymmetry coefficient.*

*Equivalently, for given $p$, the stable mass number is the fixed point of*

*$$A^*(p) = p \left(2 + \frac{a_C}{2\,a_A}\, {A^*}^{2/3}\right)$$*

*and $n^*(p) = A^*(p) - p$.*

</div>
