# Models of QOUs

## Physical interpretation and the main result

<div id="def:q-yang-mills-levi" class="definition">

**Definition 5.1** ($q$-Weighted Yang–Mills–Levi functional). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.QYangMillsLevi)*

*Let $(\mathbf{C}, \theta, G, \mathcal{S})$ be an archimedean quantum observable universe with instanton connection $A$ and substrate parameter $q$ ([substrate parameter](#def:substrate-parameter)). The *$q$-weighted Yang–Mills–Levi functional* is*

*$$S_q[A, \theta]
  \;=\; \int_M q(p)\,\lVert F_A^+|_H \rVert^2\,
        \theta \wedge (d\theta)^n,$$*

*where $q(p) = 1 + \lvert\langle L_\theta, F_A^+\rangle\rvert(p)$ ([$\mathbb{C}$-substrate via Levi form](#rem:c-substrate-via-levi)).*

</div>

<div id="conj:yang-mills-mass-gap" class="conjecture">

**Conjecture 5.2** (Yang–Mills Existence and Mass Gap). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.Torsion.YangMillsMassGap)*

***Conjecture (Yang–Mills existence and mass gap, categorical formulation).** *Let $(\mathbf{C}, A, \tau)$ be a ([quantum observable universe](#def:quantum-observable-universe)) over a commutative ring $R$ with substrate parameter $q > 1$. Let $\nabla$ be a ([categorical connection](#def:categorical-connection)) on the Frobenius–Hopf object $A$ with curvature $F_\nabla = \nabla^2$, and let $S_q[\nabla]$ be the ([$q$-weighted Yang–Mills–Levi functional](#def:q-yang-mills-levi)). Let $\Omega_0 \colon R \to \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A)$ be the ([vacuum state](#prop:vacuum-state)) — the unique $G_q$-invariant functional on the direct limit algebra $\mathcal{A}_\infty = \varinjlim \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_n)$.**

**Then:**

1.  ***Existence.** *There exists a connection $\nabla$ that is a critical point of $S_q[\nabla]$ (a categorical Yang–Mills connection), and the vacuum state $\Omega_0$ extends to a positive-definite sesquilinear form on the Hilbert completion $\overline{\mathcal{A}_\infty}$, defining a physical Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}_q$.**

2.  ***Mass gap.** *Every non-vacuum excitation $\varrho \colon \mathbf{1} \to A$ in the spectrum of the categorical transfer matrix $\mathcal{T}_q \colon \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_n)
    \to \mathrm{End}_{\mathbf{C}}(A_n)$ satisfies**

*$$\mathfrak{m}(\varrho) \;\geq\; \Delta_q \;>\; 0,$$*

**where $\mathfrak{m}(\varrho)$ is the categorical mass ([mass identity](#def:mass-identity)) and $\Delta_q$ is a strictly positive constant depending only on $q$ and the Frobenius–Hopf structure of $A$. Equivalently, the two-point function**

*$$\bigl\langle\,
  \tau(\varrho(t))\,,\;
  \tau(\varrho(0))
  \,\bigr\rangle_{\Omega_0}
  \;\sim\;
  \sum_{n \geq 0}
  A_n \exp\!\bigl(-\Delta_n\, t\bigr)
  \qquad (t \to \infty)$$*

**has $\Delta_0 = \Delta_q > 0$: there is no massless excitation above the vacuum.**

***Translation from the classical problem.** The classical Yang–Mills millennium problem asks for the existence of a quantum Yang–Mills theory on $\mathbb{R}^4$ with compact simple gauge group $G$, satisfying the Wightman axioms, and having a strictly positive mass gap $\Delta > 0$ in the energy spectrum.*

*In the QOU framework, the translation is:*

| *Classical (Wightman)*                               | *Categorical (QOU)*                                                                     |
|:-----------------------------------------------------|:----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------|
| *$\mathbb{R}^4$ spacetime*                           | *Brane tower $\{A_n\}$ over the Frobenius–Hopf object $A$*                              |
| *Gauge group $G$*                                    | *Quantum gauge group $G_q = \mathrm{Aut}_{\mathrm{Hopf}}(A)$*                           |
| *Yang–Mills action $\int \lVert F_A \rVert^2$*       | *$q$-weighted functional $S_q[\nabla, \theta]$ ([def](#def:q-yang-mills-levi))*         |
| *Vacuum state $\Omega$*                              | *Frobenius trace $\Omega_0$ ([vacuum state](#prop:vacuum-state))*                       |
| *Wightman axioms*                                    | *QOU axioms (QOU1)–(QOU5)*                                                              |
| *Hamiltonian $H$*                                    | *Categorical transfer matrix $\mathcal{T}_q$*                                           |
| *Mass gap $\Delta > 0$*                              | *$\inf_{\varrho \neq 0}\, \mathfrak{m}(\varrho) = \Delta_q > 0$*                        |
| *Two-point function $\langle \phi(t)\phi(0)\rangle$* | *Frobenius pairing $\langle \tau(\varrho(t)),\, \tau(\varrho(0))\rangle_{\Omega_0}$*    |
| *Lightest glueball mass*                             | *Categorical mass of the simplest non-trivial vortex $\varrho \colon \mathbf{1} \to A$* |

***Why the categorical setting is natural.** The mass gap is a topological consequence of the Frobenius–Hopf structure: the categorical mass $\mathfrak{m}(\varrho)$ is computed via the trace-norm through the comultiplication $\Delta$, and the topological decomposition ([topological mass](#thm:topological-mass)) shows that every non-trivial vortex acquires at least one crossing energy $\mathbf{E}_\times(q) = \tfrac{1}{2}(q - q^{-1}) > 0$ from the Skein relation. In particular, the mass gap is bounded below by the minimum crossing energy:*

*$$\Delta_q
  \;\geq\;
  \mathbf{E}_\times(q) \cdot (q - 1)^2
  \;=\;
  \tfrac{1}{2}(q - q^{-1})(q - 1)^2
  \;>\; 0
  \quad\text{for all } q > 1.$$*

*The positivity of $\Delta_q$ for $q > 1$ is the categorical shadow of confinement: the deformation parameter $q \neq 1$ breaks the classical conformal symmetry that would allow massless excitations, and the Skein relation forces every non-trivial braid word to carry strictly positive crossing energy.*

***The $\mathbb{G}_m$-torsion obstruction.** The mass gap is a regular function on $\mathbb{G}_m = \mathrm{Spec}\,\mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}]$ ([substrate as $\mathbb{G}_m$-section](#rem:substrate-gm-torsion)). It vanishes precisely on the 2-torsion subgroup $\mu_2 = \{1, -1\}$, and is strictly positive on the non-torsion locus $(1, \infty) \subset \mathbb{G}_m(\mathbb{R})$. The [not-root-of-unity axiom](#def:substrate-parameter) ensures $q \notin \mu_\infty$, placing the substrate parameter in the region where the gap is positive.*

*The [Kummer filtration](#rem:kummer-filtration-obstruction) of the obstruction space $H^2(\mathcal{S}, \mathbb{G}_m)$ provides the common algebraic framework: the mass gap and the [classical limit obstruction](#def:classical-limit-obstruction) both reduce to divisibility of $\chi(A)$ in the Kummer tower. Since $\chi(A) = -6$ for the Descartes universe, the [obstruction is one-dimensional](#thm:qou-obstruction-reduction) and persists at all primes $> 3$.*

***Relation to confinement.** In the archimedean realisation, the mass gap implies that the lightest glueball (the simplest non-trivial closed vortex $\varrho \colon \mathbf{1} \to A$ with no quark endpoints) has mass $\mathfrak{m}_{\mathrm{glue}} \geq \Delta_q > 0$. Since isolated colour charges would require a vortex of infinite length (and hence infinite mass), confinement follows: all finite-energy excitations are colour singlets.*

</div>

<div id="rem:gr-substrate-geometry" class="remark">

**Remark 5.3** (General Relativity as the Substrate Geometry).

*In this model the metric is effectively replaced by the Levi form $L_\theta$ and its coupling to the gauge curvature $F_A$. Gravity is expressed through the *Variational Bicomplex* — the double complex $(\Omega^{p,q}(J^\infty E), d_H, d_V)$ on the infinite jet bundle, where $d_H$ differentiates along the base $M$ and $d_V$ along the fibre — as the back-reaction of the gauge fields on the CR manifold $M$.*

*Variation of $S_q$ ([$q$-Yang–Mills–Levi functional](#def:q-yang-mills-levi)) with respect to the Levi form $L_\theta$ yields field equations of the schematic form*

*$$\frac{\delta S_q}{\delta L_\theta}
  \;=\; 0
  \qquad\Longrightarrow\qquad
  \mathrm{Ric}_{g_\theta} \;=\; T^{(q)},$$*

*where $\mathrm{Ric}_{g_\theta}$ is the Webster Ricci curvature and $T^{(q)}$ is a $q$-weighted stress-energy $2$-tensor on $H$ (both coordinate-free objects). The geometry of $M$ is forced to curve to accommodate the tension of the $\mathrm{SU}(2)$ instantons.*

</div>

<div id="prop:main-commutative-diagram" class="proposition">

**Proposition 5.4** (Main Commutative Diagram). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.main_commutative_diagram)*

*Let $(\mathbf{C}, \theta, G, \mathcal{S})$ be an archimedean quantum observable universe with instanton connection $A$ ([instanton](#ex:instanton)) and substrate parameter $q$ ([substrate parameter](#def:substrate-parameter)). Let $\mathbf{E}$ denote the Euler–Lagrange operator of the $q$-weighted Yang–Mills–Levi functional $S_q$ ([$q$-Yang–Mills–Levi functional](#def:q-yang-mills-levi)), and let $\nabla^A$ denote parallel transport along $A$. The following diagram commutes:*

*$$\begin{tikzcd}[row sep=2.5em, column sep=2.5em]
  J^1\mathcal{S}
    \ar[r, "{\mathbf{E}[S_q]}"]
    \ar[d, "\text{jet evaluation}"']
  & \bigl\{ L_\theta : \mathrm{Ric}_{g_\theta} = T^{(q)} \bigr\}
    \ar[d, "{q = 1 + \lvert\langle L_\theta, F_A^+\rangle\rvert}"]
  \\
  \Gamma(\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{lin}})
    \ar[r, "\nabla^A"']
  & \bigl\{ \psi : J\hbar_q\,\iota_{\xi_q}D_A\psi = \hat{H}_q\psi \bigr\}
\end{tikzcd}$$*

*where the top row sends a jet (a first-order perturbation of the gauge field) to the Einstein-type field equation via the Euler–Lagrange operator; the left column evaluates a jet at a fibre point to produce a linearised section; the right column is the coupling through the substrate field $q$; and the bottom row is the parallel-transport equation whose linearisation is the Schrödinger equation.*

</div>

<div class="proof">

*Proof of Main Commutative Diagram.* <span id="prf:main-commutative-diagram" label="prf:main-commutative-diagram"></span> [<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.main_commutative_diagram)

We verify commutativity by tracing both paths around the diagram.

**Top-right path** (variational → coupling). The Euler–Lagrange operator $\mathbf{E}[S_q]$ applied to a jet $j^1_p \sigma$ yields the variational equation $\mathrm{Ric}_{g_\theta} = T^{(q)}$ ([GR substrate geometry](#rem:gr-substrate-geometry)). Solving for $L_\theta$ determines the Webster metric, which in turn fixes the substrate field via the coupling $q(p) = 1 + \lvert\langle L_\theta, F_A^+\rangle\rvert$. This determines $\hbar_q = 1 - q^{-1}$, the $q$-Reeb field $\xi_q$, and the $q$-Hamiltonian $\hat{H}_q = -\tfrac{1}{2}\hbar_q\,\Delta_q + V_q$ appearing in the transport equation.

**Left-bottom path** (evaluation → transport). The jet evaluation map $j^1_p \sigma \mapsto \sigma(p)$ produces a section $\psi \in \Gamma(\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{lin}})$ by linearising the fibre $\mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C})$ at the chosen base-point. Parallel transport along $A$ then imposes $J\hbar_q\,\iota_{\xi_q} D_A\psi = \hat{H}_q\psi$ ([Schrödinger equation](#rem:schrodinger-jet-coaction)).

**Commutativity.** Both paths share the same input ($j^1_p \sigma$) and the same output (a section $\psi$ satisfying the transport equation at substrate parameter $q$). The key identity is that the chain rule for the composite $S_q[\nabla, L_\theta, \psi]$ factorises the variation into two coupled equations:

1.  $\delta S_q / \delta L_\theta = 0$ determines $L_\theta$ (hence $q$ and $\hat{H}_q$) — this is the top row;

2.  $\delta S_q / \delta \psi = 0$ gives $D_\nabla\psi = 0$ ([variational equations](#prop:variational-equations), Item 3) — this is the bottom row.

The coupling $q = 1 + \lvert\langle L_\theta, F_A^+\rangle\rvert$ ensures that the $q$ appearing in the top-right path equals the $q$ in the left-bottom path. Non-degeneracy of $\int_A$ ([Frobenius pairing](#def:frobenius-pairing)) guarantees that the solution sets agree: solving for $L_\theta$ first and then substituting into the transport equation yields the same $\psi$ as evaluating the jet and transporting along $A$. ◻

</div>

## Archimedean specialisations

<div id="ex:calabi-yau" class="example">

**Example 5.5** (Real hypersurface in a Calabi–Yau $2$-fold).

*Let $X$ be a Calabi–Yau $2$-fold (K3 surface) with holonomy $\mathrm{SU}(2)$, and let $M \subset X$ be a smooth, strictly convex real hypersurface. Then $M$ is a $3$-dimensional strictly pseudoconvex CR manifold inheriting its CR structure from the ambient Kähler geometry. The frame bundle of $X$ restricted to $M$ yields a natural principal $\mathrm{SU}(2)$-bundle $P \to M$. The associated state bundle $\mathcal{S} = P \times_G \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C})$ yields an archimedean quantum observable universe $(\mathbf{C}, \theta, G, \mathcal{S})$ ([$\mathbb{C}$-quantum observable universe](#ex:c-quantum-observable-universe)).*

*The K3 surface carries a hyper-Kähler structure, so $M$ inherits a natural contact form $\theta$ from the Kähler potential. The Reeb vector field $\xi$ ([Reeb decomposition](#ex:reeb-decomposition)) is the restriction of the Hamiltonian vector field of the Kähler potential to $M$, and the weight decomposition ([weight decomposition](#def:weight-decomposition)) is the splitting induced by the hyper-Kähler triple $(\omega_I, \omega_J, \omega_K)$ restricted to forms on $M$.*

*The instanton condition ([categorical instanton](#def:categorical-instanton)) specialises to the anti-self-duality equation $F_A^+ = 0$ on $X$, whose moduli space is the classical moduli of instantons on a K3 surface. The substrate parameter $q(p)$ ([substrate parameter](#def:substrate-parameter)) interpolates between this instanton connection and the Reeb component.*

*This example connects the QOU to the large body of results on gauge theory over hyper-Kähler $4$-manifolds, and shows that standard instanton moduli problems arise as special cases of the categorical framework.*

</div>

<div id="ex:ale" class="example">

**Example 5.6** (ALE links).

*Let $\Gamma \subset \mathrm{SU}(2)$ be a finite subgroup and let $X$ be the minimal resolution of $\mathbb{C}^2 / \Gamma$. The link $M = S^3 / \Gamma$ is a compact $3$-dimensional strictly pseudoconvex CR manifold. The Reeb vector field $\xi$ generates the Hopf-type fibration $S^3/\Gamma \to S^2$. Equipped with the induced principal $\mathrm{SU}(2)$-bundle $P \to M$ and state bundle $\mathcal{S} = P \times_G \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C})$, the tuple $(\mathbf{C}, \theta, G, \mathcal{S})$ provides an archimedean quantum observable universe ([$\mathbb{C}$-quantum observable universe](#ex:c-quantum-observable-universe)).*

*The McKay correspondence classifies finite subgroups $\Gamma$ by ADE Dynkin diagrams. In each case the exceptional divisors of the resolution $X \to \mathbb{C}^2/\Gamma$ are $\mathbb{CP}^1$’s arranged in the corresponding Dynkin pattern. The substrate parameter $q$ ([substrate parameter](#def:substrate-parameter)) is constant on $M = S^3/\Gamma$ (the link has a single connected component), and the weight decomposition ([weight decomposition](#def:weight-decomposition)) inherits the $\Gamma$-equivariant splitting of forms on $S^3$. The Reeb decomposition ([Reeb decomposition](#ex:reeb-decomposition)) specialises to the Hopf fibration $S^3/\Gamma \to S^2$, with the Reeb vector $\xi$ generating the $\mathrm{U}(1)$ fibre rotation.*

*The ADE classification thus provides a discrete family of quantum observable universes, one for each Dynkin type ($A_n$, $D_n$, $E_6$, $E_7$, $E_8$), with the instanton moduli space on $X$ furnishing the connection data.*

</div>

<div id="ex:brings-surface" class="example">

**Example 5.7** (Bring’s surface unit circle bundle).

*Let $S$ denote Bring’s surface (genus $4$, $\chi = -6$). The CR geometry lives on the unit circle bundle $M_S \subset T^*S$: the Liouville $1$-form restricts to a contact form $\theta$ on $M_S$. The natural projection $\pi \colon S \to \mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C})$ (degree-$4$ branched covering with $6$ branch points) lifts to a principal $\mathrm{SU}(2)$-bundle $P \to M_S$, giving an archimedean QOU $(\mathbf{C}, \theta, G, \mathcal{S})$.*

</div>

<div id="ex:cosmological-limits" class="example">

**Example 5.8** (Cosmological limits of $q$).

***Conjectural interpretation.** Consider $M = S^3$ with the standard contact form $\theta$ and the standard instanton on the Hopf bundle. As the instanton curvature concentrates near a point $p_0 \in S^3$, the substrate field $q$ is expected to exhibit two simultaneous regimes:*

- **Near $p_0$* ($q(p) \to \infty$, $\hbar_q \to 1$): maximal uncertainty $[\hat{X},\hat{P}]_q \to J$. All observables become maximally non-commutative; the Frobenius form degenerates as $\int_A(f^* f) \sim q^{-1} \to 0$. This is the *"big bang" regime*: the quantum observable universe becomes fully quantum-mechanical, with no classical shadow.*

- **Away from $p_0$* ($q(p) \to 1$, $\hbar_q \to 0$): $[\hat{X}, \hat{P}]_q \to 0$ and the Hopf algebra becomes cocommutative ($\sigma \circ \Delta = \Delta$, [Hopf non-cocommutativity](#rem:hopf-non-cocommutativity)). Observations commute, the $q$-deformed operators reduce to classical ones, and the transport equation becomes the classical parallel transport $\nabla\psi = 0$. This is the *"heat death" regime*: a fully classical, frozen universe.*

*At both limits the QOU structure *degenerates*:*

- *At $q \to \infty$: the [Frobenius pairing](#def:frobenius-pairing) $\langle f, g \rangle = \int_A(\mu(f \otimes g))$ loses non-degeneracy (axiom (1) of [quantum observable universe](#def:quantum-observable-universe) fails), so the QOU ceases to be observable.*

- *At $q \to 1$: the $q$-Hodge star $\star_q \to \star_1$ and the deformation collapses; the quantum gauge group $\mathrm{SU}_q(2) \to \mathrm{SU}(2)$ becomes a classical group, and the substrate parameter carries no information.*

*The physically meaningful regime is conjectured to be $1 < q < \infty$, where both quantum and classical features coexist. A rigorous analysis of these limiting regimes requires control over the singular behaviour of the Frobenius form as $q \to \infty$, which remains an open problem.*

</div>

<div id="ex:instanton" class="example">

**Example 5.9** (Instanton connection). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.InstantonConnection)*

*In the archimedean quantum universe ([$\mathbb{C}$-quantum universe](#ex:c-quantum-universe)), a ([categorical instanton](#def:categorical-instanton)) specialises to an *instanton connection* on $P$: a connection $A$ whose curvature $F_A$, restricted to $H = \ker\theta$, is self-dual: $F_A|_H = {*_H}\,F_A|_H$. The $q$-Hodge star $\star_q$ specialises to the Webster Hodge star $*_H$ on $\Lambda^2 H^*$, and $\star_q$-self-duality becomes $*_H$-self-duality.*

</div>

<div id="ex:irreducible-connection" class="example">

**Example 5.10** (Irreducibility of the connection). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.irreducible_connection)*

*In an archimedean quantum observable universe, [categorical irreducible](#lem:categorical-irreducible) specialises as follows: every instanton connection $A$ on $P$ is irreducible. The vanishing $H^0(M, \mathrm{Ad}(P)) = 0$ ([$\mathbb{C}$-quantum observable universe](#ex:c-quantum-observable-universe)) is the archimedean instance of $\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbf{C}}(\mathbf{1}, \mathrm{Ad}(A)) = 0$. Concretely: a non-zero section $s \in H^0(M, \mathrm{Ad}(P))$ would furnish an $\mathrm{Ad}$-invariant direction in $\mathfrak{su}(2)$ at every point, reducing the connection to $\mathrm{U}(1)$. The QOU vanishing axiom forbids this, forcing the gauge orbit of $A$ to be free.*

</div>

<div id="ex:self-dual-curvature" class="example">

**Example 5.11** (Self-duality of the curvature). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.self_dual_curvature)*

*In an archimedean quantum observable universe with $\dim_{\mathbb{R}} H = 4$, [categorical self duality](#prop:categorical-self-duality) specialises: every instanton connection $A$ on $P$ satisfies $F_A|_H = {*_H}\,F_A|_H$. The categorical Yang–Mills functional $\int_A(\star_q(F_\nabla) \cdot F_\nabla)$ specialises to $\int_M \lVert F_A|_H \rVert^2\,\theta \wedge (d\theta)^2$. The Bogomolny trick decomposes $\lVert F_A|_H \rVert^2 = \lVert F_A^+ \rVert^2 + \lVert F_A^- \rVert^2$; since $\int \lVert F_A^+ \rVert^2$ is a topological invariant (the second Chern number $c_2(P)$), minimising the Yang–Mills functional forces $F_A^-|_H = 0$.*

</div>

<div id="rem:c-substrate-via-levi" class="remark">

**Remark 5.12** (Archimedean substrate via the Levi form).

*Let $A$ be an instanton connection on $P$ ([instanton](#def:instanton)), $F_A^+$ its self-dual curvature ([self-dual curvature](#ex:self-dual-curvature)), and $L_\theta(V, W) = -i\,d\theta(V, \bar{W})$ the Levi form. Since $\Lambda^{1,1} H^* \subset \Lambda^+ H^*$ on the $4$-dimensional distribution $H$, the Webster metric and Killing form yield a natural contraction $\langle L_\theta, F_A^+\rangle_p \in \mathbb{R}$. The categorical ([substrate parameter](#def:substrate-parameter)) specialises in the archimedean realisation to the smooth field*

*$$q(p) = 1 + \bigl\lvert\langle L_\theta,\, F_A^+ \rangle\bigr\rvert(p),
  \qquad p \in M,$$*

*with $q = 1$ at classicality ($F_A^+ = 0$) and $q \to \infty$ in the deep-quantum regime. All downstream formulas ($\hbar_q$, commutators, Yang–Mills) are algebraic in $q$, so the formula $1 + x$ may equally be replaced by $\exp(x)$ without affecting the theory; the algebraic form is preferred because it is meaningful over every base ring $R$. Non-archimedean analogues appear in [Chapter](#chap:descartes-universe).*

</div>

We denote the inner product induced by the Webster metric $g_\theta$ on the horizontal distribution $H = \ker\theta$ and its exterior powers as $\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle_\theta$. For vector fields $X, Y$ and differential forms $\alpha, \beta$:

$$\langle X, Y \rangle_\theta := g_\theta(X, Y),
  \qquad
  \langle \alpha, \beta \rangle_\theta := g_\theta(\alpha^{\sharp}, \beta^{\sharp}).$$

This notation makes several dualities visually transparent:

- **Reeb duality.** The Reeb vector field $\xi$ is the metric dual to the contact form $\theta$: $\theta(X) = \langle \xi, X \rangle_\theta$ for all $X$.

- **Adjoint definition.** The $q$-codifferential $\delta_q$ is uniquely characterised by $\langle d_q\,\alpha, \beta \rangle_\theta = \langle \alpha, \delta_q\,\beta \rangle_\theta$.

- **Substrate contraction.** The natural contraction $\langle L_\theta, F_A^+ \rangle$ appearing in the substrate parameter ([substrate parameter](#def:substrate-parameter)) is exactly the inner product $\langle \cdot, \cdot \rangle_\theta$ extended to bundle-valued $2$-forms.

<div id="prop:heisenberg-commutator" class="proposition">

**Proposition 5.13** ($q$-deformed Heisenberg commutator from the Reeb fibre). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.DescartesUniverse.heisenberg_commutator)*

*Let $\hat{X}, \hat{P}$ be position and momentum observables on the fibre $\mathbb{P}^1(\mathbb{C})$, let $J \colon H \to H$ be the complex structure on the Levi distribution ($J^2 = -\mathrm{Id}$), and let $q \in \mathrm{End}(\mathbf{1})$ be the substrate parameter ([substrate parameter](#def:substrate-parameter)). Then the $q$-deformed commutator is*

*$$[\hat{X},\, \hat{P}]_q \;=\; J\,\hbar_q(p),
  \qquad
  \hbar_q(p) \;=\; 1 - q(p)^{-1},$$*

*where $\hbar_q$ is the quantum Planck constant ([quantum Planck constant](#def:quantum-planck-constant)). In particular:*

1.  *As $q \to 1$, $[\hat{X}, \hat{P}]_q \to 0$ (classical limit).*

2.  *As $q \to \infty$, $[\hat{X}, \hat{P}]_q \to J$ (maximal uncertainty).*

</div>

<div id="ex:reeb-decomposition" class="example">

**Example 5.14** (Reeb decomposition). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.ReebDecomposition)*

*In the archimedean realisation ([$\mathbb{C}$-quantum universe](#ex:c-quantum-universe)), the categorical weight decomposition ([weight decomposition](#def:weight-decomposition)) specialises to the *Reeb decomposition*. Let $\xi$ denote the *Reeb vector field*, characterised by $\iota_\xi\,d\theta = 0$ and $\theta(\xi) = 1$. Every differential $k$-form $\alpha$ ($k \geq 1$) on $M$ decomposes uniquely as*

*$$\alpha = \alpha_H + \theta \wedge \iota_\xi\,\alpha,$$*

*where $\alpha_H := \alpha - \theta \wedge \iota_\xi\,\alpha$ is the *horizontal component* ($\iota_\xi\,\alpha_H = 0$) and $\alpha_V := \theta \wedge \iota_\xi\,\alpha$ is the *vertical component*. The Reeb vector $\xi$ generates the $\mathrm{U}(1)$-action (the maximal torus, [maximal torus](#def:maximal-torus)), and the weight-$0$ subspace is the horizontal distribution $H = \ker\theta$.*

</div>

<div id="def:spatial-realization-functor" class="definition">

**Definition 5.15** (Spatial realization functor). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.SpatialRealizationFunctor)*

*Let $(\mathbf{C}, A, \tau)$ be a quantum observable universe ([quantum observable universe](#def:quantum-observable-universe)). The *spatial realization* of $A$ is the space*

*$$M = \mathrm{Spec}(A) = \{ p \colon \mathbf{1} \to A \mid
  p \text{ is a categorical point} \}$$*

*([categorical point](#def:categorical-point)), equipped with the following structures derived purely within $\mathbf{C}$:*

1.  ***Local germs.** For each point $p$, the *augmentation ideal* $\mathfrak{m}_p = \ker(p^* \colon A \to \mathbf{1})$ captures the functions vanishing at $p$. The quotient $\mathfrak{m}_p / \mathfrak{m}_p^2$ is functorially dual to the tangent space $T_p M$, giving the first-order germ decomposition $$A / \mathfrak{m}_p^2
      \;\cong\;
      \mathbf{1} \oplus \mathfrak{m}_p / \mathfrak{m}_p^2.$$*

2.  ***Kähler differentials.** The module $\Omega^1(A)$ of Kähler differentials exists in $\mathbf{C}$ by hypothesis. Under the fibre functor, $\tau(\Omega^1(A))$ maps to sections of the cotangent bundle $\Gamma(T^* M)$.*

3.  ***The contact form.** The Frobenius form $\int_A \colon A \to \mathbf{1}$ ([Frobenius pairing](#def:frobenius-pairing)) induces a canonical $1$-form $\theta_A \in \Omega^1(A)$ via pullback along the universal derivation $d \colon A \to \Omega^1(A)$.*

4.  ***The Reeb derivation.** The generator $\xi$ of the maximal torus action ([categorical Reeb](#def:categorical-reeb)) satisfies the Cartan relations $\iota_\xi \theta_A = \mathrm{id}_{\mathbf{1}}$ and $\iota_\xi\,d\theta_A = 0$ within the non-commutative differential calculus.*

*$$\label{eq:spatial-realization-diagram}
\begin{tikzcd}[row sep=2.5em, column sep=3em]
  A \ar[r, "\tau"] \ar[d, "d"']
  & C^{\infty}(M) \ar[d, "d"] \\
  \Omega^1(A) \ar[r, "\tau"']
  & \Gamma(T^* M)
\end{tikzcd}
\qquad
\begin{tikzcd}[row sep=2.5em, column sep=3em]
  \theta_A \ar[r, mapsto, "\tau"]
  & \theta \\
  \xi \ar[r, mapsto, "\tau"']
  & \xi_{\mathrm{Reeb}}
\end{tikzcd}
\qquad\text{(spatial realisation)}$$*

*Under $\tau$, these algebraic objects map to their geometric counterparts: $\theta_A$ becomes the global contact $1$-form $\theta$, $\xi$ becomes the Reeb vector field, and non-degeneracy of $\int_A$ guarantees that $d\theta$ is maximally non-degenerate on $\ker\theta$ — the defining property of a contact manifold.*

</div>

<div id="prop:categorical-archimedean-bridge" class="proposition">

**Proposition 5.16** (Categorical–geometric correspondence). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.categorical_archimedean_bridge)*

*Let $(\mathbf{C}, A, \tau)$ be a quantum observable universe with weight decomposition $\pi_H, \pi_V$ ([weight decomposition](#def:weight-decomposition)) and categorical $q$-exterior derivative $d_q$ ([categorical $q$-exterior derivative](#def:categorical-q-ext-deriv)). Under the fibre functor $\tau$, the categorical and geometric formulations of $d_q$ coincide:*

*$$\label{eq:categorical-archimedean-bridge-diagram}
\begin{tikzcd}[row sep=2.5em, column sep=3em]
  \Omega^k(A) \ar[r, "\pi_V \circ d"] \ar[d, "\tau"']
  & \Omega^{k+1}(A) \ar[d, "\tau"] \\
  \Omega^k(M) \ar[r, "\theta \wedge \mathcal{L}_\xi"']
  & \Omega^{k+1}(M)
\end{tikzcd}
\qquad\text{(categorical--geometric bridge)}$$*

*That is, $\tau(\pi_V \circ d) = \theta \wedge \mathcal{L}_\xi$, where $\theta$ is the contact form and $\mathcal{L}_\xi$ is the Lie derivative along the Reeb vector field.*

</div>

<div class="proof">

*Proof.* <span id="prf:categorical-archimedean-bridge" label="prf:categorical-archimedean-bridge"></span> The fibre functor $\tau$ maps:

- the Frobenius form $\int_A$ to the contact integral $\int_M \alpha \wedge (d\theta)^n$,

- the maximal torus generator $\xi$ to the Reeb vector field satisfying $\iota_\xi\theta = 1$ and $\iota_\xi\,d\theta = 0$,

- the weight decomposition $\pi_H, \pi_V$ to the splitting $\Omega^k(M) = \Omega^k_H(M) \oplus \theta \wedge \Omega^{k-1}_H(M)$ induced by the Reeb direction.

For a form $\alpha \in \Omega^k(M)$, the vertical projection $\pi_V(d\alpha)$ extracts the component of $d\alpha$ carrying non-zero weight under the $T$-action. In the geometric realisation, the $T$-action is the Reeb flow $\phi_t \colon M \to M$, whose infinitesimal generator is $\mathcal{L}_\xi$. The non-zero-weight part of $d\alpha$ is precisely the component along the Reeb direction:

$$\pi_V(d\alpha) = \theta \wedge \iota_\xi(d\alpha)
  = \theta \wedge (\mathcal{L}_\xi\alpha - d(\iota_\xi\alpha)).$$

On horizontal forms ($\iota_\xi\alpha = 0$), this reduces to $\theta \wedge \mathcal{L}_\xi\alpha$. For general forms, writing $\alpha = \alpha_H + \theta \wedge \beta$ and using $\mathcal{L}_\xi\theta = 0$, we obtain $\pi_V(d\alpha) = \theta \wedge \mathcal{L}_\xi\alpha$ in all cases. Therefore

$$\tau(d_q) = q^{-1} d + (1 - q^{-1})\,\theta \wedge
  \mathcal{L}_\xi,$$

which is precisely the archimedean formula for $d_q$ ([archimedean $q$-exterior derivative](#ex:q-ext-deriv)). ◻

</div>

## $\mathbb{C}_\mathfrak{p}$ Quantum Universe

## Lifting via Formal Groups and Witt Vectors

The $\mathbb{Q}_\mathfrak{p}$ realisation ([$p$-adic realisation](#ex:p-adic-realisation)) provides a QOU over characteristic $0$, while the $\mathbb{F}_\mathfrak{p}$ realisation ([finite field realisation](#ex:finite-field-realisation)) provides one over characteristic $\mathfrak{p}$. The passage between them is mediated by the *Witt vector functor* $W$ and the theory of formal groups over $\mathfrak{p}$-adic rings.

<div id="def:witt-vector-lift" class="definition">

**Definition 5.17** (Witt vector lift of a formal group). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.WittVectorLift) Let $H$ be a commutative formal group over $\mathbb{F}_\mathfrak{p}$ equipped with a skewed-Poisson structure $\pi_<$ (a biderivation $\pi_<\colon\mathcal{O}(H)\otimes\mathcal{O}(H)\to\mathcal{O}(H)$ satisfying a graded anti-symmetry and a $\mathfrak{p}$-truncated Jacobi condition). The *Witt vector lift* is the formal group $\widehat{G}$ over $W(\mathbb{F}_\mathfrak{p}) \cong \mathbb{Z}_\mathfrak{p}$ obtained by integrating $\pi_<$ in the sense of Fresse: the distribution algebra $\mathrm{Dist}(\widehat{G})$ is the $\mathfrak{p}$-adic completion of the universal enveloping algebra $\mathcal{U}(\mathrm{Lie}(H))$ deformed by $\pi_<$.*

</div>

<div id="prop:skew-poisson-integration" class="proposition">

**Proposition 5.18** (Integration of skewed-Poisson structures). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.Descartes.skew_poisson_integration)*

*Let $H/\mathbb{F}_\mathfrak{p}$ be a smooth commutative formal group and $\pi_<$ a skewed-Poisson structure on $H$. Then there exists a (generally non-commutative) formal group $G/\mathbb{Z}_\mathfrak{p}$ such that:*

1.  *$G \otimes_{\mathbb{Z}_\mathfrak{p}} \mathbb{F}_\mathfrak{p}\;\cong\; H$ (reduction modulo $\mathfrak{p}$ recovers $H$);*

2.  *$\mathrm{Dist}(G)$ is a deformation of $\mathrm{Dist}(H)$ computed via a Grobner–Shirshov basis for the relations of the enveloping algebra;*

3.  *the comultiplication on $\mathrm{Dist}(G)$ satisfies the *strong multiplicativity* condition: the Frobenius relation $(\mathrm{Id}\otimes m)\circ(\Delta\otimes\mathrm{Id}) = \Delta\circ m$ is preserved under the deformation.*

</div>

<div class="proof">

*Proof of Integration of skewed-Poisson structures.* <span id="prf:skew-poisson-integration" label="prf:skew-poisson-integration"></span>

This is the Main Theorem of Fresse. Item (1) is the existence statement; item (2) follows from the Grobner–Shirshov normal-form construction for $\mathrm{Dist}(G)$; item (3) is the strong multiplicativity theorem, which guarantees that the co-multiplication is compatible with the deformed product at every stage of the $\mathfrak{p}$-adic filtration. ◻

</div>
