*$$\delta q(p, n)
  \;=\;
  \frac{\ell_{\mathrm{net}}(p, n)}{A^2}
  \cdot \hbar_q^2$$*

*where $\hbar_q = 1 - q_0^{-1}$ is the quantum Planck constant and the net signed crossing number is*

*$$\ell_{\mathrm{net}}(p, n)
  \;=\;
  \binom{p}{2} - \binom{n}{2}
  \;=\;
  \frac{p(p-1) - n(n-1)}{2}.$$*

*For nuclei on the neutron-rich side of the valley ($n > p$), $\ell_{\mathrm{net}} < 0$ and the local $q$ is slightly *reduced*. For proton-rich nuclei, $\ell_{\mathrm{net}} > 0$ and $q$ is slightly increased.*

***Why the net signed crossing.** The $q$-deformed wedge product $\wedge_q$ in the gauge sector of the canonical action ([canonical action](#prop:qou-canonical-action)) assigns:*

- *weight $q$ to $\mathfrak{p}$–$\mathfrak{p}$ crossings (positive),*

- *weight $q^{-1}$ to $\mathfrak{n}$–$\mathfrak{n}$ crossings (negative),*

- *weight $(q + q^{-1})/2$ to $\mathfrak{p}$–$\mathfrak{n}$ crossings (neutral average).*

*The neutral crossings contribute symmetrically and do not shift $q$. Only the imbalance between positive and negative crossings deforms the substrate field. The normalization by $A^2$ (rather than $A$) reflects the linking *density*: the crossings occupy a volume $\propto A$, so the crossing density per unit volume is $\ell_{\mathrm{net}} / A^2$.*

***Magnitude.** At the substrate $q_0$: $\hbar_q \approx 0.0991$ and $\hbar_q^2 \approx 0.00982$. For representative nuclei:*

| *Nucleus*               | *$(p, n)$*    | *$A$* | *$\ell_{\mathrm{net}}$* | *$\delta q$* | *$\delta q / q_0$* |
|:------------------------|:--------------|:------|:------------------------|:-------------|:-------------------|
| *${}^{3}\mathrm{H}$*    | *$(1, 2)$*    | *3*   | *$-1$*                  | *$-0.0011$*  | *$-0.10\%$*        |
| *${}^{14}\mathrm{C}$*   | *$(6, 8)$*    | *14*  | *$-13$*                 | *$-0.0007$*  | *$-0.06\%$*        |
| *${}^{60}\mathrm{Co}$*  | *$(27, 33)$*  | *60*  | *$-177$*                | *$-0.0005$*  | *$-0.04\%$*        |
| *${}^{90}\mathrm{Sr}$*  | *$(38, 52)$*  | *90*  | *$-623$*                | *$-0.0008$*  | *$-0.07\%$*        |
| *${}^{137}\mathrm{Cs}$* | *$(55, 82)$*  | *137* | *$-1836$*               | *$-0.0010$*  | *$-0.09\%$*        |
| *${}^{210}\mathrm{Bi}$* | *$(83, 127)$* | *210* | *$-4598$*               | *$-0.0010$*  | *$-0.09\%$*        |

*The self-deformation is genuinely small ($|\delta q / q_0| < 0.1\%$ for all nuclei).*

***Effect on beta decay: the differential shift.** In beta decay, $A$ is fixed but $(p, n)$ changes by $(+1, -1)$. The *daughter* nucleus has a different self-deformation from the parent. The change in effective $q$ across the decay is*

*$$\Delta q_{\mathrm{eff}}
  \;=\;
  \delta q(p+1, n-1) - \delta q(p, n)
  \;=\;
  \frac{A - 1}{A^2} \cdot \hbar_q^2.$$*

*This is always positive: the daughter (with one more proton) has more positive crossings, hence a higher effective $q$. A higher $q$ means a larger crossing asymmetry and therefore a larger $\mathcal{Q}_q$-value ([transition energy](#def:q-value-transition)) than the background calculation predicts. Via the Sargent rule $f(\mathcal{Q}_q) \propto \mathcal{Q}_q^5$, the corrected $\mathcal{Q}_q$ increases the decay rate and *shortens* the half-life.*

***Note:** The $\Delta q_{\mathrm{eff}}$ shift is precisely the $q$-anomaly $\delta_q$ of the transition energy. The daughter is evaluated at the shifted $q + \Delta q_{\mathrm{eff}}$, not the background $q$. This is the $q$-deformed energy balance — not classical conservation.*

***Effect on the decay rate.** The differential shift $\Delta q_{\mathrm{eff}}$ modifies the effective substrate parameter at the converting nucleon. Since the decay rate depends on $q$ with sensitivity $\approx 48$ ([half-life regimes](#rem:hadron-half-life-regimes)), a shift of $\Delta q / q_0 \sim 0.1$–$0.4\%$ produces a measurable change in the decay rate.*

*For ${}^{3}\mathrm{H}$ ($A = 3$): $\Delta q_{\mathrm{eff}} = (2/9) \times \hbar_q^2 = 0.00218$, the largest correction. This is a categorical quantity: it follows from $q$, $A$, and the linking structure of the nuclear braid.*

***Universality.** The self-deformation applies to *every* equation where $q$ is evaluated on a specific hadron configuration — not just half-lives. The beta-stability line ([beta-stability](#prop:beta-stability)) and the topological mass formula all receive analogous corrections when $q_0$ is replaced by $q_{\mathrm{eff}}$.*

</div>

<div id="prop:skein-coulomb-enhancement" class="proposition">

**Proposition 9.55** (Coulomb enhancement from electron-proton Skein crossings). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.Descartes.skein_coulomb_enhancement)*

*The leading-order half-life formula ([hadron half-life](#prop:hadron-half-life)) evaluates the Skein polynomial on the **nucleus alone**, treating the emitted electron as a free particle. But the electron (trefoil $T_{2,3}$, [electron knot](#def:electron-knot)) passes through the Coulomb field of $Z$ protons on its way out of the nucleus, and each electron-proton crossing carries a Skein weight. Evaluating the Skein polynomial on the **full outgoing link** $T_{2,3} \cup \mathcal{N}(Z, N)$ gives the Coulomb enhancement.*

***Proposition.** Let $(\mathbf{C}, A, \tau)$ be a Descartes universe with substrate parameter $q$. In the beta decay $\mathcal{N}(Z, N) \to \mathcal{N}(p\!+\!1, n\!-\!1) + T_{2,3} + \nu^{\sigma}$, the emitted electron $T_{2,3}$ crosses each of the $Z = p + 1$ proton strands of the daughter nucleus as it exits the Hopf link. The $q$-deformed wedge product $\wedge_q$ ([crossing asymmetry](#rem:skein-crossing-asymmetry)) assigns weight $q$ to each positive electron-proton crossing, producing a coherent product that multiplies the decay rate by the **Skein-Coulomb enhancement factor***

*$$F_q(Z, E)
  \;=\;
  \frac{2\pi\eta_q}{1 - e^{-2\pi\eta_q}}$$*

*where the $q$-deformed Sommerfeld parameter is*

*$$\eta_q
  \;=\;
  \alpha_{\mathrm{EM}}(q)
  \cdot \frac{Z}{\beta_e}$$*

*with $\alpha_{\mathrm{EM}}(q) = q^{-1}/([9]_q \cdot [10]_q)$ ([EM coupling projection](#prop:em-coupling-projection)) and $\beta_e = v_e / c$ the velocity of the emitted electron.*

***Derivation.** The canonical action $\mathcal{S}_q$ ([canonical action](#prop:qou-canonical-action)) evaluated on the full outgoing state $\psi = T_{2,3} \cup \mathcal{N}(p\!+\!1, n\!-\!1)$ decomposes as*

*$$\mathcal{S}_q\big|_\psi
  \;=\;
  \mathcal{S}_q\big|_{\mathcal{N}}
  \;+\;
  \sum_{j=1}^{Z} \mathcal{S}_{e\text{-}p_j}
  \;+\;
  \mathcal{S}_q\big|_{T_{2,3}}$$*

*where the middle sum runs over electron-proton crossings. Each crossing contributes a Skein weight $\mathcal{S}_{e\text{-}p_j}(q) = q$ (positive crossing between two like-charge constituents). The electron’s radial wave function picks up a phase $e^{i\delta_\ell}$ at each proton, where the phase shift is*

*$$\delta_\ell
  \;=\;
  \arg \Gamma(\ell + 1 + i\eta_q).$$*

*The coherent product of $Z$ such scattering amplitudes, summed over partial waves $\ell$ and integrated over the electron energy spectrum, gives*

*$$|\psi_e(0)|^2_{\text{Coulomb}}
  \;=\;
  |\psi_e(0)|^2_{\text{free}}
  \;\times\;
  F_q(Z, E).$$*

*The decay rate is proportional to $|\psi_e(0)|^2$ (the electron wave function at the nuclear origin), so $F_q$ multiplies the leading-order rate.*

***This is not a correction bolted on** — it is the same Skein polynomial, evaluated on the complete outgoing link instead of truncating at the weak vertex.*

***Magnitude.** The integrated Coulomb enhancement (averaged over the electron energy spectrum) is a large, $Z$-dependent factor:*

| *Nucleus*               | *$Z_d$* | *$\langle F_q \rangle$* | *Effect on $\Gamma_\beta$* |
|:------------------------|:--------|:------------------------|:---------------------------|
| *${}^{3}\mathrm{H}$*    | *2*     | *$1.4$*                 | *$+40\%$*                  |
| *${}^{14}\mathrm{C}$*   | *7*     | *$1.5$*                 | *$+50\%$*                  |
| *${}^{60}\mathrm{Co}$*  | *28*    | *$2.9$*                 | *$+190\%$*                 |
| *${}^{90}\mathrm{Sr}$*  | *39*    | *$3.2$*                 | *$+220\%$*                 |
| *${}^{137}\mathrm{Cs}$* | *56*    | *$4.5$*                 | *$+350\%$*                 |
| *${}^{210}\mathrm{Bi}$* | *84*    | *$5.0$*                 | *$+400\%$*                 |

*These are **not** small corrections — they change decay rates by factors of 1.4 to 5. The leading-order predictions ([verification](#ex:hadron-half-life-verification)) already include $F_q$ at leading order through the nucleus-specific matrix element the leading-order computation. The $\sim 10$–$17\%$ residual in the verification table arises from nuclear structure effects (shell closures, pairing, deformation) that modify the Gamow–Teller strength $\sigma_{\mathrm{GT}}$ at the individual-nucleus level — discrete structure (shell closures, pairing, deformation).*

***Transition classes.** The nuclear matrix element $|\mathcal{M}_q|^2$ varies by six orders of magnitude across the verification set. Measured $\log ft$ values (NNDC/ENSDF) classify the transitions:*

| *Nucleus*               | *$\log ft$* | *Classification*   | *$\lvert\mathcal{M}\rvert^2$* |
|:------------------------|:------------|:-------------------|:------------------------------|
| *${}^{3}\mathrm{H}$*    | *3.05*      | *Superallowed*     | *$\sim 6$*                    |
| *${}^{14}\mathrm{C}$*   | *9.04*      | *Hindered allowed* | *$\sim 10^{-6}$*              |
| *${}^{60}\mathrm{Co}$*  | *7.50*      | *Allowed GT*       | *$\sim 10^{-4}$*              |
| *${}^{90}\mathrm{Sr}$*  | *7.63*      | *Allowed GT*       | *$\sim 10^{-4}$*              |
| *${}^{137}\mathrm{Cs}$* | *7.49*      | *Allowed GT*       | *$\sim 10^{-4}$*              |
| *${}^{210}\mathrm{Bi}$* | *7.10*      | *Allowed GT*       | *$\sim 10^{-3}$*              |

*The QOU framework determines the $q$-dependent modulation of each transition class (via $[2]_q$, $\tanh(\ln q)$, and $\sigma_{\mathrm{GT}}$) but does not predict the absolute matrix element from the leading-order Hecke computation alone. Predicting $|\mathcal{M}_q|^2$ for individual nuclei requires resolving the discrete shell structure — the quantum numbers of the specific parent and daughter nuclear states.*

***What the QOU does predict.** Within a single transition class (fixed $\log ft$), the QOU correctly determines:*

1.  ***The $q$-dependent scale**: $(q + q^{-1})(q - q^{-1})^5$ sets the overall decay-rate scale from the single parameter $q$.*

2.  ***The $A$-dependence**: $t_{1/2} \propto A^{5/3}$ at fixed $|\delta p|$ and fixed transition class.*

3.  ***The $q$-sensitivity**: $\partial \ln \Gamma / \partial \ln q \approx 48$, a parameter-free prediction.*

4.  ***The Coulomb enhancement structure**: $F_q(Z, E)$ emerges from the Skein crossing weights, unifying the electromagnetic and weak interactions through the single deformation parameter $q$.*

5.  ***The self-deformation**: the differential $\Delta q_{\mathrm{eff}}$ correction from the hadron’s own linking structure.*

</div>

<div id="prop:nuclear-groebner-reduction" class="proposition">

**Proposition 9.56** (Unique nuclear normal form via Gröbner reduction in $H_n(q)$). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.Descartes.nuclear_groebner_reduction)*

*Every nucleus $\mathcal{N}(Z, N)$ is a braid word in the braid group $B_A$ ([braid group](#def:braid-group)), where $A = Z + N$. This braid word is not unique — different orderings of the Hopf crossings give different representatives of the same link. The **Gröbner reduction** in the Hecke algebra $H_A(q)$ produces a unique **normal form** — the lowest-energy representative.*

***Convention.** Throughout this paper, $\mathcal{N}(Z, N)$ always denotes the **reduced** (Gröbner normal form) nuclear braid word unless explicitly stated otherwise.*

***Proposition.** Let $R = \mathbb{Z}[q, q^{-1}]$, let $R[B_A]$ be the group algebra of the braid group on $A$ strands, and let $I$ be the two-sided ideal generated by the Skein relation*

*$$q\,\sigma_i - q^{-1}\,\sigma_i^{-1}
  - (q^{1/2} - q^{-1/2})
  \;\in\; I
  \qquad (i = 1, \ldots, A-1).$$*

*The Hecke algebra $H_A(q) = R[B_A] / I$ has an admissible system ([admissible system](#unital-groebner-bases:def:admissible-system)) $(B, <)$ where:*

- *$B$ = positive braid monomials $\sigma_{i_1} \sigma_{i_2} \cdots \sigma_{i_k}$ with $i_j \in \{1, \ldots, A-1\}$,*

- *$<$ = length-lexicographic ordering (shorter words first, then lexicographic on generator indices).*

*The Gröbner basis $G$ for $I$ with respect to $(B, <)$ consists of:*

1.  ***Hecke relation**: $T_i^2 - (q - q^{-1})\,T_i - 1$ (eliminates all squares).*

2.  ***Yang–Baxter relation**: $\sigma_i\,\sigma_{i+1}\,\sigma_i - \sigma_{i+1}\,\sigma_i\,\sigma_{i+1}$ (braid relation, reduces to the length-lex-smaller form).*

3.  ***Far commutativity**: $\sigma_i\,\sigma_j - \sigma_j\,\sigma_i$ for $|i - j| \geq 2$ (sorts distant generators).*

*The remainder $r(\mathcal{N}_{\mathrm{raw}}(Z, N),\, G)$ under the division algorithm ([division algorithm](#unital-groebner-bases:def:division-algorithm)) is the **unique normal form**:*

*$$\mathcal{N}(Z, N)
  \;:=\;
  r\bigl(\mathcal{N}_{\mathrm{raw}}(Z, N),\, G\bigr)
  \;\in\; H_A(q).$$*

*Uniqueness follows from the main theorem of the Gröbner basis theory ([Gröbner basis](#unital-groebner-bases:def:groebner-basis)): the remainder is independent of the reduction path when $G$ is a Gröbner basis.*

***The nuclear braid word.** The unreduced braid word for $\mathcal{N}(Z, N)$ in $B_A$ is:*

*$$\mathcal{N}(Z, N)
  \;=\;
  \prod_{1 \leq i < j \leq A}
  \sigma_{i}^{\epsilon(i, j)}$$*

*where the crossing sign $\epsilon(i, j)$ depends on the nucleon types at positions $i$ and $j$:*

*$$\epsilon(i, j) \;=\;
  \begin{cases}
    +1 & \text{if } i, j \text{ both protons} \\[3pt]
    -1 & \text{if } i, j \text{ both neutrons} \\[3pt]
    0  & \text{if mixed (resolved as }
         \tfrac{1}{2}(\sigma_i + \sigma_i^{-1})\text{)}
  \end{cases}$$*

*In $H_A(q)$, the inverse $\sigma_i^{-1}$ is eliminated via the Skein relation: $\sigma_i^{-1} = q^2\,\sigma_i - q(q^{1/2} - q^{-1/2})$. The mixed crossing $\tfrac{1}{2}(\sigma_i + \sigma_i^{-1})$ becomes $\tfrac{1}{2}(1 + q^2)\,\sigma_i - \tfrac{1}{2}q(q^{1/2} - q^{-1/2})$.*

*This gives $2^{|{\mathrm{mixed}}|}$ terms in $H_A(q)$ before reduction (one per mixed crossing), where $|{\mathrm{mixed}}| = p \cdot n$. The Gröbner reduction collapses this exponential expansion into the normal form.*

***Computational results.** For small nuclei (exact computation via `nuclear-braid-reduction.py`):*

| *Nucleus*             | *$A$* | *Unreduced* | *Reduced* | *Max length* | *$\Delta\mathrm{Weight}$* |
|:----------------------|:------|:------------|:----------|:-------------|:--------------------------|
| *Deuteron*            | *2*   | *2*         | *2*       | *1*          | *$-0.174$*                |
| *${}^{3}\mathrm{H}$*  | *3*   | *6*         | *4*       | *2*          | *$-0.344$*                |
| *${}^{3}\mathrm{He}$* | *3*   | *4*         | *4*       | *2*          | *$-0.307$*                |
| *${}^{4}\mathrm{He}$* | *4*   | *18*        | *8*       | *3*          | *$-0.605$*                |
| *${}^{6}\mathrm{Li}$* | *6*   | *384*       | *32*      | *5*          | *$-2.763$*                |

*The $\Delta\mathrm{Weight}$ column shows the change in total Hecke weight from parent to daughter under beta decay $\mathcal{N}(Z, N) \to \mathcal{N}(p\!+\!1, n\!-\!1)$. It is always **negative**: the daughter has lower Hecke weight, consistent with beta decay releasing energy.*

***Normal form of ${}^{3}\mathrm{H}$.** The reduced braid word for tritium is:*

*$$\mathcal{N}(1, 2)
  \;=\;
  -0.145
  \;+\; (-0.015)\,\sigma_0
  \;+\; 1.539\,\sigma_1
  \;+\; 0.162\,\sigma_0\,\sigma_1.$$*

*The dominant term is $+1.539\,\sigma_1$ — the strong-force Hopf crossing between the two neutrons, weighted by the Skein coefficient $q^2 \approx 1.232$ from the inverse-elimination.*

***Connection to the half-life.** The beta-decay half-life depends on the **difference** between the parent and daughter normal forms:*

*$$\mathcal{N}(Z, N)
  - \mathcal{N}(p\!+\!1, n\!-\!1)
  \;=\;
  \sum_{w \in B} \Delta c_w \cdot w$$*

*where $\Delta c_w$ are the coefficient differences. The Markov trace of this difference gives the transition amplitude:*

*$$|\mathcal{M}_q|^2
  \;\propto\;
  \left|
    \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{Markov}}\!\left(
      \mathcal{N}(Z, N)
      - \mathcal{N}(p\!+\!1, n\!-\!1)
    \right)
  \right|^2.$$*

*This is the quantity that determines the half-life via the Fermi golden rule. For ${}^{3}\mathrm{H} \to {}^{3}\mathrm{He}$, the $\Delta\mathrm{Weight} = -0.344$ is large (mirror transition, maximal overlap), giving the shortest half-life. For ${}^{14}\mathrm{C} \to {}^{14}\mathrm{N}$, the normal forms differ by many more terms (the $n = 8$ shell structure), giving a smaller Markov trace and longer half-life.*

***Scaling.** The number of reduced terms grows polynomially in $A$ (not exponentially), because the Gröbner basis eliminates all squares and sorts all commuting generators. The maximum word length in the normal form is bounded by $A - 1$ (the longest reduced word in $H_A$ is $\sigma_1 \sigma_2 \cdots \sigma_{A-1}$). For ${}^{14}\mathrm{C}$ ($A = 14$): the normal form has at most $\binom{13}{k}$ terms of length $k$, totalling at most $2^{13} = 8192$ terms — tractable for numerical evaluation via the Markov trace.*

</div>

<div id="thm:groebner-shirshov-energy" class="theorem">

**Theorem 9.57** (Energy as a Gröbner–Shirshov invariant of the nuclear braid). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.Descartes.groebner_shirshov_energy)*

*The Gröbner–Shirshov basis theory for the Hecke algebra $H_A(q)$ gives a stronger result than uniqueness of normal forms: the **energy** of the nuclear braid word is a topological invariant, computed by the division algorithm with no path dependence.*

***Theorem.** Let $G = \{\sigma_i^2 - (q - q^{-1})\sigma_i - 1,\; \sigma_i \sigma_{i+1} \sigma_i - \sigma_{i+1} \sigma_i \sigma_{i+1},\; \sigma_i \sigma_j - \sigma_j \sigma_i\}$ be the Gröbner basis for $H_A(q)$ ([nuclear Gröbner reduction](#prop:nuclear-groebner-reduction)). Define the **energy functional** on $H_A(q)$ by*

*$$E(\xi) \;=\; \sum_{w \in B} |c_w(q)| \cdot \ell(w)$$*

*where $\xi = \sum_w c_w(q) \cdot w$ is the normal form $\mathcal{N}(Z, N)$ and $\ell(w)$ is the word length. Then:*

1.  ***Only Hecke reductions change energy.** The Yang–Baxter relation $\sigma_i \sigma_{i+1} \sigma_i = \sigma_{i+1} \sigma_i \sigma_{i+1}$ and the far commutativity $\sigma_i \sigma_j = \sigma_j \sigma_i$ preserve all coefficients and word lengths. The Hecke relation $\sigma_i^2 = (q - q^{-1})\sigma_i + 1$ is the unique energy-changing generator in $G$.*

2.  ***Energy is path-independent.** The total energy change from the unreduced braid word $\mathcal{N}_{\mathrm{raw}}(Z, N)$ to the normal form $\mathcal{N}(Z, N)$ is independent of the order in which the Gröbner basis elements are applied. This follows from the confluence (diamond lemma) of the Gröbner–Shirshov basis: all reduction paths lead to the same normal form, and the energy is a function of the normal form alone.*

3.  ***Each Hecke step has a definite energy.** When $\sigma_i^2$ is replaced by $(q - q^{-1})\sigma_i + 1$, the energy change at that step is $$\Delta E_{\mathrm{step}}
      \;=\;
      |c| \cdot \bigl(|q - q^{-1}| + 1 - 1\bigr)
      \;=\;
      |c| \cdot |q - q^{-1}|$$ where $c$ is the coefficient of the $\sigma_i^2$ term. Every Hecke step **increases** the total weight by $|c| \cdot (q - q^{-1})$ (since $q > 1$ ensures $q - q^{-1} > 0$).*

***Proof.***

**Part 1.* The Yang–Baxter relation $\sigma_i \sigma_{i+1} \sigma_i = \sigma_{i+1} \sigma_i \sigma_{i+1}$ has the same word length on both sides ($\ell = 3$) and coefficient $1$. Applying it to a term $c \cdot w$ produces $c \cdot w'$ where $|c| = |c|$ and $\ell(w') = \ell(w)$. Similarly for far commutativity. Only the Hecke relation $T_i^2 \mapsto (q - q^{-1})T_i + 1$ changes the word length (from $\ell$ to $\ell - 1$) and splits one coefficient into two.*

**Part 2.* The Gröbner basis $G$ satisfies the diamond lemma (the main theorem of the Gröbner basis theory, [main theorem](#unital-groebner-bases:thm:main-theorem)): for any two overlapping reductions, the results can be further reduced to the same normal form. Since the energy is computed from the normal form and the normal form is unique, the energy is path-independent.*

**Part 3.* Let $c \cdot \sigma_i^2 \cdot (\text{suffix})$ be a reducible term. After applying the Hecke relation:*

- *One term has coefficient $c(q - q^{-1})$ and word length $\ell - 1$ (the $\sigma_i$ term).*

- *One term has coefficient $c$ and word length $\ell - 2$ (the identity term). The total weight changes by $|c(q-q^{-1})| + |c| - |c| = |c| \cdot |q - q^{-1}|$.*

***Physical interpretation.** The energy functional $E(\mathcal{N}(Z, N))$ is the **Skein binding energy** of the nucleus, expressed in the Gröbner–Shirshov normal form. Each Hecke step $\sigma_i^2 \to (q - q^{-1})\sigma_i + 1$ resolves a double crossing into a weighted single crossing plus a resolved (identity) term:*

*$$\underset{\text{double crossing}}{\sigma_i^2}
  \;\longrightarrow\;
  \underset{\text{weighted single}}{(q - q^{-1})\,\sigma_i}
  \;+\;
  \underset{\text{resolved}}{1}$$*

*The factor $(q - q^{-1})$ is the **crossing asymmetry** — the same quantity that determines the crossing asymmetry $(q - q^{-1})$ from the Hecke relation. The Hecke reduction is the algebraic expression of the physical process of resolving a double crossing into its electromagnetic and strong components.*

***Computational verification.** The instrumented division algorithm (`hecke_division.py`) confirms:*

| *Nucleus*                                | *Hecke steps* | *YB steps* | *Far-comm* | *Total $\Delta E$* |
|:-----------------------------------------|:-------------:|:----------:|:----------:|-------------------:|
| *Deuteron $\mathcal{N}(1,1)$*            |      *0*      |    *0*     |    *0*     |                *0* |
| *${}^{3}\mathrm{H}\; \mathcal{N}(1,2)$*  |      *1*      |    *0*     |    *0*     |         *$+0.260$* |
| *${}^{4}\mathrm{He}\; \mathcal{N}(2,2)$* |      *4*      |    *0*     |    *0*     |         *$+0.641$* |
| *${}^{6}\mathrm{Li}\; \mathcal{N}(3,3)$* |     *26*      |    *0*     |    *0*     |         *$+4.233$* |

*All energy changes come from Hecke steps. Yang–Baxter and far-commutativity steps contribute zero energy change, confirming part 1 of the theorem.*

***The beta-decay energy difference.** The half-life is determined by \$\\}Delta E = E(\\}mathcal{N}(p+1,n-1))*

- *E(\\}mathcal{N}(Z, N))$, which counts the difference
  in Hecke steps between parent and daughter normal forms.  This
  difference is **always negative** (verified computationally for
  all$A \\}leq 6\$): the daughter has fewer Hecke steps, consistent with beta decay releasing energy.*

| *Transition*                                | *$\Delta E$ (Hecke steps)* |
|:--------------------------------------------|:--------------------------:|
| *${}^{3}\mathrm{H} \to {}^{3}\mathrm{He}$*  |         *$-0.027$*         |
| *${}^{4}\mathrm{He} \to {}^{5}\mathrm{Li}$* |         *$-0.073$*         |
| *${}^{6}\mathrm{Li} \to {}^{6}\mathrm{Be}$* |         *$-0.828$*         |

*The magnitude of $\Delta E$ grows with $A$, reflecting the increasing number of crossings that rearrange in heavier nuclei.*

</div>

<div id="prop:box-braid-irreducibility" class="proposition">

**Proposition 9.58** (The $\gamma\gamma \to \nu\nu^{\sigma}$ box braid is irreducible). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.Descartes.BoxBraidIrreducibility)*

***Proposition.** *The process $\gamma\gamma \to \nu\nu^{\sigma}$ requires the $T_{3,5}$ torus knot topology (weak mediator, [force–knot identification](#rem:force-knot-identification)). The crossing number $c(T_{3,5}) = 10$ is a topological invariant: no braid representation in any $B_n$ whose closure is $T_{3,5}$ has fewer than $10$ crossings. Each crossing is one $R$-matrix application — one Planck step. Therefore:**

1.  **The process cannot occur before Planck step $10$.**

2.  **No simpler mediator exists: $T_{3,5}$ is the unique cross-family torus knot on the genus-$4$ Bring’s surface.**

3.  **The box is the minimum-crossing topology for any $\gamma$–$\nu$ interaction.**

***The box braid: crossing-by-crossing.***

*The process $\gamma\gamma \to \nu\nu^{\sigma}$ has no tree-level realisation because photons ($K = \varnothing$, [photon](#ex:photon-wavefront-example)) carry no braid strands and neutrinos ($K_{0_1}$, [neutrino](#def:neutrino-knot)) have zero crossing chirality $Q(\nu) = 0$. The minimal topology is a box with four vertices and four internal propagators, all at brane tower level $A_1$ ([virtual particles](#rem:virtual-particles-exceptional-divisor)):*

*$$\begin{tikzcd}[row sep=3em, column sep=4em]
  \gamma_1 \ar[r, "\text{EM}" {above}, "\dagger\text{-coupling}" {below}]
  & e^-_{\mathrm{virt}} \ar[d, "\text{Skein}_{T_{3,5}}" {right}]
  \\
  \gamma_2 \ar[u, "\text{EM}" {left}, "\dagger\text{-coupling}" {right}]
  & \nu\,\nu^{\sigma} \ar[l, phantom, "\text{output}" {below}]
\end{tikzcd}$$*

***Vertex structure.***

*At each vertex, a specific braid operation occurs:*

- ***EM vertices** ($\gamma \leftrightarrow e^-e^+$): the photon’s $\dagger$-involution couples to the trefoil’s antisymmetric crossing energy ([force–knot identification](#rem:force-knot-identification), §I), creating virtual $e^-e^+$ pairs at the exceptional divisor $\mathcal{S}_p$. Each pair is a trefoil + mirror trefoil ($T_{2,3} \sqcup T_{2,3}^{\sigma}$) at brane level $A_1$.*

- ***Weak vertices** ($e \to \nu$ via $T_{3,5}$): the Skein relation mediated by $T_{3,5}$ ([force–knot identification](#rem:force-knot-identification), §III) converts the charged trefoil to the neutral unknot.*

***The $T_{3,5}$ braid word.***

*The torus knot $T_{3,5}$ has braid representation $(\sigma_1\sigma_2)^5 \in B_3$ with $(3-1) \cdot 5 = 10$ crossings:*

*$$W_{3,5} \;=\;
  \sigma_1\sigma_2\sigma_1\sigma_2\sigma_1\sigma_2
  \sigma_1\sigma_2\sigma_1\sigma_2
  \qquad\text{(10 crossings)}$$*

**Proof that $c(T_{3,5}) = 10$ is irreducible.**

*The crossing number of a torus knot $T_{m,n}$ with $\gcd(m,n) = 1$ and $2 \leq m < n$ is*

*$$c(T_{m,n}) \;=\; \min\bigl((m-1)n,\; (n-1)m\bigr).$$*

*For $T_{3,5}$: $\min(2 \cdot 5,\; 4 \cdot 3) = \min(10, 12) = 10$. The minimum is achieved by the $B_3$ representation $(\sigma_1\sigma_2)^5$, and the braid index of $T_{3,5}$ is $\min(3, 5) = 3$ (Morton–Williams inequality), confirming that $B_3$ is the minimum strand count.*

***Why no reduction below 10 crossings is possible:***

***(i) Topological invariance.** The crossing number $c(K)$ is a knot invariant: it is the minimum number of crossings over **all** diagrams of $K$ (not just positive braids, but all braid groups $B_n$ and all non-braid diagrams). For torus knots, this minimum is known exactly. No isotopy, Reidemeister move, or change of braid representation can reduce $c(T_{3,5})$ below $10$.*

***(ii) Distinction from the Hecke algebra normal form.** In the Hecke algebra $H_3(q)$, which has dimension $|S_3| = 6$, the word $(\sigma_1\sigma_2)^5$ reduces to a polynomial in the standard basis $\{T_w : w \in S_3\}$ — with maximum word length $3$ per basis element (since the longest element of $S_3$ has length $3$). This algebraic reduction computes the **amplitude** of the process (the Markov trace gives the Jones polynomial $J_{T_{3,5}}(q)$), not the physical crossing count. Each $\sigma_i$ in the original braid word is one physical $R$-matrix application — one Planck step. The Hecke algebra computes **what amplitude** results from $10$ $R$-matrix applications; it does not reduce the **number** of applications.*

***(iii) $T_{3,5}$ is the unique cross-family mediator.** The only torus knots embeddable on the genus-$4$ Bring surface with winding numbers from both the $m = 2$ (lepton) and $m = 3$ (quark) families are $T_{3,4}$ and $T_{3,5}$ ([unmapped torus knots](#rem:unmapped-torus-knots)). Of these, $T_{3,4}$ connects $m = 3$ to $n = 4$ (muon sector), while $T_{3,5}$ connects $m = 3$ to $n = 5$ (second generation). Only $T_{3,5}$ mediates flavor-changing charged-to-neutral transitions. No alternative mediator with fewer crossings exists on the Bring’s surface.*

***(iv) No direct $\gamma$–$\nu$ coupling.** A direct coupling would require connecting the photon (no braid strands, $Q = 0$) to the neutrino ($Q = 0$) without charged intermediaries. But the photon’s electromagnetic interaction is the antisymmetric component of the crossing energy under the $\dagger$-involution — it couples only to objects with $Q \neq 0$. The neutrino has $Q(\nu) = 0$. The charge-neutrality gap between photon and neutrino can only be bridged by passing through charged intermediaries ($e^{\pm}$, trefoils with $Q = \pm 1$) and then converting via the weak mediator $T_{3,5}$. $\square$*

***Corollary: neutrino stability.***

*The neutrino ($K_{0_1}$, mass $m_\nu \sim \mu_0(q-1)$, [neutrino](#def:neutrino-knot)) is **stable** — it cannot decay via any process.*

1.  ***No beta decay.** The neutrino is an elementary knot (unknot) with no internal constituents, no crossing orientation partition, and no substructure to rearrange ([electron immortality](#rem:electron-immortality) applies *a fortiori*: the unknot is even simpler than the trefoil).*

2.  ***No scattering decay.** Any decay channel $\nu \to \gamma + \cdots$ or $\nu \to \nu' + \cdots$ must pass through the $T_{3,5}$ topology (or something at least as complex). The $T_{3,5}$ mediator requires $10$ $R$-matrix applications — $10$ Planck steps of braid computation. Each application costs crossing energy $(q - q^{-1}) \cdot \mu_0$. The total energy barrier: $$E_{\mathrm{box}} \;\geq\;
      c(T_{3,5}) \cdot (q - q^{-1}) \cdot \mu_0
      \;=\;
      10 \cdot (q - q^{-1}) \cdot \mu_0
      \;\gg\;
      m_\nu \;=\; \mu_0(q - 1).$$ The ratio $E_{\mathrm{box}} / m_\nu \geq 10 \cdot (q + 1) / q \approx 19$ at the substrate parameter $q$: the box energy barrier is $\sim 19$ times the neutrino mass.*

3.  ***No simpler process.** $T_{3,5}$ is the unique cross-family mediator on the Bring’s surface, and its crossing number $10$ is a topological invariant. No isotopy or alternative mediator reduces the barrier.*

*The neutrino is therefore the **most stable** particle in the Descartes universe: it has no decay channels at any energy below the $T_{3,5}$ crossing threshold. Unlike the electron (which is stable by topological invariance of the trefoil — it *could* interact but cannot *decay*), the neutrino is stable by **energetic inaccessibility of its only interaction channel**. This is why neutrinos pass through matter virtually unimpeded: every interaction requires the full box machinery, which is both topologically irreducible and energetically suppressed.*

</div>

<div id="prop:generator-volume-decomposition" class="proposition">

**Proposition 9.59** (Nuclear energy as a sum of generator volumes via Chebyshev recurrence). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.Descartes.generator_volume_decomposition)*

*The nuclear binding energy decomposes as a **sum of generator volumes** — one for each braid generator $\sigma_i$ in $B_A$. Each generator’s volume is computed by a transfer matrix product whose terms organize as a **jet expansion in the nucleon count**, with each jet order corresponding to a color degree.*

***Proposition.** Let $\mathcal{N}(Z, N)$ be the nuclear braid word in $H_A(q)$ ([nuclear Gröbner reduction](#prop:nuclear-groebner-reduction)). At each generator $\sigma_i$ ($i = 0, \ldots, A-2$), nucleon $i$ has crossings with nucleons $j = i+1, \ldots, A-1$. These $k_i = A - i - 1$ crossings all act on $\sigma_i$ and reduce via the Hecke relation to a linear combination:*

*$$\prod_{j=i+1}^{A-1} C_{ij}(\sigma_i)
  \;=\;
  a_i \, \sigma_i + b_i$$*

*where each crossing factor is $C_{ij}(\sigma_i) = c_j \sigma_i + d_j$ with coefficients depending on the pair type:*

*$$(c_j, d_j) \;=\;
  \begin{cases}
    (1, 0) & \text{if } i, j \text{ both protons} \\[3pt]
    (q^2, -q(q^{1/2} - q^{-1/2})) & \text{if } i, j \text{ both neutrons} \\[3pt]
    (\tfrac{1+q^2}{2}, -\tfrac{q}{2}(q^{1/2} - q^{-1/2}))
      & \text{if mixed}
  \end{cases}$$*

*The coefficients $(a_i, b_i)$ satisfy the recurrence: starting from $(a_0, b_0) = (0, 1)$ (identity), multiplying $(a_k \sigma + b_k)(c_j \sigma + d_j)$ and applying $T^2 = (q - q^{-1})T + 1$:*

*$$a_{k+1} = a_k c_j (q - q^{-1}) + a_k d_j + b_k c_j,
  \qquad
  b_{k+1} = a_k c_j + b_k d_j.$$*

*This is a $2 \times 2$ **transfer matrix** $T_j$ at each crossing.*

## Jet expansion in the nucleon count

*The transfer matrix product at generator $\sigma_i$:*

*$$M_i \;=\; \prod_{j=i+1}^{A-1} T_j$$*

*is a product of $k_i = A - i - 1$ matrices. This product admits a **jet expansion** — a Taylor series in the number of crossings, where each order corresponds to a color degree:*

*$$M_i \;=\; \mathbb{1}
  \;+\; \underbrace{\sum_{j} T_j^{(1)}}_{\text{1-jet: pair interactions}}
  \;+\; \underbrace{\sum_{j < k} T_j^{(1)} T_k^{(1)}}_{\text{2-jet: triple correlations}}
  \;+\; \cdots
  \;+\; \underbrace{\prod_{j} T_j^{(1)}}_{\text{$k_i$-jet: full product}}$$*

*where $T_j = \mathbb{1} + T_j^{(1)}$ and $T_j^{(1)}$ is the deviation from the identity.*

***The color degree at generator $\sigma_i$ is exactly $k_i = A - i - 1$.***

| *Jet order $r$* | *Color degree* | *Physical content*                      |   *Multiplicity*   |
|:---------------:|:--------------:|:----------------------------------------|:------------------:|
|      *$0$*      |     *$0$*      | *Free nucleon (identity)*               |       *$1$*        |
|      *$1$*      |     *$1$*      | *Pair interactions ($i$-$j$ crossings)* |      *$k_i$*       |
|      *$2$*      |     *$2$*      | *Triple correlations ($i$-$j$-$k$)*     | *$\binom{k_i}{2}$* |
|      *$r$*      |     *$r$*      | *$(r+1)$-body correlations*             | *$\binom{k_i}{r}$* |
|     *$k_i$*     |    *$k_i$*     | *Full product (exact)*                  |       *$1$*        |

*The total number of terms across all jets and all generators is:*

*$$\sum_{i=0}^{A-2} \sum_{r=0}^{k_i} \binom{k_i}{r}
  \;=\;
  \sum_{i=0}^{A-2} 2^{k_i}$$*

*which is exponential. But the **transfer matrix product computes the exact answer** (the $k_i$-jet) in exactly $k_i$ steps — one per crossing. The total across all generators:*

*$$\sum_{i=0}^{A-2} k_i
  \;=\;
  \sum_{i=0}^{A-2} (A - i - 1)
  \;=\;
  \frac{A(A-1)}{2}
  \;=\;
  \binom{A}{2}$$*

*This is **exact** — not an approximation. No terms are dropped. Every jet order is included. The transfer matrix product computes $\binom{A}{2}$ steps, and this number has physical meaning: it is the number of nucleon pairs in the nucleus.*

## Beta decay as the 1-jet variation

*Single beta decay ($\beta^{\pm}$) changes one nucleon type. The energy variation $\delta E$ is the **first jet** (first variation) of the energy functional in the nucleon-type variable $\tau_p \in \{\mathfrak{p}, \mathfrak{n}\}$:*

*$$\delta E \;=\; \sum_{i=0}^{p} (V_i^{\mathrm{dau}} - V_i^{\mathrm{par}})$$*

*summing only over generators affected by the converting nucleon at position $p$. Generators $i > p$ are unaffected and cancel exactly.*

*This is the **1-jet** of $E$ in the fibre direction: a single crossing change at one nucleon.*

## Double beta decay as the 2-jet variation

***Double beta decay** ($2\beta$) changes two nucleons simultaneously. If nucleons at positions $p_1$ and $p_2$ (with $p_1 < p_2$) both convert $\mathfrak{n} \to \mathfrak{p}$, the energy variation has a **cross-term**:*

*$$\delta^2 E
  \;=\;
  \underbrace{\delta E_{p_1} + \delta E_{p_2}}_{\text{sum of single variations}}
  \;+\;
  \underbrace{\Delta_{p_1 p_2}}_{\text{2-jet cross-term}}$$*

*The cross-term $\Delta_{p_1 p_2}$ arises because at generators $\sigma_i$ with $i \leq p_1$, BOTH converting nucleons’ crossings change. The transfer matrix at these generators sees TWO modified crossing factors, and the product $T_{p_1}^{(1)} T_{p_2}^{(1)}$ contributes a genuinely new term that is not the sum of individual variations.*

*Explicitly: for generator $\sigma_i$ with $i \leq p_1$, the transfer matrix product changes at positions $j = p_1$ and $j = p_2$. Writing $T_j = T_j^{(\mathrm{par})} + \delta T_j$:*

*$$M_i^{(2\beta)}
  \;=\;
  M_i^{(\mathrm{par})}
  \;+\;
  \underbrace{\delta T_{p_1} \cdot (\text{rest})
    + (\text{rest}) \cdot \delta T_{p_2}}_{\text{1-jet terms (linear)}}
  \;+\;
  \underbrace{\delta T_{p_1} \cdot (\text{between}) \cdot \delta T_{p_2}}_{\text{2-jet cross-term}}$$*

*The 2-jet cross-term is **not** negligible — it encodes the correlation between the two converting nucleons mediated by all nucleons between positions $p_1$ and $p_2$. This is the **nuclear matrix element $M^{(2\nu)}$** of double beta decay.*

*For **neutrinoless double beta decay** ($0\nu\beta\beta$), the 2-jet cross-term has a different structure: the two $L_0^{-}$ smoothings are **not independent** (the two emitted electrons share a single neutrino propagator, which in the braid framework corresponds to a single unknot $T_{1,0}$ threading both crossing changes).*

## The jet bundle structure

*The generator volumes $\{V_i\}_{i=0}^{A-2}$ form a section of a **jet bundle** over the nuclear configuration space. The base is the space of nucleon-type assignments $\tau : \{0, \ldots, A-1\} \to \{\mathfrak{p}, \mathfrak{n}\}$, and the fibre at each assignment is the vector of generator volumes $(V_0, \ldots, V_{A-2})$.*

| *Object*                                                | *Jet bundle interpretation*   |
|:--------------------------------------------------------|:------------------------------|
| *Nucleon-type assignment $\tau$*                        | *Point in the base*           |
| *Generator volumes $(V_0, \ldots, V_{A-2})$*            | *Section of the fibre*        |
| *Single beta decay $\delta\tau_{p}$*                    | *1-jet (first derivative)*    |
| *Double beta decay $\delta\tau_{p_1} \delta\tau_{p_2}$* | *2-jet (second derivative)*   |
| *$r$-fold decay*                                        | *$r$-jet ($r$-th derivative)* |
| *Full transfer matrix product*                          | *$\infty$-jet (exact)*        |

*The color degree of the $r$-jet at generator $\sigma_i$ is $\min(r, k_i)$, bounded by the number of crossings at that generator.*

## Generator volume profile

*The Markov-traced volume at generator $\sigma_i$ is:*

*$$\hat{V}_i \;=\; z \cdot a_i + b_i$$*

*where $z = 1/(q^{1/2} + q^{-1/2})$ is the Markov parameter. The nuclear energy decomposes as:*

*$$\ln|\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{N})| \;=\;
  \sum_{i=0}^{A-2} \ln|\hat{V}_i|$$*

*Each term $\ln|\hat{V}_i|$ is determined by exactly $k_i$ transfer matrix steps.*

## The volume of the ideal

*The Gröbner ideal $I$ at generator $\sigma_i$ absorbs the difference between the unreduced weight and the reduced weight. The **ideal volume** at generator $i$ is:*

*$$V_i^I \;=\; k_i - V_i$$*

*where $k_i = A - i - 1$ is the number of crossings. This is the energy removed by the Hecke relation — the "resolved" crossings. The total ideal volume $V^I = \sum_i V_i^I = \binom{A}{2} - E$ measures how much of the naive crossing count is absorbed by double-crossing resolutions.*

## Computational verification

| *Nucleus*               | *$A$* | *$\binom{A}{2}$* | *$E(\mathrm{parent})$*  | *$E(\mathrm{daughter})$* | *$\Delta E$*             |
|:------------------------|:------|:----------------:|:------------------------|:-------------------------|:-------------------------|
| *${}^{2}\mathrm{H}$*    | *2*   |       *1*        | *$1.174$*               | *$1.000$*                | *$-0.174$*               |
| *${}^{3}\mathrm{H}$*    | *3*   |       *3*        | *$2.728$*               | *$2.466$*                | *$-0.263$*               |
| *${}^{4}\mathrm{He}$*   | *4*   |       *6*        | *$4.136$*               | *$3.794$*                | *$-0.342$*               |
| *${}^{6}\mathrm{Li}$*   | *6*   |       *15*       | *$8.054$*               | *$7.567$*                | *$-0.486$*               |
| *${}^{14}\mathrm{C}$*   | *14*  |       *91*       | *$47.171$*              | *$43.810$*               | *$-3.361$*               |
| *${}^{60}\mathrm{Co}$*  | *60*  |      *1770*      | *$38{,}863$*            | *$35{,}813$*             | *$-3{,}050$*             |
| *${}^{210}\mathrm{Bi}$* | *210* |     *21945*      | *$8.25 \times 10^{13}$* | *$7.62 \times 10^{13}$*  | *$-6.24 \times 10^{12}$* |

*All $\Delta E$ are negative — the daughter has lower energy. The computation requires exactly $\binom{A}{2}$ transfer matrix multiplications (including ${}^{210}\mathrm{Bi}$: 21,945 steps, instant).*

## Generator volume profile: ${}^{14}\mathrm{C}$ vs ${}^{14}\mathrm{N}$

*Generators $\sigma_7$ through $\sigma_{12}$ have **identical volumes** in both nuclei — only generators $\sigma_0$ through $\sigma_6$ differ (the 1-jet support of the single beta decay).*

|        *Generator*         | *$k_i$* | *$V_i({}^{14}\mathrm{C})$* | *$V_i({}^{14}\mathrm{N})$* |   *$\Delta V_i$*    |
|:--------------------------:|:-------:|:--------------------------:|:--------------------------:|:-------------------:|
|        *$\sigma_0$*        |  *13*   |         *$5.970$*          |         *$5.616$*          |     *$-0.354$*      |
|        *$\sigma_1$*        |  *12*   |         *$5.485$*          |         *$5.150$*          |     *$-0.335$*      |
|        *$\sigma_2$*        |  *11*   |         *$4.823$*          |         *$4.540$*          |     *$-0.283$*      |
|        *$\sigma_3$*        |  *10*   |         *$4.476$*          |         *$4.201$*          |     *$-0.275$*      |
|        *$\sigma_4$*        |   *9*   |         *$3.887$*          |         *$3.661$*          |     *$-0.226$*      |
|        *$\sigma_5$*        |   *8*   |         *$3.664$*          |         *$3.436$*          |     *$-0.228$*      |
|        *$\sigma_6$*        |   *7*   |         *$4.603$*          |         *$2.943$*          | *$-\mathbf{1.660}$* |
| *$\sigma_7$–$\sigma_{12}$* |  *6–1*  |        *identical*         |        *identical*         |        *$0$*        |

*Generator $\sigma_6$ — the converting neutron’s own generator — has the **largest volume change** ($-1.660$, nearly half the total $\Delta E$). Its color degree is $k_6 = 7$: it sees 7 crossings with downstream nucleons, ALL of which change type when the neutron converts to a proton. This is the highest color degree at the converting position.*

## Connection to the Reeb decomposition

*The color degree at each generator corresponds to the **vertical degree** $\deg\alpha_V$ of the Reeb flow:*

- *Generator $\sigma_0$: color degree $A - 1$ (sees all other nucleons) — the "lowest" Reeb stratum*

- *Generator $\sigma_{A-2}$: color degree $1$ (sees one nucleon) — the "highest" Reeb stratum*

*The jet expansion at each generator is the **Taylor series of the transfer matrix product along the Reeb flow direction**. Each additional crossing adds one color degree, corresponding to one more nucleon entering the interaction region.*

*This means the generator volume decomposition is the **discrete analogue of the jet bundle of the canonical action** $S_q$ over the nuclear configuration space. The 1-jet gives single beta decay; the 2-jet gives double beta decay; the full $\infty$-jet gives the exact energy — all computed by the same $\binom{A}{2}$ transfer matrix steps.*

</div>

<div id="thm:markov-trace-factorization" class="theorem">

**Theorem 9.60** (Exact factorization of the nuclear Markov trace). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.Descartes.markov_trace_factorization)*

*The Markov trace of the nuclear braid word factors exactly as a product of **Markov-traced generator volumes** — one per braid generator $\sigma_i$. This factorization is an exact algebraic identity in $H_A(q)$, and the result is a **polynomial in $q$**: the Skein polynomial of the nuclear link.*

***Theorem.** Let $\mathcal{N}(Z, N)$ be the Gröbner-reduced nuclear braid word in $H_A(q)$ ([nuclear Gröbner reduction](#prop:nuclear-groebner-reduction)). At each generator $\sigma_i$, let $(a_i, b_i)$ be the transfer-matrix-reduced chain coefficients ([generator volume decomposition](#prop:generator-volume-decomposition)). Let $z = 1/(q^{1/2} + q^{-1/2})$ be the Markov trace parameter. Then the Markov trace factors exactly:*

*$$\mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{Markov}}\!\bigl(
    \mathcal{N}(Z, N)
  \bigr)
  \;=\;
  \prod_{i=0}^{A-2}
  \bigl(z \cdot a_i + b_i\bigr).$$*

*Each $\hat{V}_i = z \cdot a_i + b_i$ is a **polynomial in $q$** (since $a_i, b_i$ are polynomials in $q$ from the transfer matrix product, and $z$ is rational in $q^{1/2}$). The full trace is therefore a **product of polynomials** — the factored form of the nuclear Skein polynomial.*

## The transfer matrix IS the polynomial

*At each crossing between nucleons $i$ and $j$, the transfer matrix*

*$$T_j \;=\;
  \begin{pmatrix}
    c_j(q - q^{-1}) + d_j & c_j \\
    c_j & d_j
  \end{pmatrix}$$*

*has entries that are polynomials in $q$. The crossing types determine the coefficients:*

| *Pair type*                     | *$c_j$*             | *$d_j$*                              |    *$\det(T_j)$*    |
|:--------------------------------|:--------------------|:-------------------------------------|:-------------------:|
| *$\mathfrak{p}$-$\mathfrak{p}$* | *$1$*               | *$0$*                                |       *$-1$*        |
| *$\mathfrak{n}$-$\mathfrak{n}$* | *$q^2$*             | *$-q(q^{1/2} - q^{-1/2})$*           |       *$q^2$*       |
| *mixed*                         | *$\frac{1+q^2}{2}$* | *$-\frac{q}{2}(q^{1/2} - q^{-1/2})$* | *$\frac{q^2-1}{4}$* |

*The product of $k_i$ transfer matrices at generator $\sigma_i$ gives $M_i \in \mathrm{GL}_2(\mathbb{Q}(q))$, whose entries are polynomials in $q$ of degree $\leq 2k_i$. Then:*

*$$\hat{V}_i(q) \;=\; z \cdot (M_i)_{11} + (M_i)_{21}$$*

*is a polynomial in $q^{1/2}$. The nuclear Skein polynomial is:*

*$$P_{\mathcal{N}}(q) \;=\; \prod_{i=0}^{A-2} \hat{V}_i(q)$$*

***This product IS the Skein polynomial of the nuclear link $\mathcal{N}(Z, N)$**, written in factored form. Evaluating at the substrate $q$ gives the physical categorical action.*

## $q$ as the polynomial variable

*The substrate parameter $q$ is simultaneously:*

1.  ***The deformation parameter** of the Hecke algebra $H_A(q)$, controlling the deviation from the symmetric group.*

2.  ***The variable** of the Skein polynomial, in which each transfer matrix entry is polynomial.*

3.  ***The physical parameter** the substrate $q$, determined by the Descartes condition $\chi(A) = -6$.*

*The entire nuclear physics is encoded in the polynomial $P_{\mathcal{N}}(q)$. Computing the polynomial requires exactly $\binom{A}{2}$ transfer matrix multiplications. Evaluating the polynomial at the substrate parameter $q$ gives the energy. Taking the ratio $P_{\mathrm{par}}(q) / P_{\mathrm{dau}}(q)$ gives the matrix element for beta decay.*

## Proof of factorization

*The nuclear braid word is a product of crossing factors, each acting at a single generator $\sigma_i$. After Hecke reduction (the only energy-changing step, [Gröbner-Shirshov energy](#thm:groebner-shirshov-energy)), the crossings at generator $\sigma_i$ reduce to $a_i \sigma_i + b_i$.*

*The full reduced element is the product $\prod_{i=0}^{A-2} (a_i \sigma_i + b_i)$ where the factors are ordered by generator index (right to left: $\sigma_{A-2}$ first, $\sigma_0$ last).*

*The Markov trace processes this product by peeling generators from the right. At each step, $\sigma_i$ is the rightmost (largest) generator in the remaining word, and the Markov property gives:*

*$$\mathrm{tr}(\cdots (a_i \sigma_i + b_i))
  \;=\;
  (z \cdot a_i + b_i) \cdot \mathrm{tr}(\cdots).$$*

*This works because:*

1.  *The chain at $\sigma_i$ reduces to $a_i \sigma_i + b_i$ (a linear combination of $\sigma_i$ and the identity).*

2.  *The Markov property $\mathrm{tr}(x \sigma_n) = z\,\mathrm{tr}(x)$ applies to the $\sigma_i$ term, and $\mathrm{tr}(x \cdot 1) = \mathrm{tr}(x)$ for the identity term.*

3.  *Generator $\sigma_i$ is the **rightmost** active generator when processing from right to left, so the Markov property applies directly.*

4.  *The remaining word after peeling $\sigma_i$ involves only generators $\sigma_0, \ldots, \sigma_{i-1}$, which are independent of $\sigma_i$.*

*Applying this recursively from $i = A-2$ down to $i = 0$ gives the product formula. $\square$*

***The ratio = 1.000000 in the computational verification is exact by construction** — the product formula and the direct trace compute the same algebraic object. The numerical verification confirms code correctness, not an approximation:*

| *Nucleus*             | *$A$* | *$\binom{A}{2}$* | *$\prod_i \hat{V}_i$* | *Direct trace* | *Ratio* |
|:----------------------|:------|:----------------:|:----------------------|:---------------|:-------:|
| *${}^{2}\mathrm{H}$*  | *2*   |       *1*        | *$0.49932008$*        | *$0.49932008$* |  *$1$*  |
| *${}^{3}\mathrm{H}$*  | *3*   |       *3*        | *$0.65630083$*        | *$0.65630083$* |  *$1$*  |
| *${}^{3}\mathrm{He}$* | *3*   |       *3*        | *$0.60100173$*        | *$0.60100173$* |  *$1$*  |
| *${}^{4}\mathrm{He}$* | *4*   |       *6*        | *$0.50430647$*        | *$0.50430647$* |  *$1$*  |
| *${}^{6}\mathrm{Li}$* | *6*   |       *15*       | *$1.07955763$*        | *$1.07955763$* |  *$1$*  |

*For heavy nuclei ($A > 6$), only the product formula is tractable — the direct computation exceeds $10^5$ terms.*

## Consequence: the chain of invariant-preserving maps

*$$\mathbb{Z}[B_A]
  \;\xrightarrow{\text{Hecke quotient}}\;
  H_A(q)
  \;\xrightarrow{\text{transfer matrices}}\;
  \prod_{i} (a_i(q) \sigma_i + b_i(q))
  \;\xrightarrow{\text{Markov trace}}\;
  \prod_{i} \hat{V}_i(q)
  \;=\;
  P_{\mathcal{N}}(q)$$*

*Each step preserves the link invariant. The polynomial $P_{\mathcal{N}}(q)$ is a well-defined invariant of the nuclear link $\mathcal{N}(Z, N)$ — it does not depend on the braid representative or the reduction path. Evaluating at the substrate $q$ projects the polynomial invariant to the physical energy.*

## The polynomial degree

*The degree of $P_{\mathcal{N}}(q)$ as a polynomial in $q^{1/2}$ is bounded by:*

*$$\deg P_{\mathcal{N}} \;\leq\;
  \sum_{i=0}^{A-2} (2k_i + 1)
  \;=\;
  A(A-1) + (A-1)
  \;=\;
  (A-1)(A+1)
  \;=\;
  A^2 - 1$$*

*For ${}^{14}\mathrm{C}$: $\deg \leq 195$. For ${}^{210}\mathrm{Bi}$: $\deg \leq 44{,}099$. The transfer matrix product evaluates this polynomial at the substrate parameter $q$ without ever expanding it.*

## Asymptotic behaviour

*For heavy nuclei ($A \gg 1$), the ratio of $L_0^{-}$ and parent traces converges:*

*$$\frac{\mathrm{tr}(L_0^{-})}{\mathrm{tr}(\mathcal{N})}
  \;\longrightarrow\;
  \frac{1}{\hbar_q}
  \;=\;
  \frac{1}{1 - q^{-1}}
  \;\approx\; 10.09
  \quad\text{as } A \to \infty.$$*

*The sub-leading correction is $O(1/A)$ and carries the nucleus-specific information (shell structure, pairing).*

</div>

<div id="prop:skein-polynomial-transfer-matrix" class="proposition">

**Proposition 9.61** (The nuclear Skein polynomial as a transfer matrix product in $q$). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.Descartes.skein_polynomial_transfer_matrix)*

*The substrate parameter $q$ is the variable of the nuclear Skein polynomial. The transfer matrix product computes this polynomial in factored form without expansion.*

***Proposition.** *Let $\mathcal{N}(Z, N)$ be a nucleus with $A = Z + N$ nucleons. The Markov trace ([factorization theorem](#thm:markov-trace-factorization))**

*$$P_{\mathcal{N}}(q)
  \;:=\;
  \mathrm{tr}_{\mathrm{Markov}}\!\bigl(
    \mathcal{N}(Z, N)
  \bigr)
  \;=\;
  \prod_{i=0}^{A-2} \hat{V}_i(q)$$*

**is a polynomial in $q^{1/2}$ of degree $\leq A^2 - 1$. Each factor**

*$$\hat{V}_i(q) \;=\; z(q) \cdot a_i(q) + b_i(q)$$*

**is a rational function in $q^{1/2}$, where $a_i(q), b_i(q) \in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}]$ are the transfer matrix coefficients at generator $\sigma_i$ and $z(q) = 1/(q^{1/2} + q^{-1/2})$ is the Markov parameter. The product $P_{\mathcal{N}}(q)$ is the **Skein polynomial of the nuclear link** in factored form. It is computed by exactly $\binom{A}{2}$ transfer matrix multiplications — one per nucleon pair.**

**Proof.* The Hecke algebra $H_A(q)$ is defined over the ring $\mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}]$. Each crossing factor $C_{ij} = c_j \sigma_i + d_j$ has coefficients $(c_j, d_j)$ in $\mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1}]$:*

| *Pair type*                     | *$c_j$*             | *$d_j$*                              |
|:--------------------------------|:--------------------|:-------------------------------------|
| *$\mathfrak{p}$-$\mathfrak{p}$* | *$1$*               | *$0$*                                |
| *$\mathfrak{n}$-$\mathfrak{n}$* | *$q^2$*             | *$-q(q^{1/2} - q^{-1/2})$*           |
| *mixed*                         | *$\frac{1+q^2}{2}$* | *$-\frac{q}{2}(q^{1/2} - q^{-1/2})$* |

*The transfer matrix at each crossing:*

*$$T_j(q) \;=\;
  \begin{pmatrix}
    c_j(q - q^{-1}) + d_j & c_j \\
    c_j & d_j
  \end{pmatrix}
  \;\in\; \mathrm{M}_2(\mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}])$$*

*has entries that are Laurent polynomials in $q^{1/2}$. The product of $k_i = A - i - 1$ such matrices at generator $\sigma_i$:*

*$$M_i(q) \;=\; \prod_{j=i+1}^{A-1} T_j(q)
  \;\in\; \mathrm{M}_2(\mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}])$$*

*has entries that are polynomials in $q^{1/2}$ of degree $\leq 2k_i$. The traced volume:*

*$$\hat{V}_i(q) \;=\; z(q) \cdot (M_i)_{11}(q) + (M_i)_{21}(q)$$*

*is a rational function in $q^{1/2}$ (the $z$ denominator $q^{1/2} + q^{-1/2}$ divides into the numerator for link invariants by Jones’s theorem).*

*The product $P_{\mathcal{N}}(q) = \prod_i \hat{V}_i(q)$ is a polynomial in $q^{1/2}$ because each factor is (after cancellation with $z$), and its degree is bounded by:*

*$$\deg P_{\mathcal{N}}
  \;\leq\;
  \sum_{i=0}^{A-2} (2k_i + 1)
  \;=\;
  2 \cdot \frac{A(A-1)}{2} + (A-1)
  \;=\;
  A^2 - 1.$$*

*The computation requires exactly $\sum_i k_i = \binom{A}{2}$ transfer matrix multiplications (one per nucleon pair). No polynomial expansion occurs — the factored form is never unfolded. $\square$*

***The triple identity of $q$.***

*The parameter $q$ plays three roles simultaneously:*

| *Role*        | *Description*                                                  |
|:--------------|:---------------------------------------------------------------|
| *Algebraic*   | *Deformation parameter of $H_A(q)$: $T^2 = (q - q^{-1})T + 1$* |
| *Topological* | *Variable of the Skein polynomial $P_{\mathcal{N}}(q)$*        |
| *Physical*    | *Substrate parameter $q$ from $\chi(A) = -6$*                  |

*These are not three different objects — they are the **same $q$**. The Hecke relation generates the polynomial; the Markov trace makes it a link invariant; evaluating at $q$ projects the topological invariant to the physical energy.*

***Degree bounds for specific nuclei.***

| *Nucleus*               | *$A$* | *$\binom{A}{2}$ steps* | *$\deg P_{\mathcal{N}} \leq$* |
|:------------------------|:------|:----------------------:|:-----------------------------:|
| *${}^{2}\mathrm{H}$*    | *2*   |          *1*           |              *3*              |
| *${}^{3}\mathrm{H}$*    | *3*   |          *3*           |              *8*              |
| *${}^{4}\mathrm{He}$*   | *4*   |          *6*           |             *15*              |
| *${}^{14}\mathrm{C}$*   | *14*  |          *91*          |             *195*             |
| *${}^{56}\mathrm{Fe}$*  | *56*  |         *1540*         |            *3135*             |
| *${}^{210}\mathrm{Bi}$* | *210* |        *21945*         |            *44099*            |

*All evaluated in milliseconds.*

***Consequence for beta decay.***

*The $\mathcal{Q}_q$-value ([transition energy](#def:q-value-transition)) is the ratio of two Skein polynomials evaluated at the substrate parameter $q$:*

*$$\mathcal{Q}_q
  \;=\;
  P_{\mathcal{N}_{\mathrm{par}}}(q)
  \;-\;
  P_{\mathcal{N}_{\mathrm{dau}}}(q)
  \;-\;
  P_{e}(q)$$*

*(in action units). Since the parent and daughter polynomials differ only at generators $\sigma_0, \ldots, \sigma_p$ (the 1-jet support of the beta decay ([jet expansion](#prop:generator-volume-decomposition))), the difference is a polynomial of lower degree — concentrated in the converting nucleon’s generators.*

***Consequence for double beta decay.***

*The 2-jet cross-term $\Delta_{p_1 p_2}$ ([generator volume decomposition](#prop:generator-volume-decomposition)) corresponds to the **interference** between two Skein polynomial modifications. In the polynomial language:*

*$$P_{\mathcal{N}}^{(2\beta)}(q)
  \;-\;
  P_{\mathcal{N}}^{(\mathrm{par})}(q)
  \;\neq\;
  \bigl[P_{\mathcal{N}}^{(\beta_1)}(q) - P_{\mathcal{N}}^{(\mathrm{par})}(q)\bigr]
  \;+\;
  \bigl[P_{\mathcal{N}}^{(\beta_2)}(q) - P_{\mathcal{N}}^{(\mathrm{par})}(q)\bigr]$$*

*The difference is the 2-jet cross-term: a polynomial in $q$ encoding the nuclear matrix element of double beta decay.*

</div>

<div id="def:transfer-matrix-operator" class="definition">

**Definition 9.62** (Transfer Matrix Operator for Nuclear Braid Interactions). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.Descartes.TransferMatrixOperator)*

*Every particle interaction in the Descartes universe is encoded by a **transfer matrix** $T_{K_1, K_2}(q) \in \mathrm{M}_2(\mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}])$ determined by the knot types $K_1, K_2$ of the two interacting strands. The transfer matrix acts as an **operator** on the Gröbner ideal of the Hecke algebra, and its entries are polynomials in $q$.*

## Definition

***Definition.** Let $K_1, K_2$ be two building block knots ([building blocks](#rem:building-block-knots)) meeting at a crossing in a braid word $\beta \in B_n$. The **transfer matrix** of the crossing is:*

*$$T_{K_1, K_2}(q)
  \;=\;
  \begin{pmatrix}
    c(q - q^{-1}) + d & c \\
    c & d
  \end{pmatrix}$$*

*where the **crossing coefficients** $(c, d) \in \mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}]^2$ are determined by the knot types:*

*$$c_{K_1, K_2}
  \;=\;
  \frac{J_{K_1}(q) \cdot J_{K_2}(q)}{J_{K_1 \# K_2}(q)},
  \qquad
  d_{K_1, K_2}
  \;=\;
  -c \cdot \frac{q \, s}{1 + J_{K_1}(q) \cdot J_{K_2}(q)}$$*

*where $J_K(q)$ is the Jones polynomial of knot $K$ and $s = q^{1/2} - q^{-1/2}$ is the Skein amplitude.*

*For the three nuclear crossing types (quarks as Borromean unknot components), this specializes to:*

| *Crossing*                      | *$K_1$* | *$K_2$* | *$c$*               | *$d$*             |
|:--------------------------------|:--------|:--------|:--------------------|:------------------|
| *$\mathfrak{p}$-$\mathfrak{p}$* | *$u$*   | *$u$*   | *$1$*               | *$0$*             |
| *$\mathfrak{n}$-$\mathfrak{n}$* | *$d$*   | *$d$*   | *$q^2$*             | *$-qs$*           |
| *mixed*                         | *$u$*   | *$d$*   | *$\frac{1+q^2}{2}$* | *$-\frac{qs}{2}$* |

## Action on the Gröbner ideal

*The transfer matrix acts on the Hecke algebra element $a\sigma_i + b$ (the Gröbner-reduced chain at generator $\sigma_i$) by left multiplication followed by Hecke reduction:*

*$$T_{K_1, K_2} \;\cdot\; (a\sigma + b)
  \;:=\;
  (c\sigma + d)(a\sigma + b)
  \;\stackrel{T^2 = (q-q^{-1})T + 1}{\longrightarrow}\;
  a'\sigma + b'$$*

*where:*

*$$a' = ac(q - q^{-1}) + ad + bc,
  \qquad
  b' = ac + bd.$$*

*In matrix form:*

*$$\begin{pmatrix} a' \\ b' \end{pmatrix}
  \;=\;
  T_{K_1, K_2}(q)
  \;\cdot\;
  \begin{pmatrix} a \\ b \end{pmatrix}$$*

*The product of $k$ transfer matrices at generator $\sigma_i$ gives the full chain reduction $M_i = \prod_{j} T_j(q)$, and the Markov-traced volume is $\hat{V}_i = z \cdot (M_i)_{11} + (M_i)_{21}$.*

## The operator algebra

*Transfer matrices compose: if strands $K_1$, $K_2$, $K_3$ cross in sequence at generator $\sigma_i$, the combined operator is:*

*$$T_{K_1 K_3} \circ T_{K_1 K_2}
  \;=\;
  T_{K_1, K_3}(q) \cdot T_{K_1, K_2}(q)$$*

*(matrix multiplication). This is **non-commutative** — the order of crossings matters.*

***The Gröbner ideal is the kernel:***

*$$I_i \;=\; \ker\!\left(
    \prod_{j} T_j(q) - M_i(q)
  \right)$$*

*The ideal $I_i$ at generator $\sigma_i$ absorbs the terms eliminated by the Hecke relation ($T^2 = (q - q^{-1})T + 1$). The transfer matrix product $M_i(q)$ is the **quotient** — the element surviving after modding out $I_i$.*

## Interaction catalogue

*Every particle interaction corresponds to a transfer matrix. The **interaction type** is determined by the knot types of the two strands at the crossing:*

### Nuclear interactions (quark-level, Level 1)

| *Interaction*                | *$K_1$*              | *$K_2$*              | *$T(q)$*             | *Physical*                |
|:-----------------------------|:---------------------|:---------------------|:---------------------|:--------------------------|
| *$\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{u}$* | *$T_{2,3}$*          | *$T_{2,3}$*          | *$T_{pp}$*           | *proton-proton repulsion* |
| *$\mathfrak{d}\mathfrak{d}$* | *$T_{2,3}^{\sigma}$* | *$T_{2,3}^{\sigma}$* | *$T_{nn}$*           | *neutron-neutron*         |
| *$\mathfrak{u}\mathfrak{d}$* | *$T_{2,3}$*          | *$T_{2,3}^{\sigma}$* | *$T_{\mathrm{mix}}$* | *proton-neutron binding*  |

### Electromagnetic interactions (electron-level)

| *Interaction*        | *$K_1$*     | *$K_2$*           | *Physical*                    |
|:---------------------|:------------|:------------------|:------------------------------|
| *$e$-$\mathfrak{p}$* | *$T_{2,3}$* | *$\mathcal{B}_3$* | *Electron-nucleus Coulomb*    |
| *$e$-$e$*            | *$T_{2,3}$* | *$T_{2,3}$*       | *Electron-electron repulsion* |
| *$\gamma$-$e$*       | *$T_{1,0}$* | *$T_{2,3}$*       | *Photon absorption/emission*  |

### Photon-electron transfer matrix

*The photon ($T_{1,0}$, unknot) crossing with the electron ($T_{2,3}$, trefoil) gives:*

*$$T_{\gamma e}(q)
  \;=\;
  T_{T_{1,0}, T_{2,3}}(q)$$*

*Since the unknot has $J_{T_{1,0}}(q) = 1$: $c_{\gamma e} = J_{T_{2,3}}(q) / J_{T_{2,3}}(q) = 1$ and $d_{\gamma e} = 0$. Therefore:*

*$$T_{\gamma e}(q) \;=\; T_{pp}(q)
  \;=\;
  \begin{pmatrix}
    q - q^{-1} & 1 \\
    1 & 0
  \end{pmatrix}$$*

***The photon-electron transfer matrix is the same as the proton-proton matrix.** This is because $J_\nu(q) = 1$ (trivial Jones polynomial), so the unknot contributes no deformation — the crossing is purely determined by the electron.*

### Shell transitions as R-I moves

*Photon absorption promotes an electron from shell $n$ to shell $n+1$. In the transfer matrix language, this is a **Reidemeister I move** on the electron-nucleus Hopf link: a curl is added to the electron trefoil, changing its writhe by $\pm 1$ but preserving its knot type.*

*The R-I move at the electron-nucleus junction:*

*$$\sigma_i \;\mapsto\; \sigma_i \cdot \sigma_n$$*

*adds one transfer matrix factor $T_{\gamma e}$ to the chain at generator $\sigma_i$. The energy change is:*

*$$\Delta E_n
  \;=\;
  \hat{V}_i^{(n+1)} - \hat{V}_i^{(n)}
  \;=\;
  z \cdot (T_{\gamma e} \cdot M_i^{(n)})_{11}
  + (T_{\gamma e} \cdot M_i^{(n)})_{21}
  - \hat{V}_i^{(n)}$$*

*For hydrogen ($A = 1$, single electron-proton junction): the transfer matrix at shell $n$ is $T_{\gamma e}^n$ (the $n$-th power). The energy:*

*$$E_n \;\propto\; \hat{V}(T_{\gamma e}^n)
  \;=\;
  z \cdot (T_{\gamma e}^n)_{11} + (T_{\gamma e}^n)_{21}$$*

*Since $T_{\gamma e}$ has eigenvalues $\lambda_{\pm} = \frac{1}{2}\bigl[(q - q^{-1}) \pm \sqrt{(q - q^{-1})^2 + 4}\bigr]$, the $n$-th power grows as $\lambda_+^n$, and the energy scales as:*

*$$E_n \;\propto\; \lambda_+^n$$*

*The **energy difference** between shells:*

*$$\Delta E_{n \to n+1}
  \;=\;
  \hat{V}(T_{\gamma e}^{n+1}) - \hat{V}(T_{\gamma e}^n)
  \;=\;
  \hat{V}(T_{\gamma e}^n) \cdot (\lambda_+ - 1)$$*

*This gives the photon energy for shell transitions — a geometric series in the eigenvalue $\lambda_+$ of the photon-electron transfer matrix.*

## Interaction as Δ operator

*Any interaction that changes the crossing type from $(K_1, K_2) \to (K_1', K_2')$ is encoded by the **interaction operator**:*

*$$\Delta_{K_1 K_2 \to K_1' K_2'}(q)
  \;=\;
  T_{K_1', K_2'}(q) - T_{K_1, K_2}(q)$$*

*This is a 2×2 matrix with polynomial entries in $q$.*

| *Interaction*       | *$\Delta$ operator*                                    | *Physical process*                                |
|:--------------------|:-------------------------------------------------------|:--------------------------------------------------|
| *$\beta^-$ decay*   | *$\Delta_\beta = T_{\mathrm{mix}} - T_{nn}$*           | *$\mathfrak{d} \to \mathfrak{u}$ crossing change* |
| *$\beta^+$ decay*   | *$-\Delta_\beta = T_{\mathrm{mix}} - T_{pp}$*          | *$\mathfrak{u} \to \mathfrak{d}$ crossing change* |
| *Photon absorption* | *$\Delta_\gamma = T_{\gamma e}$ (appended)*            | *R-I move adds crossing*                          |
| *Pair creation*     | *$\Delta_{\mathrm{pair}} = T_{ee} - T_{\gamma\gamma}$* | *$\gamma \to e^+ e^-$*                            |

*For beta decay, $\Delta_\beta$ is **universal** ([beta decay matrix](#prop:beta-decay-transfer-matrix)): the same matrix for every nucleus.*

*For photon absorption, the operator is not a difference but an **extension**: a new transfer matrix factor $T_{\gamma e}$ is appended to the chain, increasing the color degree by $1$.*

## Composition rules

***Sequential interactions** (two interactions in sequence at the same generator):*

*$$\Delta_{\mathrm{total}} = \Delta_2 \cdot T_{\mathrm{between}} \cdot \Delta_1
  + \Delta_1 + \Delta_2$$*

***Parallel interactions** (interactions at different generators):*

*$$\frac{P_{\mathrm{final}}}{P_{\mathrm{initial}}}
  \;=\;
  \prod_{i \in \mathrm{affected}} \frac{\hat{V}_i^{\mathrm{final}}}{\hat{V}_i^{\mathrm{initial}}}$$*

*The generators factorize — each affected generator contributes independently to the Skein polynomial ratio.*

</div>

<div id="prop:beta-decay-transfer-matrix" class="proposition">

**Proposition 9.63** (Beta decay as a universal matrix-valued polynomial in $q$). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.Descartes.beta_decay_transfer_matrix)*

*Beta decay is mediated by the $T_{3,5}$ torus knot with $10$ crossings ([beta decay](#def:beta-decay-skein)). The $T_{3,5}$ insertion at the converting quark produces a **universal** 2×2 matrix-valued polynomial $\Delta_\beta(q)$ that governs every beta transition in every nucleus. The transfer matrix captures the effect of the $10$-crossing weak vertex on each nucleon pair.*

## The three crossing transfer matrices

*Each nucleon pair $(i, j)$ contributes a transfer matrix $T(q) \in \mathrm{M}_2(\mathbb{Z}[q^{\pm 1/2}])$:*

*$$T(c, d) \;=\;
  \begin{pmatrix}
    c(q - q^{-1}) + d & c \\
    c & d
  \end{pmatrix}$$*

*with crossing coefficients $(c, d)$ depending on the pair type:*

*$$T_{pp}(q) \;=\;
  \begin{pmatrix}
    q - q^{-1} & 1 \\
    1 & 0
  \end{pmatrix},
  \quad
  T_{nn}(q) \;=\;
  \begin{pmatrix}
    q^2(q - q^{-1}) - qs & q^2 \\
    q^2 & -qs
  \end{pmatrix}$$*

*$$T_{\mathrm{mix}}(q) \;=\;
  \begin{pmatrix}
    \frac{1+q^2}{2}(q - q^{-1}) - \frac{q s}{2}
      & \frac{1+q^2}{2} \\[4pt]
    \frac{1+q^2}{2} & -\frac{q s}{2}
  \end{pmatrix}$$*

*where $s = q^{1/2} - q^{-1/2}$ is the Skein amplitude.*

## The universal beta decay matrix

***Proposition.** *The two elementary decay matrices $\Delta_\beta^{nn \to \mathrm{mix}}$ and $\Delta_\beta^{\mathrm{mix} \to pp}$ are identical:**

*$$\Delta_\beta^{nn \to \mathrm{mix}}(q)
  \;=\; T_{\mathrm{mix}}(q) - T_{nn}(q)
  \;=\; T_{pp}(q) - T_{\mathrm{mix}}(q)
  \;=\; \Delta_\beta^{\mathrm{mix} \to pp}(q)$$*

**There is a single universal beta decay matrix:**

*$$\boxed{
    \Delta_\beta(q)
    \;=\;
    \tfrac{1}{2}(1 - q^2) \, T_{pp}(q)
    \;+\;
    \tfrac{1}{2}\, q \, s \;\mathbb{I}
  }$$*

**where $\mathbb{I}$ is the $2 \times 2$ identity.**

**Proof.* The off-diagonal entries of both differences are $\frac{1+q^2}{2} - q^2 = \frac{1-q^2}{2}$ and $1 - \frac{1+q^2}{2} = \frac{1-q^2}{2}$.*

*The $(2,2)$ entry of both is $-\frac{qs}{2} - (-qs) = \frac{qs}{2}$ and $0 - (-\frac{qs}{2}) = \frac{qs}{2}$.*

*The $(1,1)$ entry of both is $\frac{1-q^2}{2}(q - q^{-1}) + \frac{qs}{2}$.*

*These are identical for both $T_{\mathrm{mix}} - T_{nn}$ and $T_{pp} - T_{\mathrm{mix}}$, hence the two elementary decay matrices coincide.*

*Writing in terms of $T_{pp}$ and $\mathbb{I}$: the off-diagonal entries $\frac{1-q^2}{2}$ match $\frac{1-q^2}{2} \cdot 1$ (the off-diagonal of $\frac{1-q^2}{2} T_{pp}$). The $(2,2)$ entry $\frac{qs}{2}$ is $\frac{1-q^2}{2} \cdot 0 + \frac{qs}{2} \cdot 1$. The $(1,1)$ entry is $\frac{1-q^2}{2}(q - q^{-1}) + \frac{qs}{2} \cdot 1$. $\square$*

***Explicit entries at the substrate parameter $q$:***

*$$\Delta_\beta(q_0) \;=\;
  \begin{pmatrix}
    +0.0337 & -0.1161 \\
    -0.1161 & +0.0579
  \end{pmatrix}$$*

## The decay formula

*At generator $\sigma_i$ (affected by the converting nucleon at position $p$), the transfer matrix product factors as:*

*$$M_i^{\mathrm{par}}(q) = L_i(q) \cdot T_{\mathrm{par}}(q) \cdot R_i(q)$$*

*where $L_i$ is the product of matrices to the left of the converting crossing (unchanged) and $R_i$ to the right (unchanged). The daughter matrix product is:*

*$$M_i^{\mathrm{dau}}(q) = L_i(q) \cdot (T_{\mathrm{par}}(q) + \Delta_\beta(q)) \cdot R_i(q)$$*

*The change in the transfer matrix product:*

*$$\Delta M_i(q) = L_i(q) \cdot \Delta_\beta(q) \cdot R_i(q)$$*

*The change in the Markov-traced volume:*

*$$\Delta \hat{V}_i(q)
  \;=\;
  z \cdot (\Delta M_i)_{11} + (\Delta M_i)_{21}$$*

*The $\mathcal{Q}_q$-value ([transition energy](#def:q-value-transition)) in log form:*

*$$\ln \frac{P_{\mathrm{dau}}(q)}{P_{\mathrm{par}}(q)}
  \;=\;
  \sum_{i=0}^{p} \ln \frac{\hat{V}_i^{\mathrm{dau}}(q)}{\hat{V}_i^{\mathrm{par}}(q)}$$*

*where the sum runs only over generators affected by the converting nucleon. Generators $\sigma_i$ with $i > p$ cancel exactly (unaffected by the conversion).*

</div>

<div id="sim:beta-decay-braid" class="remark">

**Remark 9.64** (Beta decay as $T_{3,5}$ braid insertion: crossing budget and transfer matrices).

*Interactive visualization of beta decay as a $T_{3,5}$ braid insertion on the nuclear braid word.*

## The $T_{3,5}$ weak vertex

*The weak interaction is carried by the torus knot $T_{3,5}$ ([force identification](#rem:force-knot-identification)), whose braid word $\beta_{T_{3,5}} = (\sigma_1 \sigma_2)^5$ has **$10$ crossings**. This simulator draws the full braid left-to-right, showing strands flowing from the parent nucleon through the $T_{3,5}$ insertion to the daughter nucleon plus lepton pair.*

## Panels

1.  ***Braid flow diagram** — the $10$-crossing $T_{3,5}$ braid inserted at the converting $\mathfrak{d}$-quark crossing. Input strands (left) carry the parent quark content; output strands (right) carry the daughter quark content plus the emitted electron ($T_{2,3}$, $3$ crossings) and antineutrino ($K_{0_1}$, $0$ crossings). Toggle between $\beta^-$ ($\mathfrak{d} \to \mathfrak{u}$) and $\beta^+$ ($\mathfrak{u} \to \mathfrak{d}$).*

2.  ***Transfer matrix crossings** — the three nuclear crossing types $T_{pp}$, $T_{nn}$, $T_{\mathrm{mix}}$ drawn as individual braid crossings with their $2 \times 2$ matrix entries evaluated at the substrate parameter $q$.*

3.  ***Hecke and Skein relations** — the Hecke relation $T^2 = (q - q^{-1})T + 1$ and the Skein relation $q[L_+] - q^{-1}[L_-] = (q^{1/2} - q^{-1/2})[L_0]$ illustrated as braid crossing reductions.*

4.  ***Universal decay matrix** — the equally-spaced property $\Delta_\beta = T_{\mathrm{mix}} - T_{nn} = T_{pp} - T_{\mathrm{mix}}$ with explicit polynomial entries.*

## Strand conventions

*Strands follow the pointed-knot convention from the building-block table ([building blocks](#rem:building-block-knots)):*

- ***Solid** ($\bullet$) = particle (positive time orientation, $T_{2,3}$)*

- ***Outlined** ($\circ$) = antiparticle (negative time / mirror, $\overline{T_{2,3}}$)*

- ***Basepoint** marked on each strand*

*The $\mathfrak{u}$-quark strands are drawn in blue (solid), $\mathfrak{d}$-quark strands in red (outlined), matching the crossing-chirality convention where positive crossings are $\mathfrak{u}\text{-}\mathfrak{u}$ and negative crossings are $\mathfrak{d}\text{-}\mathfrak{d}$.*

## The $10$-crossing budget

*$$\underbrace{10}_{\text{total}} \;=\;
  \underbrace{3}_{e^- \;(T_{2,3})} \;+\;
  \underbrace{0}_{\bar{\nu}_e \;(K_{0_1})} \;+\;
  \underbrace{7}_{\text{R2 re-reduction}}$$*

*The $7$ re-reduction crossings modify inter-nucleon crossing types at the converting quark’s strand, producing the dominant contribution to the $\mathcal{Q}_q$-value.*

</div>

<div id="prop:shell-structure-eigenvalues" class="proposition">

**Proposition 9.65** (Orbital shells from eigenvalues of the photon-electron transfer matrix). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.Descartes.shell_structure_eigenvalues)*

*The orbital shell structure of an atom is determined by the **eigenvalues** of the photon-electron transfer matrix $T_{\gamma e}(q)$. Shell $n$ corresponds to the $n$-th power $T_{\gamma e}^n$, and the shell energies satisfy a **Chebyshev recurrence** in $q$.*

## The characteristic polynomial

*The photon-electron transfer matrix ([transfer matrix operator](#def:transfer-matrix-operator)) is $T_{\gamma e} = T_{pp}$:*

*$$T_{\gamma e}(q) \;=\;
  \begin{pmatrix}
    q - q^{-1} & 1 \\
    1 & 0
  \end{pmatrix}$$*

*Its **characteristic polynomial** is:*

*$$\det(T_{\gamma e} - \lambda \mathbb{I})
  \;=\;
  \lambda^2 - (q - q^{-1})\lambda - 1
  \;=\; 0$$*

*with eigenvalues:*

*$$\lambda_{\pm}(q)
  \;=\;
  \frac{(q - q^{-1}) \pm \sqrt{(q - q^{-1})^2 + 4}}{2}$$*

***At the substrate parameter $q$:***

*$$q - q^{-1} = 0.2091, \quad
  \sqrt{0.2091^2 + 4} = 2.0054$$*

*$$\lambda_+ = 1.1073, \quad
  \lambda_- = -0.9027$$*

## Shell $n$ from the $n$-th power

*Shell $n$ of an atom is the $n$-th power of the transfer matrix at the electron-nucleus junction. Each power corresponds to one **R-I move** (Reidemeister I) — one curl added to the electron trefoil, increasing the writhe by $1$ without changing the knot type.*

*Diagonalizing $T_{\gamma e} = S \Lambda S^{-1}$:*

*$$T_{\gamma e}^n
  \;=\;
  S
  \begin{pmatrix}
    \lambda_+^n & 0 \\
    0 & \lambda_-^n
  \end{pmatrix}
  S^{-1}$$*

*where the eigenvector matrix is:*

*$$S \;=\;
  \begin{pmatrix}
    \lambda_+ & \lambda_- \\
    1 & 1
  \end{pmatrix}$$*

*The entries of $T_{\gamma e}^n$:*

*$$(T^n)_{11}
  \;=\;
  \frac{\lambda_+^{n+1} - \lambda_-^{n+1}}{\lambda_+ - \lambda_-},
  \qquad
  (T^n)_{21}
  \;=\;
  \frac{\lambda_+^n - \lambda_-^n}{\lambda_+ - \lambda_-}$$*

*These are **Chebyshev polynomials of the second kind** in the variable $\frac{1}{2}(q - q^{-1})$:*

*$$(T^n)_{21} \;=\; U_{n-1}\!\left(\tfrac{q - q^{-1}}{2}\right)$$*

## The traced volume at shell $n$

*The Markov-traced volume at shell $n$:*

*$$\hat{V}(n, q)
  \;=\;
  z \cdot (T^n)_{11} + (T^n)_{21}
  \;=\;
  \frac{(z\lambda_+ + 1)\lambda_+^n - (z\lambda_- + 1)\lambda_-^n}
       {\lambda_+ - \lambda_-}$$*

*where $z = 1/(q^{1/2} + q^{-1/2})$ is the Markov parameter.*

*Define:*

*$$\alpha \;=\; z\lambda_+ + 1, \qquad
  \beta \;=\; z\lambda_- + 1$$*

*Then:*

*$$\hat{V}(n, q) \;=\;
  \frac{\alpha \cdot \lambda_+^n - \beta \cdot \lambda_-^n}
       {\lambda_+ - \lambda_-}$$*

*Since $|\lambda_+| > 1 > |\lambda_-|$, the dominant term for large $n$ is:*

*$$\hat{V}(n, q) \;\sim\;
  \frac{\alpha}{\lambda_+ - \lambda_-} \cdot \lambda_+^n
  \qquad (n \gg 1)$$*

*The sub-dominant term $\beta \cdot \lambda_-^n = \beta \cdot (-1)^n / \lambda_+^n$ is an **alternating correction** that decays exponentially.*

## The Chebyshev recurrence

*The traced volumes satisfy the three-term recurrence:*

*$$\boxed{
    \hat{V}(n+1, q)
    \;=\;
    (q - q^{-1}) \cdot \hat{V}(n, q)
    \;+\;
    \hat{V}(n-1, q)
  }$$*

*with initial conditions $\hat{V}(0, q) = 1$ (no crossings) and $\hat{V}(1, q) = z(q - q^{-1}) + 1$ (one crossing).*

**Proof.* The recurrence is the matrix identity $T^{n+1} = T \cdot T^n$, which gives $(T^{n+1})_{21} = (T)_{11} (T^n)_{21} + (T)_{12} (T^n)_{22}$. Since $(T)_{11} = q - q^{-1}$ and $(T)_{12} = 1$, and using $(T^n)_{22} = (T^{n-1})_{21}$ (from $\det T = -1$), this becomes the Chebyshev recurrence. $\square$*

*The coefficient $q - q^{-1}$ in the recurrence is the **Hecke deformation** — the same parameter that controls parity violation ([Lee-Yang-Wu](#prop:parity-violation-skein)). At $q = 1$ the recurrence degenerates: $\hat{V}(n+1) = \hat{V}(n-1)$ (period 2, no shell structure).*

## The Rydberg formula

*The energy of shell $n$ in hydrogen is:*

*$$E_n(q)
  \;=\;
  E_0 \cdot \hat{V}(n, q)$$*

*where $E_0$ is the ground-state energy scale (from the electron-proton crossing energy at the substrate parameter $q$).*

*The transition energy (photon energy for $n \to n+1$):*

*$$\Delta E_{n \to n+1}
  \;=\;
  E_0 \bigl[\hat{V}(n+1, q) - \hat{V}(n, q)\bigr]
  \;=\;
  E_0 \bigl[(q - q^{-1} - 1) \hat{V}(n, q)
  + \hat{V}(n-1, q)\bigr]$$*

*For the dominant term ($n \gg 1$):*

*$$\Delta E_{n \to n+1}
  \;\sim\;
  E_0 \cdot \frac{\alpha}{\lambda_+ - \lambda_-}
  \cdot \lambda_+^n \cdot (\lambda_+ - 1)$$*

*The **Rydberg scaling** $E_n \propto 1/n^2$ emerges in the regime $\lambda_+ \approx 1 + \epsilon$ with $\epsilon = \lambda_+ - 1 \ll 1$. At the substrate parameter $q$: $\epsilon = 0.1073$. For low shells ($n = 1, 2, 3, \ldots$):*

*$$\lambda_+^n \approx e^{n\epsilon}
  \approx 1 + n\epsilon + \tfrac{1}{2}n^2\epsilon^2 + \cdots$$*

*The binding energy at shell $n$ (relative to ionization):*

*$$\mathbf{E}_{\mathrm{bind}}(n)
  \;=\;
  E_{\infty} - E_n
  \;\propto\;
  \frac{1}{\lambda_+^n}
  \;\approx\;
  e^{-n\epsilon}$$*

*For small $\epsilon$, this approximates $1/n^2$ over the physically relevant range ($n = 1$ to $\sim 7$). The exact formula is the **exponential** $\lambda_+^{-n}$, which reproduces the Rydberg formula to the precision of low-$n$ hydrogen spectroscopy.*

*The entire shell structure is encoded in the eigenvalues of $T_{\gamma e}(q)$ — a $2 \times 2$ matrix with polynomial entries in $q$.*

</div>

<div id="prop:quantum-dilogarithm-volume" class="proposition">

**Proposition 9.66** (Nuclear energy from the quantum dilogarithm of the Markov trace). *[<sup><span style="color: BurntOrange">$\forall$</span></sup>](https://litlfred.github.io/qou/lean/QOU.Descartes.quantum_dilogarithm_volume)*

*The Markov trace factorization ([factorization theorem](#thm:markov-trace-factorization)) gives an exact product $\prod_i \hat{V}_i$ that grows exponentially with $A$. The **physical energy** is not the product itself but its **logarithm** — the quantum dilogarithm volume of the nuclear link.*

***Three volumes of a knot.***
